530475|2026-03.headline: Tinna Rubber Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to over 18% on revenue of INR157 crores, up 22% YoY, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25%.
530475|2026-03.overview: Management reported record tire processing volumes in FY26 and a standalone EBITDA margin of 17.2%, up 286 bps. Consolidated Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY and 13% QoQ to INR157 crores, with EBITDA up 63% YoY to INR29 crores. Subsidiaries and new projects (Oman, South Africa, Saudi, TP Buildtech, PCMB, pyrolysis and rCB) carried start-up costs and geopolitical drag that management expects to normalise through FY27. Infra segment softened on bitumen shortages, which management expects to be temporary.

financial_highlights.value: revenue INR75 crores, EBITDA INR6 crores

financial_highlights.metric: Combined loss, Mbodla, South Africa and Tinna Rubber Arabia (FY26)

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 20% YoY in FY26, driven by MRP and reclaim rubber demand and exports, which grew 30% in volume. Management sees strong FY27 growth on higher virgin polymer prices and rubber blending in bitumen.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue declined from INR222 crores to INR205 crores in FY26 as the company prioritised value-added products. Bitumen shortage is expected to hit Q1-Q2 FY27 volumes, with management expecting normalisation later in the year.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23% in FY26 despite a marginal volume decline, reflecting price correction. Management expects a modest improvement in FY27.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Revenue stable YoY while volumes rose 8%. Appointed exclusive distributor in India for Zibo TAA Metal Technology (China) steel abrasives, with 30% volume growth targeted in FY27.

segments.name: PCMB (polymer compounding and masterbatch)
segments.commentary: About 4% of FY26 turnover, operating at 40% utilisation, with QoQ growth of about 75%. Budgeted FY27 revenue of about INR75 crores, rising to 8-10% of revenue. Haryana polymer compounding capacity to reach 18,000 tpa by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Pyrolysis (TPO) and rCB
segments.commentary: Pyrolysis plant has started and the rCB plant is under commissioning. FY27 revenue from both is projected at INR50-55 crores, with EBITDA margins of 15-19%. Full operation is expected by Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 20-25% over FY26.
Vision 2029 target: revenue of INR1,000 crores with EBITDA margin above 18%; management says 18% is its guidance comfort level, and the FY29 target is organic only.
Maintain about 18% EBITDA margin in FY27; consolidated EBITDA projected to cross INR100 crores in FY27.
Tire-crush capacity to rise from 185,000 tpa to 235,000 tpa by FY27, with about INR100 crores capex over FY27-28, mostly from internal accruals and up to about INR20 crores debt if needed.
Oman normalisation expected within Q1 FY27; South Africa breakeven from Q2 FY27; Saudi tire recycling plant (24,000 tpa) capex of INR20-25 crores, with work starting end Q2 or Q3 FY27.
Working capital days expected to stay at current levels, since PCMB carries higher credit terms.
capex_capacity: Tire-crush capacity in India expanded 9% to 185,000 tons in FY26; target of 235,000 tpa by FY27. Tire-crush volume rose 13% to 155,000 tons in FY26.
Capacity utilisation was 90% in India and 85% in Oman in FY26. Varale plant at 80% utilisation.
Solar capacity rose from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW in FY26; about 50% of power needs expected from renewables from FY27.
Pyrolysis plant (100 TPD feed) and rCB plant: about INR40 crores capex, largely complete. TPO stabilisation expected by end Q1 FY27 and rCB trial production in Q2 FY27.
TP Buildtech Kolkata plant commissioned, running under 25% utilisation, with three new construction system product lines launched.
Micronized rubber powder capacity being increased at at least two plants. PCMB capacity moving from a 6,000 tpa pilot to an 18,000 tpa polymer compounding facility in Haryana.
demand_pricing: Raw material economics: virgin rubber about INR240-260/kg vs recycled rubber about INR50/kg, roughly one-fifth the cost.

Bitumen prices have almost doubled, driving stronger crumb-rubber-modified bitumen (CRMB) demand, though India's bitumen supply constraint (imports of 3-3.5 million tons) hit road-work volumes in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP improved on demand; management said realisation volatility currently favours the company.
Freight rates and elevated polymer prices from the Middle East crisis raised import costs; management says the company offset these by sourcing from multiple geographies and feedstock types.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants: management cites a moat from raw material, product, customer and geographic diversity, plus 2-5 year approval cycles with tire majors.

qa_highlights.question: Vision FY29 revenue breakup by segment, and EPR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PCMB rises toward 8-10% of revenue from about 4%. Infra is expected to be about 30%, Industrial about 35%, Consumer about 10%, with the balance from rCB and pyrolysis. EPR revenue stays around INR29-30 crores a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the infra slowdown hit blended margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects better realisations on reclaim rubber and MRP to offset any infra softness, and says the bitumen-driven slowdown is temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA expected from RCB and pyrolysis plants in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined FY27 revenue of about INR50-55 crores. EBITDA margins of 15-19% are expected once the plants are fully running, with payback in line with the existing business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 42 to 55?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly due to PCMB, where industry practice carries longer credit days. Core rubber-products credit days have not changed materially, and working capital days are expected to stay at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crore capex be funded, and what is the debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of it from internal accruals, with FY27 EBITDA projected above INR100 crores. Management may take up to about INR20 crores of debt if needed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling bitumen supply and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company holds no bitumen and does not trade it. It supplies modifier to IOC and to contractors who source their own bitumen, which the company says is assured business for the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Bitumen availability (India imports 3-3.5 million tons, with Iran a key supplier) may keep infra volumes soft in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Middle East tensions delay the Saudi plant capital works (now expected end Q2 or Q3 FY27) and disrupt Oman exports; Oman normalisation is expected within Q1 FY27.
Start-up losses at South Africa and new plants; South Africa breakeven targeted from Q2 FY27, and TP Buildtech margins remain under pressure from crude, polymer and currency movements.
Receivable days rose to about 55 from 42 due to PCMB credit terms; watch whether working capital intensity persists.
Competition from new CRMB and rCB entrants; management cites strong moats but no quantified pricing impact.
Consolidated PAT growth (9%) lagged EBITDA growth; FY26 revenue growth was only 8% and infra revenue fell, so FY27 20-25% growth needs execution.
key_quotes: FY26 was another year of strong execution for Tinna Rubber, despite geopolitical uncertainties and a dynamic operating environment, we achieved record tire processing volumes and delivered robust EBITDA margins of over 17%.
But we expect that to normalize immediately because India has a very aggressive program for road construction.
Our comfort level to give a guidance to market is at 18%.

I don't see us doing any inorganic acquisition related to our business, but some adjacency business, if it comes across, where we have something new to learn or a new product line to add or new geography to add, those are the ideas we remain open to and we will look at those opportunities.
530475|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 execution, Vision 2029 and the Industrial/PCMB growth story, but cautious and deflecting on infra near-term volumes, bitumen supply, and per-ton realisation metrics. Management repeatedly stressed temporary disruption and declined to disclose new expansion locations or quantify pricing impact from competition.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin hit over 18% in Q4 FY26 (EBITDA INR29 crores on INR157 crores revenue), and management guides to maintain about 18% in FY27 with consolidated EBITDA projected above INR100 crores, helped by reclaim rubber and MRP realisations and Oman/South Africa normalisation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (tire-crush to 235,000 tpa by FY27; PCMB 18,000 tpa
rows.why: Tire-crush capacity rises 27% from 185,000 to 235,000 tpa on about INR100 crores capex over FY27-28, while India utilisation is already at 90%, so new capacity is being built ahead of demand; no new Saudi capacity is live before end Q2 or Q3 FY27 since capital works were deferred.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 20-25% FY27 revenue growth with tire-crush volume at 155,000 tons in FY26 (+13%) and Industrial exports already up 30% in volume in FY26, while Infra volumes are soft in Q1-Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 90% in India and 85% in Oman (above the 80% threshold), and management has already earmarked a further INR100 crores of capex over FY27-28, with up to about INR20 crores of debt if needed; the Saudi plant (INR20-25 crores) adds to the pipeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% (midpoint 22.5%) against FY26 growth of only 8%, so upside depends on PCMB reaching INR75 crores and pyrolysis/rCB hitting INR50-55 crores; management has not signalled a raise yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bitumen shortage (India imports 3-3.5 million tons) is expected to hit Infra volumes in Q1-Q2 FY27, Infra revenue already fell from INR222 crores to INR205 crores in FY26, and Middle East tensions could delay the Saudi plant and disrupt Oman exports.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: rCB trial production in Q2 FY27, TP Buildtech launched three new construction system product lines, and the Zibo TAA steel abrasives distribution targets 30% volume growth in FY27 with PCMB budgeted at about INR75 crores.

rows.label: South Africa breakeven and Oman normalisation
rows.when: Oman in Q1 FY27; South Africa from Q2 FY27
rows.why: Combined loss at Mbodla, South Africa and Tinna Rubber Arabia was INR1.58 crores in FY26 from start-up costs, and management expects Oman to normalise within Q1 FY27 and South Africa to break even from Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Receivable days rise from 42 to 55 on PCMB credit terms
rows.why: Receivable days rose 13 days, mainly from PCMB where industry credit terms are longer, and management expects working capital days to stay at current levels rather than improve.

rows.label: Net debt-to-equity down to 0.39 and debt-funded capex
rows.why: Total debt fell 10% to INR121 crores and net debt-to-equity fell from 0.73 to 0.39 in FY26, but the INR100 crores capex plan could add up to about INR20 crores of debt.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY26 execution, Vision 2029 and the Industrial/PCMB growth story, but cautious and deflecting on Infra near-term volumes from bitumen shortage, bitumen supply, and per-ton realisation metrics; analysts pressed on the receivable days jump and the infra slowdown's margi

530475|2026-06.headline: Tinna Rubber Q1 FY27 posted record EBITDA above INR50 crores (21%+ margin) and PAT above INR20 crores, with EPR credits adding a one-off monetisation lift.
530475|2026-06.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 profitability, with standalone and consolidated EBITDA margins above 21% and PAT margins above 13%. Standalone revenue rose 18% YoY and consolidated revenue rose 20%, with EBITDA margin up 638 bps standalone and 575 bps consolidated. Management attributed the margin gain mainly to gross margin expansion from cheaper feedstock and a higher mix of value-added products such as MRP and reclaimed rubber. Growth engines (PCMB, TPO/rCB, Oman, South Africa) are still ramping, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores and a sustainable 18-20% EBITDA margin.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR50 crores (EBITDA margin above 21%, cited as ~22%)
financial_highlights.change: Standalone EBITDA margin +638 bps YoY; consolidated +575 bps YoY

financial_highlights.value: Above INR20 crores (PAT margin above 13%; INR21 crores cited)
financial_highlights.change: Standalone PAT margin +471 bps YoY; consolidated +416 bps YoY

financial_highlights.value: ~INR9 crores; EBITDA margin 8.53%; PAT INR0.34 crores
INR19 crores revenue; INR3 crores EBITDA

financial_highlights.change: Threefold vs INR4 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR30.58 crores (company figure); analyst read INR27.19 crores for Q4 FY26 vs company figure INR29.85 crores
financial_highlights.change: Increase of ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst; company to clarify by email

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 58% YoY; MRP volumes +28% and reclaimed rubber volumes +37% YoY; run-rate cited at INR45-46 crores per quarter. Exports volume +46% YoY.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Revenue +7% YoY; volumes +33% YoY on rubberized bitumen demand amid bitumen shortage. Secured a 15,000 tonne rubberized bitumen processing order for FY27. Bitumen emulsion hit by supply constraints.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Volumes declined (analyst cited ~20%); binder and synthetic grass prices rose up to threefold, delaying turfing projects. Management says consumer is ~8-10% of business.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Revenue steady with marginal volume decline, supported by price corrections. Exclusive India distributorship for Zibo TAA Metal Technology steel abrasives; ~50% volume growth targeted in FY27.

segments.name: Tire recycling (India and Oman)
segments.commentary: India capacity utilisation 88%, volumes +35% YoY but down 10% QoQ on softer consumer demand. Oman utilisation 78%, hit by West Asia conflict.

segments.name: PCMB / PP Buildtech
segments.commentary: PCMB at 82% utilisation of initial 6,000 tpa; total capacity 18,000 tpa after Haryana expansion; targeted ~10% of FY27 revenue. Kolkata plant commissioned Q4 FY26; targeting >30% growth and INR100 crores revenue in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR670-700 crores (INR675-700 crores cited in later reply).
EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20% for FY27, described as sustainable despite Q1 at ~22%; management declined to confirm either 18% or 22%.
Vision 2029: INR1,000 crores revenue by FY29, 25%+ revenue CAGR, 33%+ profitability CAGR, EBITDA margin above 18%, ROCE above 30%, presence in 10 locations.
Capex of ~INR100 crores across FY27-FY28; INR27 crores spent in Q1 FY27; ~INR60 crores to be capitalised in FY27. Capex could rise if demand stays strong.
TPO/rCB (pyrolysis oil and recovered carbon black) contribution of 7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 crores). TPO sales from Q2 FY27; rCB production from Q3 FY27.

South Africa breakeven expected Q2 FY27; Phase 2 tyre crumb production expected Q2 or Q3 FY27. Saudi Arabia (24,000 tpa) construction targeted toward end of calendar 2026, subject to Middle East normalisation.
Expansion of India tyre crushing capacity to 235,000 tpa (+27%) by FY27; MRP capacity 3,500 tpa addition by Q3 FY27 to 20,000 tpa total.
capex_capacity: India tyre crushing capacity 185,000 tpa, rising to 235,000 tpa by FY27 (+27%).
MRP capacity: 3,500 tpa expansion commissioning by Q3 FY27, taking total to 20,000 tpa.
TPO plant at Varle: trials began Q1 FY27; commercial sales Q2 FY27; stabilisation by Q3 FY27. rCB production Q3 FY27, commercial sales by Q4 FY27.
Rooftop solar: Gummidipoondi 999 kW (June 2026) and Varle 2,218 kW (July 2026). Renewable capacity raised from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW; renewables were 51% of power in Q1 FY27.
Management is exploring de-bottlenecking and possibly a greenfield India plant; India utilisation cited at 80-85% by analyst. Blended utilisation target 75-80% by year-end across geographies.
demand_pricing: Industrial demand supported by rising raw material costs and ESG-driven tyre-maker demand; MRP and reclaimed rubber volumes growing fast.
Rubberized bitumen demand rose as bitumen supply tightened and prices rose due to the West Asia conflict; government push to reduce import dependence.
Consumer turfing demand hit by binder and synthetic grass price spikes; management says the market is intact and will recover once prices stabilise.
EPR credits: ~100,000 units monetised in Q1 at a floor price of ~INR2,500 per unit (~INR25 crores cash). Management says EPR contributes ~INR25-30 crores a year at PBT level.
Margin gain attributed to raw material optionality and value-added product mix. Management said inventory gains were very marginal.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin rise is due to inventory gains, and is there margin normalisation ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains were very marginal. Management said the changes are systemic (raw material optionality, value-added mix), and expects some front-ended costs from new projects, so 18-20% is the sustainable range.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the 400-500 bps margin expansion; material plus inventory cost fell to 46% of sales.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main contribution came at gross margin, from cheaper raw material and higher realisation from value-added products, plus scale efficiencies. Overall EBITDA margin expanded about 4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How is EPR monetisation accounted for, and what is its contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said accrued EPR credits from prior years were monetised against unbilled revenue. Q1 P&L impact was already booked in FY26. Annual EPR contribution is about INR25-30 crores at PBT level. Analysts' questions on clean PAT were not fully resolved on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter Chile and Saudi Arabia, and will overseas investment scale up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Oman's limited scope and similar operating parameters for Saudi Arabia, and end-of-life tyre sourcing and hedging for South Africa and Chile. India remains the core investment focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for infrastructure given the West Asia situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bitumen shortages hit some projects, but rubberized asphalt demand rose as contractors sought cheaper alternatives. Infrastructure revenue grew 7% in Q1, and Q1 is the peak road-work season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue guidance of INR670-700 crores was reiterated; margin should sustain at 18-20% even though Q1 was 22%.

risks_watch: Earnings quality: the INR21 crore EPR monetisation and its treatment in the P&L were unclear on the call; analysts could not get a clean recurring PAT.
Other expenses rose ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst; company promised an email clarification.
Geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) affecting bitumen and binder supply, Oman utilisation (78%), and the Saudi project timeline.
Consumer segment volumes declined; recovery depends on binder and synthetic grass prices.
Q2 FY27 monsoon-related seasonality in infrastructure; capacity ramp-ups of TPO, rCB and PCMB must deliver to hit INR670-700 crores.
Management's margin guidance (18-20%) is well below the Q1 print (22%); watch for Q2 and Q3 margin normalisation.
530475|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the strategy, but guarded on forward numbers: management declined to confirm either 18% or 22% margin, and deflected several EPR accounting questions to email follow-ups.
key_quotes: We are delighted to share that we have commenced FY27 on a very strong note, delivering our best ever quarterly profitability.
I will neither confirm that we will achieve 18% nor will I confirm we will achieve 22%.
Our focus -- our core investment will remain India for the foreseeable future.
Our hedge comes from the fact that we cater to consumer business, industrial business, infra business, steel now PCMB and also TPO and rCB.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin ~22% (up 638 bps standalone) came from cheaper feedstock and value-added mix, but management guides 18-20% as sustainable and expects front-ended costs from new projects, so margins are more likely to normalise than expand.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: India tyre crushing capacity rising from 185,000 to 235,000 tpa (+27%) by FY27 with MRP addition of 3,500 tpa by Q3 FY27, and India utilisation already at 88%, so new capacity is firmly committed and coming live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Industrial volumes growing fast (MRP +28%, reclaimed rubber +37% YoY), Infrastructure volumes +33% on a 15,000 tonne rubberized bitumen order, and steel abrasive volume growth of ~50% targeted in FY27, offset by consumer volumes down ~20%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: India utilisation at 88% and management is exploring de-bottlenecking and possibly a greenfield India plant, with ~INR100 crores capex across FY27-FY28 and capex that could rise if demand stays strong.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated INR670-700 crore revenue and 18-20% margin rather than raising them, and declined to confirm either 18% or 22% margin, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 margin guide of 18-20% sits well below the Q1 print of ~22%, but management reiterated it; risk is from West Asia bitumen/binder disruption, consumer volumes down ~20%, and the Saudi timeline, with the INR670-700 crore revenue guide dependent on TPO/rCB and PCMB ramp-ups.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TPO commercial sales from Q2 FY27, rCB production from Q3 FY27 (commercial sales by Q4 FY27) and TPO/rCB guided at 7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 crores).

rows.label: 15,000 tonne rubberized bitumen processing order for FY27
rows.why: Secured order for 15,000 tonnes of rubberized bitumen processing, with infrastructure volumes +33% YoY amid bitumen shortage.

rows.label: South Africa breakeven and Saudi Arabia 24,000 tpa plant
rows.when: Q2 FY27 breakeven; Saudi construction toward end CY2026
rows.why: South Africa breakeven guided for Q2 FY27 with Phase 2 tyre crumb in Q2/Q3 FY27, but Saudi construction is subject to Middle East normalisation and Mbodla plus Saudi start-up loss was ~INR53 lakhs.

rows.label: EPR credit monetisation and earnings quality
rows.why: About 100,000 EPR units monetised at ~INR2,500 (~INR25 crores cash) and management puts annual EPR at INR25-30 crores PBT, but clean recurring PAT was not resolved and other expenses rose ~INR5.4 crores QoQ per analyst.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q1 print, capacity ramp and the INR670-700 crore revenue guide, but guarded on margins (declined to confirm 18% or 22%) and deflected EPR accounting questions to email; analysts pushed on clean PAT, the one-off EPR lift and the ~INR5.4 crore QoQ rise in other expenses

530475|2026-09.headline: Tinna Rubber Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% to INR157 crores and PAT 45% to INR17 crores; H1 PAT up 60% to INR38 crores.
530475|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR157 crores (up from INR120 crores), with EBITDA of INR29 crores (18.8% margin) and PAT of INR17 crores (10.9% margin). H1 revenue rose 25% to INR313 crores, EBITDA 50% to INR63 crores (20.4% margin) and PAT 60% to INR38 crores (12.2% margin). Management said profitability moderated from Q1 due to start-up costs, geopolitical uncertainty and subsidiary performance, and reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue, INR126 crores EBITDA and INR70 crores PAT. Expansion moved forward with a 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site (INR250 crores over 3 years), while the Saudi Arabia tyre recycling plant has been delayed by the West Asia conflict.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 38% to INR112 crores despite bitumen supply constraints; management cites it as a main growth driver with Industrial, and notes monsoon and cold-weather seasonality in Q2 and Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 37% to INR85 crores; exports were about 6% of total revenue with export volume growth of about 15%.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: H1 revenue rose to INR21 crores from INR19 crores, driven by price correction with stable volumes.

segments.name: Steel (by-product)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR57 crores from INR53 crores, mainly on price correction with stable volumes; management describes it as a by-product of tyre recycling.

segments.name: PCMB (Polymer Composites & Masterbatch)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue more than tripled to INR27 crores after 12,000 tpa added at Gannaur; capacity now 18,000 tpa, targeted at 8-10% of FY27 revenue and about INR70 crores top line. Management said this business runs at lower EBITDA margin than the core.

segments.name: TP Buildtech (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR41 crores with EBITDA INR4.7 crores, contributing INR1 crore at consolidated level; best-case target of INR100 crores revenue by FY27.

segments.name: Oman subsidiary
segments.commentary: Ran at 90% utilisation in H1; EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 6.4% in FY26; PAT of INR1.3 crores in H1.

segments.name: South Africa and Saudi Arabia (start-up)
segments.commentary: Combined start-up loss of about INR94 lakhs in H1; South Africa Phase 1 complete with semi-processed exports begun, and 9,000 tpa crumb line delayed 3-4 months.

financial_highlights.change: EBITDA up 37% YoY; margin vs 18.0% a year ago
down from INR121 crores at end FY26
vs about INR6.7 crores in Q1 FY27

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin (about 16% per analyst) come off versus prior quarters, and what about PCMB mix and steel price trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin was 18%-plus in Q2 (reported 18.8%), Q1 was an aberration with raw material and inventory benefits, and PCMB runs at lower margin than core as a new business still stabilising with R&D spend.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company's sourcing and margin stability differentiated versus peers hit by geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited diversity of geography, raw material base and customer base, pan-India presence, and multiple tyre origins, without commenting on competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Where is India capacity being added to reach 235,000 tpa, and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 10-15k tpa comes from debottlenecking, South Africa adds about 10k tpa this year, and Saudi (24k tpa) is delayed; the 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site is needed as existing land is largely exhausted.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR250 crores Andhra Pradesh capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding options are open over the next 6 to 12 months given a strong balance sheet; the INR250 crores is exclusively Tinna Rubber and spread over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Saudi plant and the Panipat land acquisition risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi land is allotted and contractors identified, but no advances released pending local stabilisation; Panipat is a fully depreciated plant of under 2 acres that could be moved within 3-4 months, and management is making representations to the state government.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential from Andhra Pradesh and what is Vision 2029 INR1,000 crores implication?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex to sales of 2.5-3x implies INR250-300 crores revenue from INR100 crores capex; INR1,000 crores by FY29 is reachable with Andhra and Saudi, with 5-10% variance possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited front-ended hiring ahead of projects (growth of 20-30% annually), start-up costs, and provision for performance bonus in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of about INR700 crores reiterated; management said it is roughly halfway there at H1 (INR313 crores).
FY27 EBITDA target of INR126 crores and PAT of INR70 crores reiterated; management aims for EBITDA margin of 18% plus and at least 10% PAT conversion.
PCMB to contribute 8-10% of FY27 revenue, about INR70 crores top line this year, and at least INR125 crores next year.
Tyre pyrolysis and rCB business expected to earn EBITDA margin around 18%, similar to core; rCB production starts Q3 with commercial sales from Q4.

Vision 2029 targets: INR1,000 crores revenue, revenue CAGR above 25%, profitability CAGR above 33%, EBITDA margin above 18%, ROCE above 30%, and expansion from 8 to 10 locations. Management said INR1,000 crores by FY29 is within reach, with 5-10% variance possible.

Saudi Arabia plant construction expected to begin in H2 FY27, subject to geopolitical situation; no advances or payments released yet. Oman: no further capex planned; Saudi to take about INR25 crores more.
capex_capacity: Completed INR45 crores of capex in H1 out of INR100 crores planned across FY27 and FY28.
3,500 tpa micronised rubber powder expansion on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning, taking MRP capacity to 20,000 tpa.

530517|2026-03.headline: Relaxo Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.1% YoY to INR 751 crore, with EBITDA margin at 16.5%, aided partly by GST cut-driven channel restocking.
530517|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 751 crore (+8.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 124 crore (+10.6%) and PAT INR 68 crore (+20.4%), with PAT margin at 9.0%. Management attributed the volume recovery to GST cut from 12% to 5%, channel restocking by distributors and better consumer demand, and said the underlying growth is closer to 5-6% over the last two quarters. FY26 revenue fell to INR 2,702 crore from INR 2,790 crore, while PAT rose 5.3% to INR 179 crore. Management has taken 2-3 price increases of roughly 15-18% at consumer level to offset input cost and wage inflation linked to West Asia tensions and Haryana labour costs.

530517|2026-09.headline: Relaxo Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11.6% to INR 702 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% as input and wage costs outran pricing.
530517|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 702 crore (up 11.6% YoY), with EBITDA up 5.1% to INR 85 crore and PAT up 2.2% to INR 37 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 9.6% to INR 1,407 crore, while EBITDA margin was 13.8% (H1) and PAT margin 6.5%. Management attributed margin pressure to West Asia-driven raw material volatility, statutory minimum wage hikes and brand/retail investments, and said margins will stay under pressure unless the conflict settles. Price increases of roughly 15-18% in open footwear and 6-7% in Sparx closed footwear drove realisations up over 20%, with volumes falling in mass slippers. The company also announced a Kenya JV (Relaxo Kenafric Footwears) for East Africa manufacturing.

530549|2026-09.headline: Shilpa Medicare posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of INR538 crores (+35% YoY) and EBITDA of INR151 crores at a 28% margin.
530549|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue (INR538 crores, +35% YoY) and record EBITDA (INR151 crores, +37% YoY), with H1 revenue crossing INR1,000 crores for the first time. Growth was broad-based across API, formulation and biologics. Gross margin compressed by roughly 700 bps YoY and sequentially, as raw material cost to sales rose from 28.65% to 35.72%, which management attributed to higher API sales and global API raw material inflation. Net debt was steady at INR612 crores despite INR252 crores of H1 capex funded from internal accruals. Management gave no revenue or utilisation guidance on peptides, albumin or Rotigotine beyond timing milestones.

segments.name: Formulation
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR210 crores (+50%+ YoY); H1 INR407 crores (+70% YoY). Excluding licensing income, the base business grew 87% in the quarter, led by EU complex finished dosage formulations. India business grew 2.5x in H1, led by Nor-UDCA.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR65 crores (+150% YoY); H1 INR117 crores (+92% YoY), driven by licensing and partnership deals and CDMO. Management says biologics is 12% of revenue and only Adalimumab is commercially supplied in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 700 bps, and how much cost increase has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Bhutada said the strong API quarter (lower-margin) versus higher-margin formulation drove the decline. qa_highlights.question: Why was the CDMO platform carved out from API?
qa_highlights.answer: As a one-stop integrated partner (KSM to final API for peptides; clone development to fill-finish for biologics; in-house payload, linker, antibody and conjugation for ADC), it aims to win more programs each year. Management confirmed the carve-out was to serve CDMO clients better.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Jadcherla with the US FDA and the plant risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working with the US FDA on remediation, with no impact on revenues or the 2–3 year plan. The EU re-inspected and cleared the plant, and most US critical filings are moved to CMO sites.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Rotigotine delayed, and when will it launch?
qa_highlights.answer: A European variation approval for one raw material took an extra two quarters. The launch is now set for H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of biologics revenue is licensing versus CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each quarter will carry a mix of CDMO, biosimilar and licensing revenue, and did not break it out.

qa_highlights.question: What share of service and licensing income is licensing, and is its gross margin 100%?
qa_highlights.answer: Alpesh Dalal declined to give the licensing split or assume 100% margin. He said there are no COGS, but related R&D and other expenses sit in those lines.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from API raw material inflation and API mix; watch whether it eases once raw material prices settle.
Regulatory: Jadcherla US FDA remediation remains open; US supply now depends on CMO sites.
Timing risk on launches: Rotigotine has slipped by two quarters, and Ondansetron depends on state approvals.
Peptide capacity is ahead of confirmed orders; utilisation disclosure deferred to H2 FY28.
Nilotinib generic competition in Europe, and the tender-based pricing that governs it.
Biologics earnings quality: lumpy licensing income versus recurring CDMO and biosimilar revenue.

530555|2026-03.headline: Paramount Communications Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24.5% QoQ to INR 573 crore, but FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 117.5 crore (6% margin) on US tariff disruption.
530555|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sequential recovery: revenue INR 573 crore (+13.6% YoY, +24.5% QoQ), EBITDA incl. other income INR 38.8 crore at 6.7% margin, and PAT INR 20.5 crore. FY26 revenue rose about 23% to INR 1,912 crore, but absolute EBITDA and PAT declined YoY due to US tariffs escalating from 10% to 50% during 2025. Management redirected volumes to domestic demand, which grew about 27%, and retained a US presence at sub-economic margins. The Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore, Phase 1) is the main growth lever, with a stated INR 5,000 crore revenue ambition by FY31.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Grew 37.3% to INR 1,001 crore in FY26, led by power cables; domestic order book at INR 508 crore (87% of order book).

segments.name: Domestic B2C and distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 10.6% to INR 179 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Domestic B2G (government/PSU)
segments.commentary: Stable at about INR 182 crore in FY26, so its share of revenue fell.

segments.name: Exports (USA-led)
segments.commentary: Grew 13.9% to INR 550 crore in FY26 despite tariffs; eight active US distributors versus two in FY22.

guidance_outlook: FY27 (informal, assuming current metal prices hold): top-line growth of 15-20% and at least 10% volume growth; no formal guidance given.
Margins expected to return to FY25 levels as a first milestone, with pre-tariff margin levels targeted by end of FY27.

Narmadapuram Phase 1: investment about INR 300 crore by FY28; partial operations from Q1 FY28; sales target about INR 500 crore in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore in FY29; expected 9-10% margin and 3-4 year payback.

Long-term aspiration: INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31, implying doubling every 3-4 years; Phase 1 capacity alone seen at INR 3,600-4,000 crore, with Phase 2 (INR 200-300 crore capex) to exceed INR 5,000 crore.
Working capital expected to normalise within Q1 FY27 after receivables rose on Q4 back-ended dispatches.
capex_capacity: Two existing plants at Dharuhera (Haryana) and Kushkhera (Rajasthan) described as running at optimal utilisation for three to four years; physical space constraint reached.
Existing-plant capex of about INR 50-55 crore a year, over INR 160 crore across the past three years.

Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh): about 31 acres allotted by MPIDC and possession taken; civil works underway; long-lead machinery ordered; building construction to start shortly; commissioning from FY28.

Narmadapuram products: EHV cables up to 132 kV (starting with 33 kV, then 66 kV and 132 kV), transmission conductors, elastomeric EBeam and EPR cables, lead-sheathed rubber cables; EHV approvals expected by FY28.

Funding: about INR 122 crore of equity raised (about INR 92 crore from investors, about INR 30 crore from promoters), plus internal accruals and modest debt; current debt only about INR 110 crore of working capital limits.
demand_pricing: Management cites six demand drivers: India T&D capex of INR 3.35 lakh crore (FY26-30), renewables (210-220 GW solar and 50-60 GW wind by FY30), data centres (about 70% higher cable density for AI facilities), US grid capex above USD 1 trillion, construction capex of INR 18-19 lakh crore, and railways (FY27 budget INR 3 lakh crore).

US tariffs: 10% reciprocal tariff from 2 Apr 2025, raised to 25% in August and 50% by end-August 2025; IEEPA tariffs invalidated by US Supreme Court (Feb-Apr 2026), which management says restored India's competitiveness.
Management says it kept US presence at sub-economic margins at lower volumes; competitors from Vietnam, South Korea, Cambodia, Ecuador and Egypt had a tariff advantage in FY26.
Pricing policy: no firm-price orders with delivery beyond 3-4 months; metal is bought the next working day after order receipt; price-variation formulas increasingly accepted by customers.
Management expects Q2 FY27 onwards to see stronger US demand pull, with one or two new products to be launched in the US next quarter.
Middle East, Europe, Australia and Africa flagged as opportunistic markets, with the Middle East a focus area in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new plant reach optimum utilisation, and what is the payback and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 (INR 300 crore) targets INR 1,200 crore revenue by FY29; payback 3-4 years; margin 9-10%. No formal guidance, but 15-20% top-line growth and at least 10% volume growth assumed if metal prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the domestic market not scaled up the top line or bottom line over the past year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is capacity, not demand; the plants have run at full utilisation for four years, and the company diverted US volume to domestic. FY24 precedent: US sales fell from INR 400 crore to INR 280 crore while domestic doubled from INR 400 crore to INR 800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables roughly double, and when will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 65% of Q4 sales were dispatched in the second half of the quarter; over three-quarters had been realised by 15 May 2026. Working capital cycle moved only from 99 to 101 days; CFO said most dispatches are against LCs.

qa_highlights.question: Can Paramount return to FY25 margins, and what drives margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 EBITDA margin is the first milestone. Drivers: new products, US tariff normalisation, power, renewable and data-centre demand, and operating leverage on volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will EHV lead times exceed 5-6 months, and how is raw material risk handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it avoids long-delivery firm-price orders and prefers 3-4 month horizons or price-variation clauses; EHV would follow the same policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the longer-term aspirational revenue and margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crore by FY31; Phase 1 capacity can reach about INR 3,600-4,000 crore, and Phase 2 to exceed INR 5,000 crore. Margins expected to move towards peer range as scale grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when the balance sheet has low leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity was about INR 122 crore of the INR 300 crore project; management said it diversifies the funding mix, with working capital needs still to be bank-funded and current debt about INR 110 crore.

risks_watch: Receivables: working capital cycle at 101 days; management says receivables normalise in Q1 FY27 with over three-quarters of Q4 receivables already collected. Watch the Q1 FY27 receivable run-rate.
US tariff regime and recovery: margins in the US remain below pre-tariff levels; watch whether volumes and margins improve each quarter from Q2 FY27.
Narmadapuram execution: commissioning slated for Q1 FY28 with EHV approvals expected by FY28; the 9-10% margin and INR 1,200 crore FY29 target depend on it.
Raw material (copper and aluminium) pass-through: policy is to avoid long firm-price orders, but EHV and longer-cycle orders may test this.
Management's FY31 INR 5,000 crore target and the FY27 guidance are informal and conditional on metal prices holding.

530555|2026-06.headline: Paramount Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore; operating margin (ex other income) expanded 320 bps YoY to 6.6%.
530555|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore but fell 7.7% QoQ, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4-to-Q1 pattern. Operating profit excluding other income rose 129.2% YoY to INR 34.7 crore, with margin up 320 bps YoY and 136 bps QoQ to 6.6%. The US export recovery after the IEEPA tariff invalidation drove exports to INR 155 crore (29%+ of revenue, up about 77% QoQ), while domestic revenue reached INR 374 crore. Order book rose to INR 615 crore from INR 583 crore, and a fresh equity raise of about INR 122 crore lifted net worth to INR 894 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is in line with expectations and FY25-level margins are targeted by at least Q4 FY27. Drivers cited: normalisation of US exports after the IEEPA duties were struck down (expected to add 300+ bps), and a higher-margin domestic power cable mix (~57% of Q1 revenue). Exports were 29%+ of revenue vs 15% in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Narmadapuram, and are there cost or time overruns?
qa_highlights.answer: Most critical machinery is ordered, with delivery lead times long but expected on time. Civil construction has started and major works are expected to take 6-7 months. Management does not expect major overruns. About INR 30 crore+ has been spent, plus more than INR 155 crore over three to four years on existing plants.

qa_highlights.question: How is Narmadapuram capex funded, and what utilisation supports the INR 1,200 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt drawn yet; funding is from equity raised, internal accruals and planned term loan. Post phase 1, debt-equity is targeted below 0.3x. INR 1,200 crore is at 75% utilisation (the CFO-level comment referred to FY29). Approvals up to 66 kV are in place; 132 kV approvals are expected to start within about a year of manufacturing, with some possibly in 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export order book only INR 97 crore despite strong export revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is deliberately keeping export orders low: firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months delivery, and most customers now bear tariff changes. Management still expects INR 700-800 crore of US exports this year, versus INR 155 crore in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation, and what growth is possible in FY27 versus FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants run at practically 100% utilisation, and the constraint is manufacturing capacity rather than demand. FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%. FY28 growth is expected to be much faster once Narmadapuram starts. The INR 5,000 crore FY31 target is seen as a floor to beat.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin progress at risk if H2 export mix falls, and how do export margins compare with domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export EBITDA was negative in FY26, about -4% to -4.5% at EBITDA level. Pre-FY26 export margins were about 1.5% above domestic. It said the company can pivot quickly between domestic and export, citing FY23 and FY25 shifts, and expects export margins to keep improving each quarter.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Order book at 30 Sep 2026 was INR 731 crores (domestic INR 632 crores, export INR 99 crores), including INR 575 crores of power cable and specialized conductor orders. HTLS order book was above INR 200 crores as of the call date.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY (CFO-level range given as 15-18% for existing plants in one answer); H1 run rate described as indicative.

Operating margin to return to FY25 levels by Q4 FY27; about 8% operating margin targeted around Q4, excluding customer claw-backs, which are expected to show in Q3 results. Management said 'we are hopeful' on the 8% figure.

Narmadapuram plant: partial commissioning in Q1 FY28; revenue of about INR 500 crores in FY28 and INR 1,200 crores in FY29; capacity to double to about 60,000 MT over 3-4 years, with about 30,000 MT planned in that period.
Working capital: medium-term target 90-100 days, expected to normalize in H2 FY27.
Five-year target of INR 5,000 crores revenue by FY31, described as a guidance that will not be revised; management hopes to beat it.
Debt-equity expected to stay below 0.6-0.7 at most, and around 0.3 once the plant is operational. Long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters for a INR 300 crore capex plan.
capex_capacity: Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh) greenfield plant, third facility: foundation and civil works under way; critical machinery ordered; partial commissioning expected Q1 FY28.

Narmadapuram scope: 220 kV AC power cable line, HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type), e-beam and rubber cables. Approvals take about 1-1.5 years for 220 kV, about 12 months for 132 kV, and 3-6 months for full 66 kV range after the plant is operational.
Existing Dharuhera and Khushkhera plants running at optimal utilization; some further capex planned at both to lift revenue.
Current capacity is about 30,000 MT; management plans to double it with the new plant.
demand_pricing: Management cites T&D investment, renewables, railways and metro, and data centers as multiyear demand drivers; the National Electricity Plan projects about INR 5 lakh crore of EHV transmission investment in 2027-2032.
Management sizes HTLS reconductoring at about INR 50,000 crore over 5 years; the company says it is among the top 5 HTLS players in India and offers up to 765 kV conductors.

Copper hit record highs in the quarter; aluminium (over 75% of metal value consumed) softened. Policy is to book metal the next working day after a firm-price order, and to avoid firm-price orders beyond 3-4 months.

US tariffs: IEEPA tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court in February 2026; Indian cables now at par with Asian and European competitors. Most customers now carry tariff changes on their accounts.
Management says it is not chasing volume at the expense of margin; it is seeking approvals in Middle East, Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia, with results expected within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin glide path, given export claw-backs and the tariff effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating margin went from 1.3% in Q2 FY26 to 3.3% in Q3 and 5.2% in Q4, then 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 7.3% in Q2 FY27. Management expects domestic margins to matter more, with US exposure kept at about 30% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8% margin target before or after claw-backs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8% target is ex of claw-backs and that net claw-backs would be shown separately, visible in Q3. It was also said to be hopeful, not yet achieved, for Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is firm, and what is the cancellation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 731 crore order book comprises firm orders only, with very rare cancellations, and that even in the worst US period there were no major cancellations. It also said FY27 revenue visibility is comfortable given the H1 run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR 5,000 crore FY31 target be achieved sooner, and what margin goes with it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY31 is a conservative guidance it will not revise, but it hopes to beat it. It gave no EBITDA margin target for that revenue level.

qa_highlights.question: What are the approval timelines for the new plant's product ranges, and what revenue will come before 220 kV approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant will run on 11/33/66 kV orders from day one, with 132 kV approvals in about 12 months and 220 kV taking longer. It said the INR 500 crore FY28 and INR 1,200 crore FY29 targets will not be driven mainly by 220 kV in the first two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter B2C or face new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no plans to enter the high-cost B2C segment. B2C house wire is about INR 100 crore of roughly INR 2,000 crore revenue, and it expects B2B to be unaffected by new entrants given its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 300 crore capex be funded, and what will leverage be?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said debt-equity is 0.14x now, with long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters. Management expects debt-equity to stay around 0.3 after the plant is operational, and below 0.6-0.7 at most.

risks_watch: Metal price volatility, particularly copper and aluminium, and the company's ability to pass it through in 3-4 month order cycles.
Working capital at 108 days versus the 90-100 day target; management attributes this to early supplier payments and expects normalization in H2.
Narmadapuram execution: 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years, and FY28/FY29 revenue targets depend on ramp-up and product qualification.
Claw-back amounts and their timing, which could affect reported margins versus the 8% operating margin target.
Management's shift toward non-US export markets is at an early stage, with results expected in 1-2 years and substantial contribution in 2-3 years.
Management said the new plant's approvals and ramp-up could push the HTLS margin benefit later.
530555|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and the margin recovery, but cautious on specifics: management declined to give an EBITDA margin target and called the 8% operating margin goal 'hopeful' rather than assured. It was also evasive on HTLS technology and brand choices, saying those would not be discussed publicly.
key_quotes: When we last spoke in August, I said that we had started FY27 on a strong note and the two engines of our business, domestic and exports, were both working for us at the same time.
We are not chasing volume at the cost of margin and most of our customers now carry tariff changes to their account.
We do not accept firm-price orders with long delivery periods beyond 3 to 4 months because that is how we protect ourselves from metal volatility.
We have not achieved. It's not happened, but we can say that we are hopeful, yes.

rows.why: Operating margin rose from 1.3% in Q2 FY26 to 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 7.3% in Q2 FY27, and management targets about 8% by Q4 FY27, though it called this 'hopeful' and it excludes customer claw-backs due in Q3.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore capex) is under construction with partial commissioning guided for Q1 FY28, taking capacity from ~30,000 MT toward ~60,000 MT over 3-4 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY, H1 FY27 revenue was up 24.1% YoY, and the order book stands at INR 731 crore including INR 575 crore of power cable and conductor orders.

rows.why: Management said some further capex is planned at Dharuhera and Khushkhera, but no size or timing was given beyond the INR 300 crore Narmadapuram plan, and utilisation is described only as 'optimal' with no figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it hopes to beat the INR 5,000 crore FY31 target and that FY27 revenue visibility is comfortable, but it held FY27 growth at 15-20% and called the 8% margin only hopeful.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Narmadapuram will produce 220 kV AC power cable, HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type), e-beam and rubber cables, with 11/33/66 kV orders from day one and 132 kV approvals in about 12 months.

rows.label: Non-US export approvals (Middle East, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia)
rows.why: Management is seeking approvals in these regions with results expected within 1-2 years and substantial contribution in 2-3 years, while US exports are guided at INR 700 crore or 25-30% of FY27 revenue.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation to 90-100 days
rows.why: Net working capital days rose to 108 from 101 at end FY26 against a 90-100 day target, and management expects normalisation in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Debt-equity stays low after the plant
rows.why: Debt-equity is 0.14x now, with long-term loans for the INR 300 crore capex to be tied up in coming quarters and management expects it to stay around 0.3 once the plant is operational.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the order book and FY27 growth of 15-20%, but cautious on the 8% margin target, calling it 'hopeful', and declined to give an EBITDA margin target; analysts pressed on margin glide path, claw-backs, and order book firmness.

530655|2026-03.headline: Goodluck India Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin above 10% and PAT up 34% YoY to over INR56 crore, while FY27 growth guidance was trimmed to 14-15%.
530655|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR1,097 crore, with management citing EBITDA margins above 10% and PAT up 34% YoY to over INR56 crore. Standalone Q4 sales fell to INR1,061.46 crore from INR1,104.62 crore, while standalone Q4 EBITDA rose 11.7% to INR104.19 crore. FY26 revenue growth of about 4% to 5% fell well short of the earlier 15-20% guidance, which management blamed on lower HRC prices and the West Asia conflict disrupting dispatches. Defence (artillery shells) began production in Jan-Feb 2026 after licensing in October 2025 and contributed about INR46 crore revenue and INR29 crore EBITDA in FY26, a margin inflated by start-up depreciation and interest per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 14-15% (earlier 15-20%), with management hopeful but conditional on West Asia conflict easing.
Defence EBITDA margin guided at 30-35% once volumes are sufficient, though management said FY26's margin was not sustainable.

Steel prices fell from April 2025 to April 2026 per management, though an analyst noted HRC rose from about INR48,000 to INR58,000 per tonne between December 2025 and May 2026.
West Asia conflict raised consumable costs; management said pass-through takes 1-2 quarters. Exports slowed by about 5-10% due to longer transit times.
Raw material (HRC) shortage in March-April reportedly persists, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What was FY26 defence revenue and EBITDA, and why is the margin so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue was INR46 crore and EBITDA INR29 crore. Management attributed the high margin to start-up depreciation and interest being booked over only 2-3 months of production, with material stuck at port. It said 30-35% margins are the sustainable guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 steel business grow, given utilisation near 95%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity is being added via GI conduit pipe and front fork tube lines, taking capacity to 6 lakh tonnes in 9-12 months, so volume growth of 13-15% is expected in steel.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue grow only 4-5% against the 15-20% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lower steel prices from April 2025 to April 2026 hurt realisation, and the West Asia conflict disrupted dispatches in March. FY27 guidance was trimmed to 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did capex and debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the INR340 crore capex figure, citing WIP of about INR232 crore. Debt rose because working capital increased from slower realisations and inventory build-up in the domestic glut.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and repayment schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR1,000 crore at March 2026 (INR800 crore working capital, INR200 crore term loan) against about INR50 crore cash. Term-loan repayments are INR54 crore in FY26 and INR51 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for conduit pipes and front fork tubes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conduit pipe margins are normally 15-25% and planning should use 15-20%. Front fork tube margins were put at 15-16%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia crisis hit Q1 FY27 and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is premature to call Q1. It expects margins to hold through product and market reshuffling, with a possible 5-10% export impact that could resolve within weeks.

Working capital and inventory days have risen and management said normalisation is not yet visible, pushing debt higher.
Defence margin sustainability: FY26 margin was flattered by start-up costs, and the guided 30-35% has not yet been demonstrated.
Timing of the 400,000-shell expansion (about INR400 crore) and of the 6 lakh tonne steel capacity.
Management declined to give shell pricing or margin on the recent order, and deferred the defence IPO and subsidiary questions to separate channels.

530655|2026-06.headline: Goodluck India Q1 FY27 standalone revenue up ~23% to INR1,205.9 cr, EBITDA up 15% to INR110.5 cr; Defence expansion delayed 6-9 months.
530655|2026-06.overview: Standalone income from operations rose to INR1,205.94 crore from INR983.29 crore YoY, while standalone EBITDA rose 15% to INR110.53 crore and PAT rose to INR49.66 crore from INR40.14 crore. Management cited 31% consolidated revenue growth, 46% consolidated EBITDA growth and 67% consolidated PAT growth, with EBITDA margin above 10%. Defence (Goodluck Defence & Aerospace) won orders of INR255 crore and INR52 crore for 155 mm shells, but its capacity expansion has slipped 6-9 months due to financial closure. A preferential issue at the Defence subsidiary (about 75 lakh shares at INR375, about INR285 crore) drew heavy shareholder criticism over valuation and the choice over a rights issue at parent level.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Defence subsidiary being listed separately rather than demerged, and how does that create value for current shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers recommended a separate listing; the listing will be based on future numbers. Parent shareholders benefit as a subsidiary's value accrues to the group.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the subsidiary stake sold through a preferential issue instead of a rights issue at Goodluck India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial advisers preferred this route and that the company needs funds for growth. Management acknowledged a differing view and said it would consider feedback.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidiary's implied valuation from the INR285 crore issue at INR375/share?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-issue outstanding shares about 4.91 crore; post-issue about 5.66 crore shares (about 75 lakh new shares). Implied valuation not explicitly stated; dilution cited as about 10.5% (an investor said 15%).

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Defence expansion slipped and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Delay is due to financial closure of the project and approvals; expansion now expected to start by Q4 FY27, with commercialisation around a year later.

qa_highlights.question: What are Defence margins and revenue in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Defence revenue about INR80 crore at about 38% EBITDA; management is guiding 30-35% sustainable margin, stating it is conservative.

530655|2026-09.headline: Goodluck India Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose ~38% YoY to INR13.7 bn, with EBITDA up 31% and margin pressured ~150 bps by freight and gas costs.
530655|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 total income grew about 38% YoY to INR13.7 bn, EBITDA rose to INR1.27 bn (9.3% margin vs 9.18%), and PAT reached INR506 mn (up ~19%). Sales volume grew 18.1% to 133,374 tonnes, while H1 volume grew 13.5% to 256,093 tonnes. Management attributed the margin squeeze to higher international freight and gas prices, estimated at ~150 bps. Management also proposed amalgamating Goodluck Defence and Aerospace and Goodluck Green Energy into Goodluck India, targeting 12–16 months for completion.

530759|2026-03.headline: Sterling Tools FY26 standalone fasteners EBITDA rose 17.1% to INR111 crore at 15.3% margin, but management flags Q1 FY27 cost pressure and a delayed EV timeline.
530759|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 standalone fastener business total income up 11.4% YoY to INR725.9 crore, EBITDA up 17.1% to INR111 crore, and margin of 15.3% versus 14.5%. Profit before exceptional items rose 27.6% to INR74 crore and operating cash flow was INR83.3 crore. A subsidiary-level Q4 loss of INR21 crore was attributed to a bad-debt provision on one bigger customer, which management said is still likely recoverable. The EV business timeline was pushed out by 3 to 5 years and target aspirations deferred by about a year, with SEM expected to return to profitability in FY28 rather than FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there annual price-reduction contracts with OEMs, and what margin pressure is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Aggarwal said there are no price-reduction contracts; Q1 FY27 will be a special pressure quarter, with price increases from customers expected from Q2 and efficiency gains to offset.

qa_highlights.question: What is the domestic market share and non-auto revenue exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates 25-30% share of the domestic automotive fastener market; revenue is predominantly automotive. Railway is early-stage and not expected to be meaningful for two years.

qa_highlights.question: When will SEM return to EBITDA and PBT profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep said SEM will not be profitable in FY27 but there is no reason it cannot be profitable in FY28; other businesses depend on their start-up timelines.

qa_highlights.answer: Atul said there may be short-term pressure, but steady-state EBITDA margin should be maintained around 15% plus.

qa_highlights.answer: Atul said capex will be commercialised by Q4 FY27, revenue potential about INR800 crore plus, rising to INR900-1,000 crore; asset turn around 2x, with 24-month turnaround on brownfield capex.

Subsidiaries SEM and STML continue to lose money; both are guided to break even in FY28 at combined revenue of about INR225-250 crore. Capacity utilisation is 90-95% and an INR88 crore fasteners capex (misstated as INR80 crore on the call) is mostly expected to commission in H2 FY27.

530813|2026-03.headline: KRBL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR1,526 crore as record domestic sales (+22%) offset a 33% export drop from Middle East disruption; PAT INR155 crore.

Q4 gross margin fell to 29.6% (from 31.5%) and EBITDA margin to 15.5% (from 16.2%), with PAT of INR155 crore (10.1% margin) against INR154 crore a year earlier. For FY26, total income rose 9% to INR6,168 crore, with EBITDA margin of 15.8% and PAT margin of 10.5%. Management said Q1 export trends are hard to call and gave no monthly export numbers; it expects demand to rebound once the conflict settles.

rows.why: New Gangavathi facility for regional products is expected to be operational by end of Q3 FY27, with a 25% regional rice growth target on a base of about INR270 crores; no capacity size was disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27, with recovery from Q2 FY27
rows.why: Management maintains about 10% domestic volume growth for FY27 and says bulk-pack volumes resume in Q2 and Q3 after a Q1 dip; export volumes expected to recover from Q2 with Q2 exports 'much better', though Q1 Middle East exports fell from INR485 crore to INR244 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Inventory of 389,000 tons of rice is described as comfortable and paddy stock fell to 71,000 tons from 91,000 tons, with management planning to buy more this season, but no capex amount was disclosed and utilisation was not given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called Q1 margins unsustainable and withheld price guidance, and FY27 export recovery depends on the Strait of Hormuz staying open; Q1 export revenue fell about 50% to INR244 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: More regional rice varieties are to be listed on quick commerce platforms later this year, and the masala portfolio targets an INR25 crore annualised run rate by FY27-end from about INR9 crores now (up 74% YoY).

rows.label: Saudi Arabia distributor appointment and direct entity
rows.why: 3-4 distributor candidates identified, but finalisation awaits peace in the region; the direct entity programme is deferred while wholesaler shipments continue.

rows.label: Basmati price rise if Gulf supply gap reopens
rows.why: Basmati realisations were up about 20% YoY and 13% QoQ, Pakistani basmati is priced about USD100/ton above Indian material, and Pakistan's rice exports fell about 26% in volume; a rise hinges on peace and the size of the new crop.

rows.label: ED matter and governance
rows.why: The company disclosed an ED matter and management declined to respond to queries on it, so the outcome is open.

tone.note: Management was confident on the domestic franchise, 10% volume growth and export recovery timing, but cautious that Q1 margins are unsustainable and evasive on FY27 price guidance, Saudi distributor timing and the ED matter; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, inventory purchases and the Gulf

530813|2026-09.headline: KRBL Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,727 crore (+14% YoY) on a 33% domestic surge, while exports fell 41% in H1 on Middle East disruption.
530813|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was KRBL's highest-ever quarterly revenue, driven by domestic branded consumer packs (volume +18% YoY per management, with a later +19% figure) and a selective INR102 crore bulk rice sale. Exports remained the weak spot: H1 export revenue was INR541 crore (-41%), almost entirely from bulk exports to the Middle East, though Q2 exports rose 22% QoQ to INR297 crore. PAT was INR159 crore (14.6% margin) versus INR172 crore (11.2%) a year earlier, and cash plus treasury investments rose to INR2,895 crore. Management guided Q3 EBITDA of 16-20% and FY27 EBITDA of 17-19%, with paddy prices up sharply for the new crop.

financial_highlights.change: vs 29.2% in Q2 FY26; 32.9% vs 33.5% QoQ per analyst figures
vs INR172 crore (11.2%) in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank incl. treasury investments
financial_highlights.change: vs INR2,157 crore a year earlier

financial_highlights.value: INR2,203 crore (paddy INR146 crore, rice INR1,900 crore)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR2,118 crore-equivalent prior year (paddy INR123 crore, rice INR1,995 crore)

segments.name: Domestic (India business)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue ex-power INR1,390 crore in Q2 (+33% YoY); H1 INR2,612 crore (+24%). Branded rice INR1,134 crore (+23%); unbranded INR166 crore including a one-off INR102 crore bulk sale.

segments.name: Branded consumer packs
segments.commentary: Consumer pack volume growth accelerated to 18% in Q2 from 7% in Q1; modern trade and e-commerce +31%, general trade +10% after a ~5% decline in Q1. Bulk packs +11% YoY in Q2; regional rice +42% in Q2, +32% in H1.

segments.name: Export (bulk and branded)
segments.commentary: H1 export revenue INR541 crore (-41%), driven by bulk exports to the Middle East; branded exports +18% in H1 and non-Middle East exports +14% in H1. Bulk sales in H1 described as almost zero.

segments.name: Edible oil and masala
segments.commentary: Uplife oil Q2 turnover about INR6 crore; masala H1 sales about INR4.5 crore vs INR3.1 crore, with a FY27 exit run-rate ambition of about INR25 crore.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 16-20%, with management saying it could be near 20%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 17-19%.
Domestic rice volume growth of about 10% YoY targeted for FY27 (H2 specifically); management said the 19% Q2 rate is not a promise.
Domestic price increases of about 7-8% in Q3 on average (management), after earlier cited 15-18% on specific price points.

Exports expected to recover progressively in H2 FY27, dependent on Gulf conditions; management said FY27 exports could match or beat last year's roughly INR1,500-1,550 crore, and the analyst's INR7,500 crore revenue / 16-17% PAT scenario was described as feasible if exports recover.
If the US-Iran situation settles, bulk exports could more than double, with management citing 30,000-40,000 tons or more; Iran previously ~100,000 tons a year.

qa_highlights.question: What export and volume growth is expected from here, and would exports double if the US-Iran situation settles?
qa_highlights.answer: Anil Mittal said exports could more than double once a US-Iran agreement is reached, with bulk sales (near zero in H1) possibly reaching 30,000-40,000 tons or more. Ayush Gupta reiterated about 10% domestic volume growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected in Q3 given the low-cost inventory and higher paddy prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Anoop Gupta guided Q3 EBITDA of 16-20%, saying old-crop stock earns higher margins and new-crop margins will be lower; he later said the figure would be nearing 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 vs Q1 volume growth, and why did gross margin fall from 33.5% to 32.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Jain cited 18% QoQ rice volume growth and 18% QoQ domestic growth, and attributed the margin dip to lower forex and treasury gains in other income, with higher freight and advertising costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation for domestic and export sales and the Q3 price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic realisation was about INR80/kg and exports about INR132/kg. Management said Q3 domestic prices would be about 7-8% higher on average, after earlier citing 15-18% increases.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach about INR7,500 crore with a 16-17% PAT margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Jain said H1 revenue was about INR3,200 crore. He said the scenario looks feasible only if H2 exports recover to at least the prior year's roughly INR1,550 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are quick commerce contribution, the Middle East outlook, and capital return plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce is 8-9% of India business with a 41.1% share. Anoop Gupta said a buyback could be considered and the company would discuss it internally. The dividend policy is 15% of profit, with management indicating it could exceed that.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on the Strait of Hormuz, freight and war-risk premiums, and banking channels; Iran is largely shut due to tighter US sanctions since August.
Paddy inflation (about 20% YoY) may compress margins as new-crop costs flow through, even with price increases of about 7-8% in Q3.
Consumer pack sustainability in H2 and whether the 18-19% Q2 volume growth holds; the India Gate price increase may trigger a shift to loose rice or smaller packs.
Uplife edible oil availability on e-commerce platforms; management said e-commerce sales are slow and investment needs are high.
Sub-judice ED matter, on which management declined to take questions.
Monsoon-linked crop estimates (basmati crop reported modestly above last year, with October rain damage) and possible next-year weather risk.

We would rather protect the quality to our business than chase volume.
We will not chase the market.

Modern trade and e-commerce consumer pack volumes +31%; general trade +10% after about 5% decline in Q1. Bulk packs +11% YoY in Q2, October described as another strong month; regional rice +42% in Q2, +32% in H1.

Domestic realisation about INR80/kg in both Q1 and Q2 FY27, about 12% higher than Q2 FY26. Export realisation about INR132/kg in Q2. Price increases taken across the portfolio in Q3: management said 7-8% on average, after earlier citing 15-18% on specific price points.

Guidance: domestic rice volume growth of about 10% for FY27 (H2 focus), with management saying the 19% Q2 rate is not a promise; FY27 exports expected to match or beat the prior year's roughly INR1,500-1,550 crore; FY27 EBITDA 17-19%; Q3 EBITDA 16-20%, with management later saying it would be nearing 20%.
