530999|2026-03.headline: Balaji Amines Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% YoY to INR403 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25% versus 19% a year earlier.
530999|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR403 crore (up about 12% YoY) and EBITDA was INR102 crore against INR68 crore, lifting margin to 25% from 19% in Q4 FY25 and 18% in Q3 FY26. PAT reached INR65 crore versus INR40 crore a year earlier. Management said production was briefly hit in March 2026 by a geopolitical situation but was managed through inventory planning. For FY27 management guided to 10-15% consolidated volume growth in Q&A, and to 20-30% volume growth and 22-23% EBITDA margin by end-FY27 (wording varied during the call). Specialty subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals was running partially during modifications, which depressed its quarterly margins.

segments.name: Amines
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 7,746 MT. Management said DMF and butylamines run at low utilisation as battery-chemical demand has yet to ramp.

segments.name: Amines derivatives
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 8,935 MT; described as a stable operating base.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 10,660 MT. Subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals ran only about 10-20 days a month during modifications, and management said Q4 subsidiary margins are not a usable benchmark.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume growth of 10-15% (Q&A, for this year), with 20-30% volume growth cited for the period to end-FY27 once new plants ramp.
EBITDA margin expected to be sustainable at 22-23% of sales (stated for end-FY27).
Management targets INR3,000 crore revenue in FY28 (said to be reached in 2028); an earlier-cited INR2,000 crore target was referenced by an analyst.
DME plant at Unit 4 expected to commission in Q1 FY27; utilisation of 30-40% in FY27, 50-60% by year-end, and 80-90% in the following year, subject to road transport permission.
Balaji Specialty Chemicals Unit-I (EDA-based DETA, TETA, PIP, AEEA, AEP) expected in H1 FY27; Unit-II Chincholi (HCN, NaCN, EDTA, EDTA-2Na) expected in Q4 FY27.

Standalone capex remaining for DME, NMM and ACN is about INR20 crore; subsidiary capex about INR275-290 crore consolidated this year (INR200-250 crore subsidiary spend). Phase 1 of the INR750 crore expansion is INR350-400 crore.
capex_capacity: Standalone capacity cited by an analyst at 2,93,000 MT; an analyst estimated utilisation at 35-40%, which management did not dispute.
NMM project of 5,000 TPA under execution, commissioning during FY27; improved-process Acetonitrile (ACN) plant to commission in Q2 FY27.
DME plant at Unit 4 (about 1 lakh tonne capacity) ready to commission; road transport permission awaited, expected in about a month per management.
Balaji Specialty Chemicals expansion of about INR750 crore in phases, Maharashtra Mega Project status under Package Scheme of Incentives 2019.
Battery chemicals unit is running at 20-25% capacity, with production also going to agro and pharma uses.
demand_pricing: Management said raw material costs were up to 2-3x normal in some cases; monoethanolamine was cited at about 3x normal.
EDA/DETA prices averaged about INR300/kg in Q4 and were INR270-280 currently, per management.
Indicative prices: DME about INR100-120/kg, ACN about INR240, NMM about INR250-300.
A large metformin customer that backward-integrated still buys DMA-HCl; management put it at 15-20% of outflow for that product.
Ammonia and methanol available; prices volatile, with purchases now made in shorter lots every 3-4 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand with standalone utilisation around 35-40%, and which products are low-utilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new projects are new products, not capacity adds for existing lines. Low utilisation is in DMF, butylamines and battery chemicals (DMC) because battery demand has not started.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken in Q4 and what realisation growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers accepted price increases in Q4 and margins were held through inventory management. Guidance: 20-30% volume growth and 22-23% EBITDA margin by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR2,000 crore to INR3,000 crore FY28 target realistic given DME approvals and slow specialty demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DME manufacturing permissions are in place and only transport approval is pending. It reaffirmed INR3,000 crore revenue in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did subsidiary other expenses drop and what are subsidiary raw material trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary worked about 10-15 days a month during modifications, with repair costs partly capitalised. Monoethanolamine costs were about 3x normal. Management said the quarter was not a benchmark and asked analysts to email the company secretary for modelling inputs.

qa_highlights.question: What is remaining standalone capex and FY27 subsidiary capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone balance is about INR20 crore. Subsidiary spend is about INR200-250 crore this year after INR110 crore already spent, for total consolidated capex of INR275-290 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will DME be sold before transport permission arrives and what volume is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Samples went out in 500 kg cylinders for trials, and bulk orders follow permission. Management said FY27 utilisation would be marginal, with 60-70% growth next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company increase its stake in BSE, and what is the status of the greenfield project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake increase needs both boards and shareholders, and an IPO is not yet decided. On capex, it said modifications at the subsidiary began last year, and it plans to invite investors to a plant visit around June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of antidumping duties on DMF and EDA?
qa_highlights.answer: No DMF application has been filed, and the old case remains. The EDA case was at final stage, but duty exemptions run to end-June, so the outcome is pending.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: ammonia, methanol and monoethanolamine prices and supply are moving every few days, and management said margin holds depend on this.
Battery chemicals demand (DMC, DMF, electrolytes) has not ramped, and a plant running at 20-25% is still dependent on a customer start.
DME commissioning depends on road transport permission and the first-time product market acceptance; management guides to 30-40% FY27 utilisation.
Subsidiary Balaji Specialty Chemicals is partly idle during modifications, so its quarterly numbers are not clean; watch Q1 and Q2 FY27 ramp-up.
Antidumping duty decisions on EDA and DMF are pending; government exemptions run to end-June 2026.
Management guidance was inconsistent on FY27 volume growth (10-15% vs 20-30%) and on the FY28 revenue target (INR2,000 crore vs INR3,000 crore).

Tone turned defensive when analysts questioned the INR3,000 crore FY28 target and subsidiary performance.

530999|2026-09.headline: Balaji Amines Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to INR472 crores and PAT 82% to INR67 crores, though EBITDA fell sequentially to INR106 crores.
530999|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR472 crores, up about 36% YoY and up from INR461 crores in Q1, while EBITDA was INR106 crores (22% margin) versus INR121 crores (26%) in Q1. Sales volume rose about 13.5% QoQ to 24,491 MT but was down about 6% YoY. H1 FY27 PAT was INR146 crores, up about 98%, despite H1 volumes falling to 46,078 MT from 53,735 MT. The company commissioned the expanded Acetonitrile plant (1,440 TPM) and the DME plant, and it received PESO approval for DME road tanker valves; brownfield and greenfield specialty chemicals projects have slipped toward FY27 end and Q4 FY27 respectively.

segments.name: Amines (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 6,525 MT. Unit-4 methylamine utilisation is only about 15-20% per management, while Unit-3 ran at about 80%.

segments.name: Amines Derivatives (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 8,974 MT. DMF plant utilisation rose from about 30-40% to more than 50% on DMF prices of INR110-115 per kg. EDA utilisation is about 50-60%.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 8,992 MT. DME and Acetonitrile are ramping; Acetonitrile is priced around INR230-240 per kg.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to reach INR3,500-4,000 crores top line by FY28-29, which the analyst had framed as a INR3,000-4,000 crore aspiration.
All expansions, including Acetonitrile, DME, DMF, NMM and the Balaji Specialty Chemicals projects, are to be completed by end of FY27. From Q1 FY28, the focus shifts to utilisation of 80-90%.

Unit-1 brownfield at Balaji Specialty Chemicals (EDA derivatives) is expected to be commissioned by end FY27. Unit-2 greenfield at Chincholi (hydrogen cyanide, sodium cyanide, EDTA) is targeted for Q4 FY27, with some products possibly slipping to February or March 2027.
NMM commercialisation is targeted during FY27.

DME: bulk supply is expected once Road Tanker approval is received (3-4 weeks) and the BPCL LPG-blending approval is in place. Capacity utilisation could exceed 90% with that approval, or 50-55% without it.
Acetonitrile: full capacity of 1,440 MT per month expected in 2-3 weeks; management guided minimum 1,000-1,200 MT per month from December, subject to market acceptance.
DME pricing indicated at INR90-100 per kg currently, expected to be competitive with LPG once methanol falls below INR80 per kg.
capex_capacity: Expanded Acetonitrile plant commenced commercial production in Q2 FY27 at 1,440 tons per month capacity, with improved process technology.
DME plant commissioned; PESO approval received for DME road tanker valves. Road tanker approval expected in 3-4 weeks. 7-8 ISO tanks exported for aerosol use; about 20-25 cylinders sold domestically.

Unit-1 at Balaji Specialty Chemicals (brownfield EDA derivatives: DETA, TETA, Piperazine, AEEA, AEP) is being run in 10-15 day cycles alternating with modifications. Remaining work is small equipment erection, to finish in one or two cycles by January 2027.
Unit-2 greenfield at MIDC Chincholi is in equipment erection and installation, targeted for Q4 FY27.

Di-isopropylamine process improvement reported as yielding positive results. Management also cited a DMC/DMC-PC order from a battery electrolyte client for 500-1,000 MT, with delivery expected from next month.
demand_pricing: Volumes lag because raw material prices are volatile, so the company is booking orders against demand rather than building inventory. H1 FY27 volume fell about 14% YoY.
DMF prices rose to INR110-115 per kg from earlier levels. Management said Chinese dumping had previously made Indian DMF uneconomic.
EDA price improved, but anti-dumping duty recommended by the Commerce Ministry was not implemented by the Finance Ministry. The company plans a High Court writ petition within about one month.
Methanol is about INR61-62 per kg versus INR6 when management began the business. Management expects normal levels of INR26-30. Ammonia is INR80-90 versus a normal INR45-50.
DME demand is mainly aerosol in India (over 50,000 tons consumption) and export; LPG blending is pending BPCL and government approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the DMF plant now that DMF prices have risen, and when will Unit-4 methylamine improve?

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on DMC supply to the battery electrolyte client and on any further capacity?

qa_highlights.question: Why is EDA volume not picking up after anti-dumping, and what is the next step?

qa_highlights.question: What approvals remain for DME LPG blending, and what pricing should be used?

qa_highlights.question: What Acetonitrile pricing should be assumed, and what is the value growth outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Unit-1 brownfield expansion been delayed from July, then October, to year-end?

qa_highlights.question: PAT grew about 25% against 4% revenue growth: how much is from finance costs or tax, and what is the normalized PAT growth trajectory?

qa_highlights.question: Can the existing order book support double-digit growth without material new wins, and what is its execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is to be executed over about 3 years, with book-to-bill around 3x. Target new order inflow is about Rs 8,000 crore this year, needed for 10% growth this year and 15% next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company have any exceptional items in FY27, after about Rs 150 crore in the last two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect exceptional items this year. Last year's items were mainly Vivaad-se-Vishwas settlements and some investment write-downs.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the Telangana land sale and further monetization?
qa_highlights.answer: The sale was 27 acres for Rs 26-27 crore, leaving about 400 acres in Telangana. Other parcels are under discussion. Non-core monetization target is Rs 150-200 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge reduction timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters and the company are in talks with lenders and expect a substantial reduction this year. Management said around 85-90% of shares are pledged and expects at least a 15-20% reduction, without a specific timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Patel Smondo OC timing and occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: OC is expected this financial year after a pending litigation closes. The third tower is a service apartment tower, ready to occupy once OC comes. Some buyers have taken possession for fit-outs.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 15%, and are buybacks or ESOPs being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm 15% margins because competition has risen and a large project was lost last year. Margins are targeted at 13-14%. Buybacks will be considered after debt reduction, which may take two to three years. ESOPs will be handled through the existing ESOP trust.

qa_highlights.question: How much working capital and capex will execution need, and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Client advances against bank guarantees or surety bonds should cover most needs. Working capital borrowing of Rs 100-200 crore may be needed in between. The 14.02% margin is mostly project mix, with an average of 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Dredging, and the arbitration awards above Rs 1,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is looking at dredging work, alone or with partners. Arbitrations are being followed up, and settlements are explored where possible. PSUs usually litigate through all courts.

qa_highlights.question: Receivable days and Q2 revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 40-45, and this continues in new contracts. Q2 is seasonally slower because of monsoon, with some ups and downs but no major disruption expected.

qa_highlights.question: Hydro bids under evaluation and outcome timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Bids under evaluation total about Rs 9,000 crore, mostly Arunachal and North-East hydro, with a Rs 60,000 crore pipeline. Management said outcomes are hoped for by Diwali, which the CEO called hopeful.

qa_highlights.question: Retention money and release timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention is about 5% of each contract, around Rs 200-250 crore on the balance sheet. It is mostly released at project end, though some projects allow withdrawal against bank guarantees.

531147|2026-09.headline: Alicon Q2 FY27 total income hit a record Rs 652 crore (+50% YoY), with EBITDA up 14% YoY to Rs 65.3 crore and margin at 10%.

guidance_outlook: Opex-to-AUM target of about 7% by March 2027 (vs peak of c.9-10%); currently at about 8%, management says on track.
Long-run opex-to-AUM view: around 6% would be 'fairly good'; the lowest historical MFI level was c.4.5-4.75%.
Management says INR5,000 crore AUM is achievable within about 18 months; no formal guidance on timing given.
No capital raise needed to reach INR5,000 crore AUM, per management.
Management remains positive on H2 FY27, with Q4 historically the strongest quarter.
Possible CGFMU renewal could bring one-time opex load and provision reversals; management said the outcome is unknowable at this stage.
capex_capacity: Operating model: separated credit and recovery from branch operations; independent credit team for MFI, separate recovery team for branches needing support.
Loans under the new credit structure show c.15% lower default rates than the earlier model (management cautions the true test is the next credit cycle).
Around 110,000 applications processed per month, leading to 25,000-30,000 disbursed customers.
Digital collections: c.49% of microfinance collections via UPI and e-NACH as of Sep 2026; individual lending c.40% of MFI portfolio.
Workforce c.5,200 employees (errata to 5,700) across 11 states.
demand_pricing: Competition: management says smaller players and some large players face difficulty; banks serving MFIs via BC/co-lending have pulled back in certain cases, while fintechs and gold loans compete for rural borrowers.
Good-quality customers face very competitive demand; borrowers with past defaults are hard to lend to.
Rejection rates remain high by design; management says it would rather turn away business than take on future problem customers.
Average ticket size in LAP and MSME fell QoQ; management attributed this to credit policy and risk tolerance, not demand.
Incremental borrowing cost fell to 11.3%; Acuité reaffirmed A- with outlook revised to positive, CARE reaffirmed A- stable.

qa_highlights.question: How is competitive intensity in your geographies, given SFBs pulling back from MFI and small NBFC liquidity stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition persists from fintechs and gold loans, and some large players are struggling too; banks via BC and co-lending have pulled back in some cases, but Arman has no problem accessing bank funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the collection efficiency dip from 96.9% in June to 96.2% in September normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a post-monsoon dip is normal historically; Maharashtra saw some deterioration and Gujarat saw impact from low rainfall; Vivek Modi said the c.40bp PAR 30-90 rise is being watched but not overly worried about, with a delayed drought impact possible.

qa_highlights.question: Does CGFMU non-renewal change strategy, given MFI cover fell from c.90% to 51%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said strategy is unchanged; CGFMU is an insurance layer, not a substitute for underwriting; the company survived 34 years without it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CGFMU renewal and UPI MDR affect provisions, opex and the 7% target?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi said NCGTC indicates a strong likelihood of a policy with delay, and any premium could be P&L-neutral versus provision reversals. On UPI MDR, the company is awaiting industry-level exemption and has not included it in the 7% target.

qa_highlights.question: When will AUM reach INR5,000 crore and what is the opex-to-AUM outlook; is capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR5,000 crore is definitely achievable in about 18 months with compounding; opex-to-AUM around 6% would be good; no capital raise needed while growing near ROE.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Arman standalone provisions decline QoQ (INR5.2 crore to INR4 crore) despite portfolio growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Modi attributed it to better asset quality, lower write-offs, and a higher LAP share (c.13%, GNPA sub-1.5%) versus unsecured (c.3%); the CGFMU-covered MSME book of c.INR200 crore+ also helps.

risks_watch: CGFMU renewal timing and terms; loans originated from April 1, 2026 are not covered; MFI cover is down to 51% of the portfolio and MSME cover to 30%.
Drought in Maharashtra and Karnataka (7.6% of AUM): Maharashtra fresh delinquencies rose about 1% in October; impact may lag several months.
Possible UPI MDR cost on digital collections if no exemption is granted; the impact is currently unquantified.
Microfinance PAR 30-90 up about 40bp QoQ; management asked investors not to track QoQ basis points.
Opex-to-AUM target of 7% by March 2027 remains at about 8% today; cost trajectory vs growth.
Sustainability of the 15% lower default-rate benefit of the new credit structure, untested through a full credit cycle.
531179|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operating turnaround and growth, with explicit caution on Maharashtra and Karnataka drought stress, the CGFMU lapse and UPI MDR; management was candid about not having answers on CGFMU terms or MDR, and deflected some questions (e.g., the 'antifragile' theme) with humour.
key_quotes: Q2 has been a particularly strong quarter for Arman.
Our rejection rates remain high, and we are perfectly comfortable with that.
It does not change our strategy, and I think I made that in my kind of said that in my opening remarks as well, that CGFMU was available.
Even today, as far as Arman is concerned, we have no problem accessing bank funding or anything like that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Opex-to-AUM guided from about 8% toward 7% by March 2027 (peak c.9-10%), and Namra NIM rose to 16.6% from 15.37% in Q1, with cost-to-income down to 42.6% from 51.7% peak in Q4 FY26; offset risk from CGFMU and UPI MDR costs is unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM at INR3,209 crore (+51% YoY) with Q2 disbursement INR818 crore (+72% YoY); management says INR5,000 crore is achievable in about 18 months, roughly 56% above current AUM, though no formal timing was guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no capital raise is needed to reach INR5,000 crore AUM, and no new capex or branch expansion was discussed beyond the operating model change.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Maharashtra and Karnataka drought stress (7.6% of AUM), PAR 30-90 up about 40bp in microfinance, and CGFMU cover down to 51% for MFI (from c.90%) could pressure provisions, though management calls the CGFMU outcome unknowable.

rows.label: CGFMU renewal and UPI MDR outcome
rows.why: NCGTC indicates strong likelihood of a delayed policy, with any premium possibly P&L-neutral versus provision reversals; UPI MDR exemption pending and excluded from the 7% opex target, impact unquantified.

rows.label: Opex-to-AUM falls to about 7%
rows.why: Opex-to-AUM currently about 8% versus peak c.9-10%, management says on track; cost-to-income already fell to 42.6% from 51.7% in Q4 FY26.

rows.label: Borrowing cost decline and rating upgrade
rows.why: Incremental borrowing cost fell to 11.3% from 11.7% in Q1, and Acuité revised outlook to positive from A- reaffirmed; Arman has no problem accessing bank funding.

tone.note: Management was confident on the turnaround, AUM growth and cost trajectory, but cautious on drought stress, CGFMU renewal terms and UPI MDR; analysts pressed on competition, collection efficiency dip from 96.9% to 96.2%, and provisioning trends.

531201|2026-03.headline: Shilchar FY26 revenue INR652 crore (+5%) and EBITDA margin 29%, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 21% on deferred Middle East and US shipments and oil-led input inflation.
531201|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations was INR652 crore (about 5% growth), EBITDA INR190 crore (29% margin) and PAT INR158 crore (+8%, EPS INR138). Q4 FY26 was weak: revenue INR152 crore, EBITDA margin 21%, PAT INR28 crore, as a large March export volume (INR35-40 crore) could not be shipped due to West Asia logistics disruption and US tariff uncertainty had slowed order intake earlier. Management says these were temporary, dispatches to the Middle East resumed in April, and it is seeking price revisions from customers for raw material inflation (oil roughly doubled since February, other commodities up 10-25%). FY27 guidance is INR800-850 crore revenue with margins targeted at 29-31%, and the Gavasad expansion (6,500 MVA, total 14,000 MVA) is due for commissioning in April 2027.

financial_highlights.change: down roughly 7-8 percentage points vs prior quarters per analyst; management said margin would have matched Q1-Q3 without March disruption

financial_highlights.value: Export about INR52 crore; domestic about INR100 crore

segments.name: Domestic transformers (incl. renewables/solar & wind)
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic revenue about INR100 crore; domestic renewable transformer order inflows described as strong, with India commissioning 55 GW renewables in FY26. Price revisions being secured from domestic customers, with at least a couple agreed.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 export revenue about INR52 crore, with about INR35-40 crore of March shipments deferred. Middle East was about 30% of FY25-26 revenue; US was 18-19% of FY26 revenue. Export share of current INR452 crore order book is about 30-32%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target INR800-850 crore; management said it is conservative and could reach INR900 crore, with the INR800 crore figure described as the floor it is confident of.
FY27 volume target about 7,000 MVA vs about 6,000 MVA dispatched in FY26.
Q1 FY27 described as a normal quarter; no April actuals disclosed. Management expects growth to resume from the coming quarter.
EBITDA margin target for FY27 of 29-31%, with management saying it will try to maintain or increase margins.

Expansion (Gavasad expansion 3): 6,500 MVA, total 14,000 MVA, commissioning April 2027, capex about INR120 crore funded from internal accruals. Full benefit expected in FY29-FY30; power transformer approvals (up to 160 MVA, 220 kV class) need registration and customer audits.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity 7,500 MVA; FY26 dispatches about 6,000 MVA (79% utilisation on a dispatch basis). Management said production utilisation is higher, with closing stock carried into FY27.

Gavasad expansion 3: adds 6,500 MVA, taking total to 14,000 MVA; commissioning targeted April 2027; civil foundation complete, PEB erection and utility work in progress, major production equipment ordered; capex about INR120 crore funded from internal accruals.
New facility can make transformers up to 160 MVA, 220 kV class; until power transformer approvals come through, it will produce solar and wind transformers.
Management said it would plan further expansion beyond 6,500 MVA and announce it later; once fully utilised, the company could reach about INR1,500 crore turnover.
Current power transformer lead time is 12-16 weeks. Bushings are sourced from Yash Highvoltage (Vadodara); China imports are also planned.
demand_pricing: FY27 order book about INR452 crore, about 30-32% export; management said FY27 order visibility is roughly INR800 crore, with robust domestic and export inquiries.

Price revisions sought from almost all customers for raw material inflation: oil up about 100% since February, other commodities up 10-25%. Some customers have agreed, others are in discussion; for fixed-price orders the company is invoking force majeure, while PV-clause orders pass through prices at dispatch.
Transformer oil is 8-12% of transformer cost. Company says it books copper or aluminium when orders are won, but this time suppliers also could not hold prices.
US tariffs were cut to about 10% from 50% (announced August 2025), and management says it is now winning US orders again. Management expects US export growth over the next 2-3 years.

Management says the competitive situation is good, with no overcapacity seen in distribution transformers. It also said new inquiries will be quoted at higher prices reflecting current raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin compression, and are price hikes being accepted?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower export mix in March (deferred shipments) changed the raw material ratio, and oil prices spiked in March. Price increase discussions are active with almost all customers; some have agreed and supply has resumed for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR80-90 crore lost Q4 sales be recovered in Q1, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipping has resumed and deferred transformers are going out. The FY27 target is INR800 crore, which management says it is confident of; Q1 will be a normal quarter, but no figure was given for the first half.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 guidance lowered from INR850-900 crore to INR800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is taking a conservative stance; INR800-850 crore is the expected range and INR900 crore is possible given past beats.

qa_highlights.question: Why did utilisation rise only about 2 points (77% to 79%) if demand is strong, and can 100% be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is on a dispatch basis; the Middle East shipment delay cost roughly 2-3 points, so 82-83% was possible otherwise. Management aims for 90-95%, not 100%; the analyst's implied-realisation math (about INR11 lakh per MVA) pointed to near-100% utilisation, which management called a thumb-rule estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the US and Middle East business is there, and what is the expected export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: US was 18-19% of FY26 revenue. Middle East was about 30% of FY25-26 revenue. The current order book is about 30-32% export.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have a hedging or price-escalation structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders are usually hedged by booking copper or aluminium on receipt. This time suppliers also demanded price increases, which management called force majeure. Some orders have PV escalation clauses; fixed-price orders are being renegotiated.

risks_watch: Customer price revisions: some fixed-price orders are unresolved, and margin recovery depends on how many customers accept.
Oil and commodity inflation (oil about +100%, other commodities +10-25%) could persist or reverse; management said it cannot predict this.
Middle East shipping normalisation and the ~INR35-40 crore of deferred March exports; April actuals were not disclosed.
Utilisation risk: FY26 dispatches were 79% of 7,500 MVA, and the FY27 volume target of 7,000 MVA needs strong execution.
Expansion execution (April 2027 commissioning) and 220 kV power transformer approvals, plus new capacity from peers.

Management blamed the Q4 miss on external factors it describes as temporary.

Both of these factors were temporary in nature and we expect Shilchar to resume its growth trajectory from the coming quarter.

531201|2026-06.headline: Shilchar Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 134.60 crore with EBITDA of Rs 29.23 crore and PAT of Rs 20.86 crore, hit by West Asia shipping costs and slow price pass-through.
531201|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 134.60 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 29.23 crore and PAT of Rs 20.86 crore. Management attributed the soft quarter to a sharp rise in container costs from the West Asia crisis, which delayed export dispatches, and to slow negotiations to pass on raw material price increases on domestic orders. Management said it lost roughly Rs 30-35 crore of potential revenue and that Q1 capacity utilisation was about 60-65%. It maintained FY27 guidance (Rs 800 crore revenue was referenced by an analyst, not reiterated as a number) and expects Q2 to be notably better than Q1, with Phase-3 expansion (6,500 MVA) due for commissioning in April 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Computed from EBITDA/revenue; management did not state it. Historical margin cited by analyst as about 30%

Over and above shipments made until the call date; about 70% domestic, 30% export

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export dispatches slowed as container costs rose three to five times for some geographies versus pre-crisis levels; management says customers are buying only minimum volumes, not cancelling. Export is about 90% of export orders on an ex-works basis per management, and the order book is about 30% export.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic dispatches were slowed by negotiations to pass on raw material price escalation on existing orders, with April and May the worst months and conditions easing since. Management says domestic market is normal versus last year and no lower-margin pressure in lower KV classes; order book is about 70% domestic.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annual outlook unchanged; management says it is on track for the top-line target and expects no problem achieving it, though geographic mix may shift if West Asia persists.

EBITDA: management does not expect problems achieving EBITDA as Q2 orders are at current raw material prices; expects Q2 EBITDA higher than Q1 but gave no margin percentage.

Phase-3 expansion (about 6,500 MVA) on track for commissioning in April 2027; new facility to drive growth from FY28; bigger-KV transformer orders expected later due to customer audits, approvals and type testing.
Margin normalisation depends on exports returning; if domestic-heavy mix persists, margins could dip slightly. New capacity to carry lower initial margins to build references.

Additional about 4.5 acres of land bought adjacent to existing Gavasad site for future expansion; product and KV class not yet disclosed.
Prototyping for larger transformers takes about 3-4 months after production starts; discussions under way with a few customers on bigger units.
Company will not supply state utility companies; plans to focus on exports once domestic references are established.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand in both export and domestic markets remains firm; customers are buying minimum volumes due to freight costs and uncertainty.
Export orders being deferred, not cancelled; management says delivery dates pushed by about 1-2 months (e.g., June to July or August).
Only 50-60% of raw material price rise passed on to customers for orders in hand from Q4 and Q1; current orders priced at current market prices.
Lead time for custom transformers is about 10-16 weeks; management says customers prefer Shilchar on quality, service and shorter lead time.
Management says competition is not the issue for exports: customers are not buying from rivals, just holding purchases.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Q1 revenue loss from shipment delays and whether FY27 Rs 800 crore guidance is being revisited.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to call it a loss but said Rs 30-35 crore could have been done without the crisis; it reiterated FY27 top-line target with no anticipated problem.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material cost increase was passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50-60% of the price rise was passed on for orders from Q4 and Q1; current execution is at market prices so EBITDA is not expected to be a problem.

qa_highlights.question: Order book size and domestic/export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book close to Rs 500 crore over and above shipments to date; about 70% domestic and 30% export; mostly for Q2, Q3 and some Q4, with Q2 fully booked.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins stay near 30% EBITDA, and will the 220 KV expansion be lower margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins can match prior years if exports recover; otherwise a slight dip. New 220 KV-class capacity will carry lower initial margins to build references, with better margins later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 export focus not shifted to domestic earlier, leaving capacity underused?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shipping was normal in April but costs spiked from late April/May; it shifted focus to domestic promptly, but custom orders take time to win and execute, benefits showing in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 capacity utilisation and export/domestic revenue split and receivable/inventory days?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was about 60-65%; export/domestic revenue split and inventory and receivable days were not disclosed on the call and will be sent by email.

531201|2026-09.headline: Shilchar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 43% QoQ to INR192.61 crore with EBITDA margin at 20.8%, while FY27 INR750 crore target is reiterated.
531201|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR192.61 crore, up 43% QoQ and 12% YoY, as deferred Q1 export dispatches landed and domestic demand stayed strong. EBITDA excluding other income was INR40.06 crore (20.8% margin, up from 16.4% in Q1) and PAT was INR32.98 crore (16.5% margin). Management reiterated the FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore, with H1 sales of about INR330 crore and an order book of over INR550 crore. Margins remain below the roughly 28-30% levels of FY24-FY26, and management shifted guidance to absolute EBITDA (INR200-250 crore) rather than percentage margin.

financial_highlights.metric: Net working capital increase in H1
financial_highlights.change: includes financial assets up to about INR29 crore, per analyst

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Export mix was about 40% in Q2 and the order book is about 60:40 domestic:export. Middle East shipments were still below normal, offset partly by North America, where US tariffs were withdrawn in February. Management said export margins are higher than domestic, but did not quantify.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic demand was described as very strong throughout. Mix is mainly renewable-related transformers, with distribution transformers made in very small quantities.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR750 crore reiterated; management said it will be more than that, and analysts were told quarterly run-rate of INR225-230 crore is needed.

Corporate sales fell 14% against a high base, exports fell 3%, general trade grew 8% and e-commerce grew 32%. 531266|2026-03.headline: VST Tillers FY26 revenue rose 25% to INR1,240 crore; Q4 revenue up 9% to INR328 crore, operational EBITDA margin 14.2%.
531266|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 25% year on year to about INR1,240 crore (transcript also cites INR1,248 crore), led by power tillers, which grew 35% to 50,332 units. Q4 revenue rose 9% to INR328 crore, with operational EBITDA margin of 14.2% versus 13.4% a year earlier, and operational PAT (excluding fair value gains/losses) up 36% to about INR39 crore. Management declined to guide FY27 growth, citing fuel and commodity inflation, a monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA, and fertiliser availability concerns; it said April and May demand was good and expects Q1 growth over the prior year. Price hikes were taken across tillers and tractors at the end of April.

segments.commentary: FY26 domestic volume 4,596 units, up 18.6%; Q4 domestic volume 1,244 units, up about 20%. Q4 tractor exports rose to 430 units from 260.

segments.commentary: FY26 volume 11,346 units vs 7,458 (about 52% growth); Q4 volume 2,947 units, up 27%. Front and rear rotary weeders launched in Q4.

segments.name: Power reapers
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 3,464 units, up 44%; seasonal, so minimal Q4 volume.

segments.name: Zetor / higher-HP tractors
segments.commentary: Single 8+2 variant (3.5 litre engine) currently; FY26 target is about 1,000 units; target 5,000-6,000 units by FY30. Sold through a few dealerships with month-on-month volume increases.

Fertiliser availability described as a likely problem, with no specific data; monsoon forecast at 92% of LPA.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number; it is tracking month by month and quarter by quarter, expects Q1 growth over the prior year, and targets 25% but said specifics are difficult to call given uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins be maintained with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance moved to a 12% to 14% operational EBITDA margin range, up from 11% to 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up plan for the Zetor brand and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about 1,000 Zetor units in FY27 and 5,000 to 6,000 by FY30, with more variants and a 4WD variant to come.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and the European business shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 export momentum was better; Netherlands-based operation to launch in June/July 2026 as planned, and management is confident of export growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory held at about 36 days; receivables cut from about 75 days to 51 days, with further reduction targeted over the next 2 to 3 years via the TOC supply chain model and SRM digitisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large investment balance be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Three areas: technology and products, global expansion (US re-entry with launch by end-2027), and inorganic opportunities in adjacencies; no specific deal announced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the electric tractor investment in Zimeno Inc (US)?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment already provisioned for; US subsidy removal and tariffs halted drivetrain exports. Expertise gained is being used to launch electric weeders and tillers first, with an all-India launch planned for early Q2 FY27.

531266|2026-06.headline: VST Tillers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR313.4 crores, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 45 bps to 12.85% on raw material inflation.
531266|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR313.4 crores from INR282.4 crores, and PAT rose to INR48.7 crores from INR44.6 crores. Operational EBITDA margin (excluding other income and fair value gains) was 12.85%, versus 13.3% a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to commodity and raw material inflation. Power tillers grew about 18% and power weeders about 56% in volume, while domestic tractors grew 4.5% and tractor exports were 275 units. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 outlook, saying it would be clearer in about a month, and said the July volume softness reflected a high base.

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA (excl. other income and fair value gain)

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Volume grew about 18% in Q1; management cites 16-20% tiller growth over recent quarters and expects 15-20% to continue. Bajaj Finance retail financing volume roughly doubled to about 1,000 units from about 400 a year earlier, but still only 8-9% of retail sales versus a 15-20% target.

segments.name: Power weeders (SFM)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 56% in Q1 and management has been clocking 50-60% growth for several quarters. Retail counters added more than 500 in three months, taking the network toward a target of about 2,000 counters by year-end, on top of 750-800 SFM dealers.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 4.5% in Q1 but supply lagged demand during ramp-up of the new variant, per management. Management expects Q2 growth, with substantial volume increases in Q3 and Q4; 40-50 HP is described as a crowded segment.

segments.name: Tractors (exports)
segments.commentary: 275 tractors sold in Q1. Europe: about 1,400-1,500 tractors per management, with entry into Turkey and the Nordics planned. Africa: 75 HP tractor shipments started. US expansion described as unclear.

segments.name: Reapers
segments.commentary: Seasonal product; volumes expected to pick up in Q2 with the harvest season. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 outlook given; management said it is too early and will comment in about a month, since H2 depends on monsoon and rabi sowing.
Management said demand outlook is positive through September, with the next 15-20 days critical for kharif crop survival.
Long-term target of about 20,000 tractors by FY30 (including 5,000-6,000 international units); revenue vision of INR3,000 crores by 2030.
More than 30 tractor variants planned over the next three years; three global platforms (A, B, C) to launch over 12-36 months.
Tractor dealer additions targeted at 50-60 in FY27, versus 40-50 last year.
capex_capacity: A new production facility will need investment in roughly the next two years, per the CEO.
Tiller-tractor hybrid product (geared, with differential) to roll out from the factory starting this month, with substantial volume in Q3 and Q4.
International distributor logistics infrastructure delayed from Q1 but expected operational in Q3.
Hydrostatic transmission tractor being seeded for export markets, not sold in India.
Bangalore land of about 19 acres; manufacturing already moved out, only administrative office remains; no monetisation decision yet.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand issue in tillers; July volumes declined YoY against a very high base.
Tractor 40-50 HP segment is crowded and highly competitive; company is acquiring market share through product breadth.
Commodity inflation (steel, forgings, castings, aluminium, copper), elevated and volatile natural rubber prices, and high crude and freight costs weighed on margins.

Emission norm: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026, which management says will not create a big cost increase for end customers. Stage 5 for all tractors in 2032 could add 25-30% to tractor technology cost today, though this may fall over time.
Possible 100% US tariff under a bill in Congress is a risk to US expansion plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tractor growth lagging the industry despite new launches, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 supply did not fully meet demand during the new-variant ramp-up; management expects Q2 growth and substantial increases in Q3-Q4. Strategy includes more than 30 variants over three years and state-by-state rollout of the FENTM series, starting with Gujarat, then Maharashtra.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the Bajaj Finance tie-up and other financing partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail financing reached about 1,000 units versus about 400 a year earlier, but only 8-9% of retail, against a 15-20% target. Other partners include Chola, TVS and nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is tiller export viable, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 300 units last year. A geared tiller with differential for Europe and India and an electric tiller/weeder are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any moderation in demand given July volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed July to a high base in tillers. It sees growth continuing at least through September, with tillers at 16-20% growth and weeders at 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation policy and non-core asset plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the policy is to maximise shareholder value and it expects to deploy capital over the next 18-24 months. No development on non-core assets yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the implications of upcoming emission norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026 is already ready. TREM 3A from April 2028 is covered. Full Stage 5 for tractors in 2032 may add 25-30% to technology cost at current prices.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression from raw material inflation; Q1 margin down about 45 bps YoY.
Tractor market share: domestic tractor growth of 4.5% trails the industry; July volumes were lower YoY.
Monsoon uncertainty over the next 15-20 days affects kharif output and rabi sowing.
Tariff risk to US expansion, and the possible 100% tariff bill in Congress.

rows.why: Fleet at 100% utilisation with signed contracts covering the full FY27 and new machines (EV units in Q2, wind units from October, Reliance Kutch demand from October) adding units, though no explicit FY27 volume growth % was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 100% with 98-99% floor management guides, and the UAE/KSA roadmap follows once client demand data is collected by next month-end, so further capex announcements are likely even though quantum is undisclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on demand and the order book covers FY27, but gave no explicit revenue or margin guidance numbers to raise and the INR 70-72 crore book looks small against the Q1 run-rate of INR 1,680 lakh.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Receivable days of ~200 (per analyst) against management's 60-70 day target, wind revenue depends on OEM output of 2-5 machines a month with ~5-month lead time, and management declined FY28 numbers; the disclosed figures were not reconciled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Electric machines ordered for two clients (~2-month lead time, expected Q2 FY27), 80-ton data-centre tower cranes live in 4-5 months, and 900-ton wind cranes from October, with revenue expected Q3-Q4 FY27.

rows.label: UAE and KSA entry
rows.why: Planned via new entities subject to approvals; KSA yields ~4% per month vs ~2.5% in India and KSA EBITDA margin expectation 50-52%, but no CapEx quantum or roadmap yet and KSA showed a six-month demand halt.

rows.label: Debtor days fall to 60-70
rows.why: Management says core receipts are under 60 days, but an analyst cited ~200 debtor days, so the target depends on next quarter's reported receivables reconciling.

rows.label: Borrowing cost falls as 9.75% loans are repaid
rows.why: Borrowings of ~INR 80-85 crore at ~8.5-8.75% average cost against legacy loans at 9.75%, and banks now fund ~100% of machine cost with LTV ~50-60%, which adds debt as capex continues.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, 100% utilisation, the INR 400 crore capex programme and the wind and UAE/KSA entries, but evasive on FY28 numbers, wind economics, UAE/KSA capex size and the receivables reconciliation; analysts pressed on the ~200 debtor-day figure.

531279|2026-09.headline: Trishakti Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 133% YoY to INR 1,551 lakhs, with EBITDA margin of 60.89%.
531279|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR 1,551 lakhs (up 133% YoY), EBITDA of INR 944 lakhs (up about 141%) and PAT of INR 519 lakhs (up 223%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 2,989 lakhs, EBITDA INR 1,790 lakhs and PAT INR 949 lakhs. Management said about INR 370 crore of the INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme (incl. GST) is deployed, and announced "Mission 2030" targeting cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30. Receivable days rose over the past two years; management attributed this to a family settlement and said the cycle will normalise to about 60-65 days by year end.

financial_highlights.metric: Total H1 revenue incl. other income (per Q&A)
Gross block deployed vs FY25-27 programme (per Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: Approx INR 370 crore of INR 400 crore

segments.name: Crane and equipment rental (only segment discussed)
segments.commentary: Fleet includes rough terrain, all terrain, crawler, truck-mounted cranes, AWPs and 70-80m man lifts; management says fleet utilisation has been about 100% for three years. Management claims current ARR is about INR 78 crore after INR 40 crore of machines added in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 60-65 crore retained; management said it expects to surpass this, with an executable order book of about INR 78 crore and core revenue from operations above INR 75 crore.
Mission 2030: cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30, possibly by FY29 if demand holds; peak revenue of around INR 300 crore cited.
Net debt expected at INR 400-500 crore until FY30; debt-to-equity to stay under 2 for the next 1-1.5 years; deleveraging expected after FY28.
Gross block expected to exceed INR 400 crore by FY27 year end, with INR 90-95 crore (ex-GST) in CWIP to be deployed in Q3 and about INR 125 crore of wind energy capex to arrive from early November.
ARR expected to reach about INR 120 crore from December 2026 to FY28 Q3 as CWIP machines deploy.
UAE and KSA expansion deferred until balance sheet deleverages; paperwork said to be 60-70% complete.
capex_capacity: INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme: about INR 370 crore deployed (incl. GST), more than 90% complete and ahead of schedule by about six months.
CWIP of about INR 77-78 crore ex-GST (INR 95 crore incl. GST) yet to be deployed in Q3 FY27; contracts reportedly already won for these machines.

Wind energy fleet expansion of about INR 125 crore; machines to arrive from early November; OEMs can supply only 4-5 machines per month in India; management targets replacing 250-300 machines as wind turbines shift from 3.3 to 5.2 MW.

Mission 2030 implies about INR 600-700 crore of incremental capex over three years (about 2.5% of net debt repaid monthly per management); 80-ton tower cranes for data centre work in transit, expected October-November.
Two 70-80m man lifts in fleet; management says about 20-22 such machines exist in India.
demand_pricing: Management says it receives RFQs daily as a central vendor to L&T, Reliance, Tata Steel and others; capex is concentrated in Gujarat and Odisha.
Management says crawler cranes above 150 tonnes are in strong demand; lower-tonnage truck-mounted cranes (80-100 t) are also in demand.
Fleet utilisation about 100% versus an industry figure of about 80% cited in the presentation; management attributes this to 11-12 month contracts versus competitors' 3-4 month contracts.

Management said rental yields are stable and not expected to rise; machine pricing in India is fixed by rental yields. Double-shift operation on 15-20% of machines is said to add about 50% revenue on those machines.
Management said a data centre tower crane generates much higher yield, and specialised 70-80m man lifts earn more than two times current fleet monthly revenue per machine.

qa_highlights.question: Why have debtor days risen over two years, and what is the plan to fix it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a family settlement from three years ago that extended the cycle; about INR 75 lakh of provision was created this quarter and the cycle should return to about 60-65 days by year end. Management also said about INR 3 crore is over one year old, linked to the family settlement.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects net debt of INR 400-500 crore until FY30, funded by bank debt and internal accruals; most FY24-FY25 machines to be free of bank financing by FY28. Only fixed-rate loans apart from the CC limit, which was unused since January; 25 bps rate increase expected on new funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on equity dilution and UAE/KSA expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is the first priority and equity dilution is a final option; it could double the fleet by next year if debt is hard to raise. UAE and KSA expansion depends on internal accruals or equity; KSA local-stake rules reportedly changed after 1 May, allowing 100% ownership.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance INR 60-65 crore or INR 70-80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance has always been INR 60-65 crore, and that INR 72 crore is only the current ARR; H1 revenue from operations was about INR 30 crore and it expects to beat guidance given the order book and H2 seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why are yields not improving with the new fleet, and is sustainability at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields are fixed and not expected to rise, but are sustainable; it cited three years of OEM free-of-cost servicing that defers opex, and buying power giving 5-10% machine discount versus competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the receivable cycle elevated, and what caused the move in other current liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end revenue is not billed for 10-12 days because overtime is computed, so trade receivables run high; the move to monthly GST filing shifted about INR 2.5-3 crore of billing, and cash flow should improve from this quarter. Other current liabilities relate to machine funding timing.

risks_watch: Receivable days remain elevated; management promises normalisation to about 60-65 days by Q4 FY27, with the annual report providing clarity.
Mission 2030 assumes fleet utilisation above 90% through FY30; management acknowledged this may be bold.
Debt-to-equity to remain under 2 for 1-1.5 years; net debt of INR 450-500 crore at peak, and possible equity dilution if debt funding is constrained.
Customer concentration in Gujarat and Odisha capex cycle; no soft commitments from customers for expansion, per management.
Machine import dependence above 250 tonnes and rising global machine costs; yields not expected to rise.
Gross block and revenue timing depend on delivery of wind energy and tower crane machines, now in transit.
531279|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, utilisation and Mission 2030, but cautious on near-term balance sheet: management repeatedly deferred UAE/KSA expansion and equity dilution decisions. Answers on receivables and FY27 revenue guidance were somewhat repetitive, and some answers on yields and imported machine pricing were unclear.
key_quotes: Mission 2030 is not simply about owning more machines. It is about building a stronger Trishakti with greater capabilities, deeper customer relationships, and a larger role in India's infrastructure growth story.
We have already won contracts for all these INR 95 crores worth of machines.
Our guiding principle is simple. We want to grow with India, build for the long-term, and turn our ambition into measurable execution.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin was 60.89% and management says rental yields are stable and not expected to rise, while double-shift operation on 15-20% of machines adds about 50% revenue on those machines; the margin gain depends on mix and utilisation rather than price.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About INR 370 crore of the INR 400 crore FY25-27 programme is already deployed (over 90% complete), with INR 90-95 crore ex-GST CWIP machines due for deployment in Q3 and about INR 125 crore of wind energy capex arriving from early November.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fleet utilisation is about 100% and ARR is expected to reach about INR 120 crore from December 2026 to FY28 Q3 as CWIP machines deploy, against current ARR of about INR 72-78 crore, with the order book at about INR 78 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 100% for three years against an industry figure of about 80%, and Mission 2030 implies about INR 600-700 crore of incremental capex over three years, so further capex is guided with a plan behind it.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects to surpass the INR 60-65 crore FY27 guidance, citing the INR 78 crore order book, current ARR of about INR 72-78 crore and H2 seasonality, after H1 revenue of INR 2,989 lakh.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR 2,989 lakh is about half of the INR 60-65 crore guidance, the executable order book is about INR 78 crore, and management expects to surpass guidance; the main watch item is receivable days, which management says normalise to 60-65 days by year end.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 80-ton tower cranes for data centre work are in transit for October-November, and wind energy and crawler fleet additions of about INR 125 crore plus INR 90-95 crore CWIP arrive in Q3, with management citing 150-tonne+ crawler demand.

rows.label: Net debt capped at INR 400-500 crore until FY30; deleveraging after FY28
rows.why: Net debt is guided at INR 400-500 crore until FY30 and debt-to-equity under 2 for 1-1.5 years, with most FY24-25 machines free of bank financing by FY28, but Mission 2030 capex of about INR 600-700 crore keeps leverage high.

rows.label: Receivable days normalise to 60-65 by year end
rows.why: Management blames a family settlement and about INR 75 lakh provision this quarter, says about INR 3 crore is over one year old, and expects cycle normalisation, but this is not yet visible in the numbers.

rows.label: UAE and KSA expansion deferred
rows.why: Management deferred UAE and KSA expansion until deleveraging, with paperwork 60-70% complete and funding dependent on internal accruals or equity.

tone.note: Management was confident on utilisation (about 100%), order book and Mission 2030, but cautious on balance sheet, deferring UAE/KSA expansion and equity dilution; analysts pressed on receivable days, FY27 guidance versus ARR and yield sustainability, and some answers were repetitive or unclear.

531335|2026-03.headline: Zydus Wellness Q4 FY26 net sales grew 62.1% on Comfort Click, but net profit fell 5.8% as seasonal brands dropped 9.8% in the domestic business.
531335|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales rose 62.1% YoY, driven by the Comfort Click acquisition, with international like-to-like growth of 31.4% and domestic growth of only 1.7%. Domestic seasonal brands fell 9.8% as a delayed summer and rain in March and mid-April left retail and wholesale pipelines unfilled, while skin and hair care rose 39.7% and food and nutrition rose 9.4%. EBITDA grew 42.2% to INR 2,701 million, but net profit fell 5.8% due to higher finance costs from the acquisition debt, higher amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items. Management said operating leverage and the 17-18% EBITDA margin goal remain intact, while the seasonal recovery is expected from May onwards.

financial_highlights.metric: International incl. Comfort Click like-to-like growth (Q4)

financial_highlights.change: Seasonal -9.8%, skin and hair care +39.7%, food and nutrition +9.4%
Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +17%
Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +2.3%

segments.name: Seasonal brands (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 declined 9.8% and FY26 declined 18.8%; management attributed it to a delayed summer, March/April rains in the East and North, and missed retailer pipeline build. Seasonal carries above-average gross margin and EBITDA, so its weakness diluted the mix.

segments.name: Skin and hair care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 39.7% and FY26 grew 21.9%. Everyuth grew at strong double digits in FY26 and Cuticolor has been in the portfolio for about six months, sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce.

segments.name: Food and nutrition (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 9.4% and FY26 grew 15.5%. RiteBite Max Protein grew at roughly 50% in FY26 (about INR 244 crore per analyst), and management said actual branded growth is higher than reported due to contract manufacturing optimization.

segments.name: International incl. Comfort Click
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth of 31.4% in Q4 and 29.5% in FY26. Comfort Click has been held for seven months; it is EPS accretive on a standalone basis in Q4, and the total-to-constant-currency gap is about 3%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a recovery in seasonal brands from May onwards, and hopes some early-season misses can be recovered if summer progresses normally; it declined to forecast the full season.
Seasonal brands are expected to deliver consistent double-digit growth over three to four years, per management.
EBITDA margin aspiration of 17-18% reiterated for the next couple of years, measured excluding Comfort Click.
Comfort Click EPS accretive from Q4; management maintained its earlier guidance for the next two years.
Tax rate: FY26-27 is a mix of cash tax and deferred tax asset utilisation; FY27-28 is expected at about 25%, and FY28 at full cash tax.
Operating leverage expected to play out across the business excluding Comfort Click, which has largely variable spend.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.

Launch activity in Q4: Max Protein Ultimate RTD, Max Protein Roots Ghee Jaggery Bar and Korean flavour chips; Sugar Free D'lite Choco Spread; Everyuth Tan Removal Face Wash; Glucon-D Recharge (liquid and sachets); seven Comfort Click launches across WeightWorld and Animigo.
Complan NutriGro was relaunched and moved to direct supply in the kids segment; VieMax by Complan launched in adult nutrition.
Channel expansion: Boots.com (UK) for WeightWorld and MaxMedix; Amazon UAE for vitamins and supplements.
Management said no divestments are planned, and capital allocation across brands is considered appropriate.
demand_pricing: Rural demand recovery continued to outpace the gradual urban improvement; quick commerce and e-commerce growth remained strong.
Quick commerce is about 7-8% of total domestic business; e-commerce is about 44-45% of organized trade.
Sugar Free Green reported its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; sweetener market share rose 24 bps (MAT March 2026); Nutralite grew at double digits despite gas supply headwinds.
Management said supply disruption from the Middle East conflict has been limited, affecting only a very small part of the business.
Gross margins were in line with plan; management cited brand-level margin improvements and exits from low-margin products.

qa_highlights.question: What weighed on seasonal growth and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak North and East markets, March/April rains, and a missing retailer pipeline build ahead of summer. It expects a recovery from May onwards but declined to forecast the season.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be expected to move toward the 17-18% aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins are in line with plan and the miss was driven by mix from weak seasonal sales. Umesh Parikh said operating leverage will play out across the business excluding Comfort Click.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce changing the innovation and channel approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said the portfolio is designed for quick commerce consumers while keeping the traditional channel SKUs. Quick commerce is about 7-8% of domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Comfort Click margin trajectory and is it EPS accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Umesh Parikh said Comfort Click is in line with or slightly ahead of expectations, and it became EPS accretive in Q4. The currency tailwind is about 3%, the gap between reported and constant-currency growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company divest slow-growing categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said there are no plans to divest any category and no major change in capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cuticolor gaining traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Cuticolor is positioned as a derma-backed, Korean-origin safe hair colour sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce, with repeat buying and early traction, after about six months in the portfolio.

risks_watch: Seasonal recovery depends on May-June temperatures and rainfall; a further weak season would hit the margin mix and FY27 growth.
Domestic growth was only 1.7% in Q4 and 2.4% in FY26, with the seasonal decline masking growth in the rest of the portfolio.
Net profit fell 5.8% in Q4 and 43.2% in FY26 despite EBITDA growth, as finance costs, amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items rose. Watch the tax mix in FY27.
Comfort Click's growth depends on European online VMS demand, FX (GBP/EUR) and the supply chain; the US and UAE are early-stage bets.
Watch whether the 17-18% EBITDA margin target is reached without Comfort Click, given that management gave no new timeline.
Management declined to disclose RiteBite and Nutralite brand-level growth and category data, and geographic segment disclosure is still under consideration.
531335|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long term and on Comfort Click and RiteBite, but defensive on the near term: it attributed the seasonal miss to external weather and channel timing and gave no new margin timeline. Management avoided quantifying several questions, including brand-level growth, Comfort Click EBITDA and the timing of the margin target.
key_quotes: So our margins at a gross margin level has actually in line with what we have planned.
It's not about that we have to clean up every time. It is just that the pipeline buildup, which is in anticipation of summers, as the summer kick in, they start buying in advance.
So I think if we segment the portfolio, this concern remains. But now if you look at the new portfolio and as the expanded portfolio, the saliency of this business has reduced.
I think there are no new numbers. We've talked about in the next couple of years, we hope to get to our 17-18.

rows.why: Management expects seasonal recovery from May, but declined to forecast the season; domestic growth was only 1.7% in Q4 and 2.4% in FY26, while skin and hair care grew 39.7% in Q4 and food and nutrition 9.4%.

rows.why: Management declined to forecast the full seasonal season and expects only to recover some early-season misses if summer progresses normally; the call gives no basis for a raise.

rows.when: Q4 FY26 launches already done; further rollout over next 2-4
rows.why: Launches already under way include Max Protein Ultimate RTD, Max Protein Roots Ghee Jaggery Bar, Korean flavour chips, Sugar Free D'lite Choco Spread, Everyuth Tan Removal Face Wash, Glucon-D Recharge, seven Comfort Click launches, and VieMax by Complan.

rows.label: Channel expansion: Boots.com (UK) and Amazon UAE
rows.why: Boots.com (UK) listing for WeightWorld and MaxMedix and Amazon UAE for vitamins and supplements are live channel expansions, though management called the US and UAE early-stage bets.

rows.label: Seasonal brands double-digit growth over 3-4 years
rows.why: Management expects consistent double-digit growth in seasonal brands over three to four years, but FY26 seasonal declined 18.8% and Q4 fell 9.8%, so near-term recovery is unproven.

rows.when: FY27-28; FY27 mix of cash tax and deferred tax asset
rows.why: Management guided FY27-28 at about 25% and FY28 at full cash tax, so the FY27 tax mix will affect reported profit growth against the 43.2% FY26 net profit decline.

tone.note: Management was confident on Comfort Click (EPS accretive in Q4, international LFL +31.4%) and RiteBite, but defensive on the seasonal miss, blaming weather and channel timing and giving no new margin timeline; analysts pushed on margin path to 17-18% and seasonal recovery.

531335|2026-06.headline: Zydus Wellness Q1 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million, while reported net profit fell 7%.
531335|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, helped by the Comfort Click consolidation, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million and EBITDA margin up about 0.4% on a like-to-like basis. Reported net profit declined 7%, but profit excluding amortisation of acquired brands grew 26.5%. The domestic business grew 4.6%, with Skin & Hair Care up 34.5% and Food & Nutrition up 16%, while seasonal brands fell 12% due to unseasonal rains in the East and North. International (including Comfort Click) grew 24.8% like-to-like, and management said the summer weakness was recovering in the second half of the quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: Net profit excluding amortisation of acquired brands
International business (incl. Comfort Click) like-to-like growth
A&P as % of total sales (reported, incl. Comfort Click)
financial_highlights.change: Core like-for-like described as similar to last year

segments.name: Skin and Hair Care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Grew 34.5% in the quarter. Everyuth delivered strong double-digit growth, with its facial cleansing rank improving from fifth to fourth and tan removal ahead of internal expectations.

segments.name: Food and Nutrition (domestic)
segments.commentary: Grew 16%. Complan grew faster than the prior quarter despite category degrowth; RiteBite Max Protein grew more than double its historical rate; Nutralite delivered strong growth.

segments.name: Seasonal brands (domestic)
segments.commentary: Declined 12% on a softer summer. Nycil was hit hardest by North and East rains and retailer inventory; Glucon-D was flattish as East offset gains elsewhere.

segments.name: International incl. Comfort Click
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth of 24.8%. Comfort Click carries much higher margins and is EPS accretive; launched WeightWorld D2C in the US, Walmart marketplace, and noon UAE with a physical UAE base.

guidance_outlook: International growth: management said it will maintain its 'double-digit' framing and declined to give forward-looking numbers.
Comfort Click: management expects continued EPS accretion and margin improvement if the current momentum holds, despite the seasonally weak September and December quarters.
Effective tax rate: Q1 ETR near 27% due to UK thin-cap disallowances (about 25% underlying). For FY27, about 12-15 points of the 25% are cash; from FY28 the full 25% is expected to be cash.
Finance cost: lower after switching the GBP loan to a euro loan at a much lower rate; the run-rate is expected to hold unless euro benchmark rates move significantly.
Seasonal brands: management expects a positive trajectory for the rest of the year; trade inventory is said to be no higher than last year and the product shelf life is three years.
capex_capacity: Comfort Click costs: an analyst cited about INR 80-85 crore a quarter of interest and depreciation, which management did not dispute.

New launches: Complan Power Play RTD milkshake (vanilla and chocolate, no added sugar), VieMax Diabetes Care, and additional RiteBite Max Protein range (millet wafer bar, Roots, Korean chips, RTDs, cookies).
Comfort Click support and service teams remain in India even as operations expand into the US and Middle East.
Management said more launches are coming in the next few quarters, with a long-term pipeline described as robust for two to three years.
demand_pricing: Consumer demand held up, with spending shifting towards premium products; quick commerce and e-commerce remain the primary growth engines with strong double-digit growth.
Pricing discipline, mix improvement and premium offerings offset input cost volatility, which management described as manageable.
Core gross margin expansion stayed strong, with additional margin support from Comfort Click.
Geopolitical disruption: management said the company's impact was limited to mitigation measures.
Nycil faced channel destocking and slower uptake because of high retailer inventory from the prior year; management said it expects a more positive finish to the year.

qa_highlights.question: Was international growth constrained by stock availability or supply chain issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no specific constraints; 25% is a good growth rate, but it will keep guiding to double-digit growth and does not give forward-looking numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effective tax rate outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ETR was near 27% (about 25% underlying, distorted by UK thin-cap disallowances). For FY27, 12-15 points of the 25% are cash; from FY28 it is expected to be fully cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: The GBP loan was refinanced into a euro loan at a much lower rate; the finance cost run-rate should hold unless the euro benchmark moves materially.

qa_highlights.question: What was the 12% seasonal decline by geography?
qa_highlights.answer: East (continuous April-May rain) and North were the main drags. Glucon-D's gains in North, West and South were offset by East. Nycil was hit by North and East plus retailer stock. Growth recovered in the second half of the quarter but not enough to offset the full-quarter drag.

qa_highlights.question: Will Comfort Click be EBITDA-positive in the seasonally weak September and December quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Comfort Click has been EPS accretive since Q4 FY26 and expects net margin, EBITDA and PBT to rise if momentum continues. Comfort Click's US presence is 'very small' but growing well and is too early to judge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Complan's growth despite category degrowth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from the core kids segment (better nutrition, advertising, distribution), celebrity endorsement, toddler (NutriGro), adult nutrition (VieMax, VieMax Diabetes Care) and RTD entry (Complan Power Play). Kids nutrition is the core driver.

qa_highlights.question: What were A&P spends and digital mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported A&P was 18.2% of total sales, including Comfort Click, which spends heavily on advertising. Like-for-like core A&P was similar to last year. Digital's share of spend is rising.

risks_watch: Seasonal brands: Nycil and Glucon-D weakness in East and North, with retailer inventory from last year still weighing; management expects a more positive finish but the full-year recovery is not yet proven.
Comfort Click profitability in seasonally weak September and December quarters, given about INR 80-85 crore a quarter of interest and depreciation (analyst estimate, not disputed by management).
Tax: Q1 ETR near 27% from UK thin-cap disallowances; FY27 cash tax covers only about 12-15 of the 25 points, with full cash tax expected from FY28.

Finance cost: run-rate depends on euro benchmark rates after the GBP-to-euro loan switch.
Reported net profit fell 7% in Q1 even as EBITDA rose 55.3%; the gap is attributed to amortisation of acquired brands.
key_quotes: 25% is a good growth. We've been talking about our double-digit growth.
We normally don't give a forward-looking. We just said double digits, so that's what we will maintain.

531344|2026-03.headline: CONCOR posted record FY26 throughput of 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), but PAT fell 4.5% and Q4 domestic EBIT margin collapsed to 0.2%.

531358|2026-06.headline: Choice International Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs. 319 crore, with PAT of Rs. 61 crore (up 26% YoY).

Management described the quarter as a steady start, with broking at 59% of revenue, advisory at 28% and NBFC at 13%. Management said Rs. 900 crore from NH Investment & Securities into Choice Equity Broking is expected in Q2 FY27, with growth from it expected from Q3. Analysts pressed on the flat sequential run-rate over the last three quarters, and management's answers on timing and quantification were largely qualitative.

+26.37% YoY; analyst noted PAT declined QoQ

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs. 45 crore; loan book Rs. 836 crore; focus on secured MSME, microlap and rooftop solar lending; GNPA 3.78%, NNPA 2.74%, NIM 11.10%.

qa_highlights.question: What return or ROCE is targeted on the incremental NH capital?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the NNPA improvement came from recoveries versus upgrades?

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental NBFC lending secured and how is credit quality protected?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the NBFC segment still running given its low returns?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 100-branch opening target on track?
