531358|2026-09.headline: Choice International Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to Rs 379 crore and PAT rose 23% to Rs 69-70 crore, a record quarter.
531358|2026-09.overview: Management reported record consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 379 crore (up 33% YoY from Rs 284 crore), EBITDA of about Rs 131 crore (34.5% margin) and PAT of about Rs 70 crore (18.3% margin, up 23%). Broking and distribution and advisory each contributed roughly half of revenue, with NBFC at about 12%. The company completed a Rs 900 crore NH Investment & Securities investment in the broking arm via CCPS, announced a 1:1 bonus issue, and moved the Feedback Infra acquisition forward with a Letter of Intent from the Resolution Professional. Management flagged regulatory risk to insurance commissions and NBFC funding costs after the repo hike. Note that the call cites PAT as Rs 69 crore in one place and about Rs 70 crore in another.

segments.name: Broking and distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 178 crore and PBT about Rs 42 crore; 218 branches, client assets and custody Rs 66,300 crore, ADTO down 12% QoQ in line with market. MTF book Rs 463 crore. Wealth AUM about Rs 6,000 crore (MF Rs 4,100 crore, PMS/AIF Rs 291 crore).

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 145 crore and PBT about Rs 45 crore, supported by five mainboard and SME IPOs (about Rs 680 crore issue size). Government advisory order book Rs 710 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 46 crore and PBT about Rs 4 crore; total loan book Rs 935 crore. Margins hit by microfinance stress over recent quarters, per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects roughly 20% ROE and aims to maintain it.
Customer growth of about 30-40% in tier 3 and beyond geographies; MTF-led activity expected to add about 10 percentage points to overall growth rate.
Pipeline of 24 IPO mandates with estimated fundraise of Rs 6,210 crore; at least four to five IPOs expected in H2 FY27.

Feedback Infra expected to become part of Choice in about the next quarter, subject to NCLT approval; existing order book Rs 300 crore-plus, with about Rs 200 crore-plus of order book to be added post acquisition.
FY30 target advisory mix of roughly 50:50 between government advisory and investment banking.
H2 priorities: StrikeX adoption, new digital products, MTF expansion using NH capital, NCD and fixed income distribution, AMC active schemes.

MTF book Rs 463 crore; management says deployment of the NH money began after 27 October and expects it to be deployed in the current quarter.
Feedback Infra acquisition pending NCLT approval; Letter of Intent received from Resolution Professional after Committee of Creditors approval.
Choice Large and Midcap Fund (first actively managed AMC scheme) NFO closed on the day of the call; collection figures to be shared shortly.
demand_pricing: Product distribution (structured and fixed income) reached Rs 1,636 crore in H1 FY27 versus Rs 512 crore a year earlier and above full-year FY26 volume of Rs 745 crore.
IPO fees generally 3% to 8-9% of issue size depending on sector and company; management sees no major margin pressure.
Wealth AUM yield of about 60-75 bps; management says regulators are unlikely to cut commissions materially.
Insurance: proposed commission and distribution-expense changes could pressure intermediary revenue, depending on final framework and product mix.
Market context: MTF industry book moderated from about Rs 1.6 lakh crore to Rs 1.5 lakh crore by October end; RBI repo rose from 5.25% to 5.50% in October.
India Post Payments Bank pilot: over 25,000 customers and AUM of about Rs 1.12 crore in roughly 38 days; revenue impact too early to assess.

qa_highlights.question: Demat accounts are up 14% but active accounts are flat; what is holding back activation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dormant accounts are a result of the NSE 12-month active UCC rule, and a dedicated team is working on reactivation through portfolio alerts and research reports.

qa_highlights.question: How do CBA-sourced revenues compare with direct digital clients in payout and scale?
qa_highlights.answer: CBAs are treated as branch originators, and payouts range from 15% to 40% depending on product; CBA and branch revenue cannot be separated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and impact of the Feedback Infra acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Resolution plan approved by CoC; NCLT hearing pending. Management expects margin improvement from larger projects and about Rs 200 crore-plus of order book to be added after acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Why focus on tier 3 and beyond cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited under-penetration, higher lifetime customer value from physical distribution, and a 30-40% customer growth target in these geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IPO fee and H2 IPO pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Fees range from 3% to 8-9%; management did not disclose SEBI observation status and expects at least four to five IPOs in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What are the terms and timeline for NH's CCPS conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Conversion is about three years away and the ratio is not yet fixed, pending conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 146 crore advisory revenue sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said advisory revenue depends on the number of IPOs during the quarter, and government consulting remains at about Rs 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 MTF income exceed Rs 100 crore given the NH capital deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MTF revenue will be added as the book grows and expects deployment in the current quarter; no explicit Q3 number was given.

rows.why: Resolution plan approved by CoC and LoI received; existing order book is Rs 300 crore-plus and about Rs 200 crore-plus is to be added post acquisition, with NCLT hearing still pending.

531400|2026-09.headline: Almondz Global Securities Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.9% YoY to INR40.09 crore, with profit up 2.4x to INR9.13 crore.
531400|2026-09.overview: Management reported consolidated revenue of INR40.09 crore (up 17.9% YoY) and profit of INR9.13 crore (2.4x), with margin at 22.8%. Premier Green (green fuel JV, 41% stake) drove growth, with Himachal running at 285 KLPD and Odisha plant fully operational. Infra consulting revenue rose 21.1% to INR31.35 crore, while financial services revenue grew 2.7% to INR8.05 crore but profit fell on weak capital markets and lower mark-to-market gains. Management is pursuing a demerger of the infra consulting business, with a second demerger of Premier Green planned afterwards.

segments.name: Infra engineering consulting (Almondz Global Infra Consulting)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR31.35 crore (+21.1%) and profit INR2.90 crore (+19.8%) on higher DPR revenue. H1 order inflow INR154 crore, versus INR72 crore in H1 last year; total order book above INR400 crore to execute over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Green fuel (Premier Green Innovations, 41% stake)
segments.commentary: Himachal unit ran at full 285 KLPD; quarterly revenue INR202.24 crore and profit INR12.59 crore. Odisha 200 KLPD plant is operational and produced 71 lakh litres in its initial phase; full OMC supply expected from third week of November.

segments.name: Financial services (broking, merchant banking, investment banking, wealth)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8.05 crore (+2.7%) and profit INR2.51 crore, lower due to weak capital markets and reduced mark-to-market gains from last quarter. Wealth management AUM about INR1,500 crore, concentrated in 20-25 family offices.

guidance_outlook: Premier Green: ~INR1,000 crore revenue expected this year (FY27), versus INR700 crore in FY26; ~INR1,400 crore targeted next year, with ~INR800 crore from Himachal and ~INR600 crore from Odisha.
Premier Green capacity utilisation: targeting 80% in Q3 and 100% in Q4 of the 485 KLPD total capacity; 12.80 crore litres of ethanol allocated from Himachal and Odisha.
Infra consulting: revenue expected about INR160 crore this year (versus INR131 crore last year), with at least 25% growth next year.
Financial services: 20-25% revenue growth expected this year versus INR61 crore last year, with similar growth next year; management expects significant fee growth in Q4 FY27.
Management says all three businesses should grow at least 25% YoY over the next five years and expects to remain confident about H2.

Second demerger of Premier Green proposed after the first; ratio to be set on valuation at that time. Infra business is investing in technology-led automation.
demand_pricing: Infra: largest ever sole bid INR33 crore program management consultancy mandate from Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation; DPR for 422 km NaMo Expressway (Odisha); authority engineer role for Itarsi-Nagpur 3rd line (Central Railway); first Uttar Pradesh State Bridge Corporation project; first overseas assignment in Zambia; PPP Centre of Philippines empanelment.
Premier Green: OMC allocations finalised for FY27; orders released by oil marketing companies only the day before the call.

Financial services focus on small-cap growth companies with expected valuations of INR100-500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline and the 5-year growth expectation for each listed business?
qa_highlights.answer: NSE approval expected any time; SEBI and NCLT filings follow, with 6-9 months to listing. Management expects each of the three businesses to grow at least 25% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How is the capital markets business positioned amid market volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the private placement pipeline targets small-cap growth companies on five-year advisory relationships; about 4 mandates closed in last 2 years and about 5 in execution. The investment book is split equally between debt and equity; private equity exposure is split equally between listed and unlisted stocks.

qa_highlights.question: How will broking and wealth management be scaled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says broking and wealth growth comes through the investment banking book; wealth AUM is about INR1,500 crore, mostly from 20-25 family offices, with 25-30% annual AUM addition. Management does not see it as a retail broker. A shareholder requested AUM and new client disclosure; management agreed to implement.

qa_highlights.question: Which company is growing fastest and how will the structure look post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Premier Green is the fastest-growing, with ~INR1,000 crore expected this year. Post-demerger, AGSL keeps a 40% stake in Premier Green, with its profit share added to the bottom line; financial services is expected to grow 25-30% next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Avonmore holding structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Avonmore Holdings is an NBFC and promoter company; it owns 51% of AGSL, 40% of Almondz Infra Consultancy and 11% of Premier Green. A 100% subsidiary, Almondz Finance, is being merged into Avonmore, with one licence to be surrendered.

531431|2026-06.headline: Shakti Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37.9% YoY to INR859 crores, but EBITDA margin stayed near 9.6% on raw material and realisation pressure.
531431|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly revenue of INR859 crores (up 37.9% YoY from INR623 crores) and PAT of INR52 crores, up 35% QoQ, with PAT margin at 6% versus 4.5% in Q4 FY26. EBITDA margin was about 9.6%, which management said was broadly stable sequentially, while YoY EBITDA fell from INR144 crores to INR83 crores due to raw material inflation (about INR36 crores) and lower sales realisation (about INR25 crores). Solar pump installations rose 57.6% YoY to 27,678 units, and the order book was about INR1,000 crores as of 22 July 2026. Management reiterated a target of INR5,000 crores revenue by FY29 and tied margin recovery to PM-KUSUM 2.0 launch and easing raw material prices.

rows.why: Portable liquid vaporiser (patent applied), SHOR rechargeable with animal alarm and Xtrabright were launched in Q2; management targets Mosquito portfolio above INR 100 crore by end FY29.

rows.label: Debt-free within about 2 years
rows.why: Net debt INR 153 crore at September before INR 90 crore Noida plot proceeds in October; CFO says no major capex is planned and the company should be debt-free in about 2 years, possibly sooner.

rows.label: EPR dry cell clarity and subsidy decision
rows.why: EPR compliance deadline extended to 30 November and clarity expected by Q3, with financial impact not yet provided; Jammu NCSS subsidy (INR 20-25 crore a year if approved) not yet granted.

rows.label: Medium-term CAGR disclosure
rows.why: Battery, non-battery and new-category CAGR projections are to be shared around February-March 2027; management declined a multi-year CAGR on this call.

tone.note: Management was confident on alkaline, rechargeables and the Mosquito portfolio, but cautious on H2 margins as zinc hardens; analysts pressed on margin recovery, EPR, Jammu subsidy and multi-year growth, which management largely deferred to Feb-Mar 2027.

531548|2026-03.headline: Somany Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin rose to 11.4% and FY26 to 9.3%; management guides at least 150 bps more margin improvement in FY27 despite gas-price shock.
531548|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales grew about 6% and FY26 about 5%, with EBITDA margin up in both periods (11.4% in Q4, 9.3% for FY26). Capacity utilisation was broadly flat at about 79% for the year, rising to 82% in Q4, and Somany Max reached near breakeven versus a loss of about INR 9 crore in Q4 FY25. Gas prices jumped from about 9 March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation, and Morbi capacity was disrupted, which management sees as a share-gain opportunity for organised players. Working capital improved sharply, with receivable days at 40 (from 51) and working capital lower by 4 days to 9 days. Management passed through about 16-17% tile price hikes and about 8% bathware and sanitaryware hikes, and said input cost increases are being fully recovered in retail but only about 85-90% in projects.

segments.name: Tiles
segments.commentary: GVT volumes up 3% while ceramic and PVT volumes fell 3%; average tile price increase of about 16-17% since March 2026. Company-wide utilisation around 79% for the year.

segments.name: Sanitaryware and bathware
segments.commentary: Sanitaryware grew 8% in FY26 to INR 320 crore; management targets double-digit growth in FY27. Bathware price hike of about 18% taken in February on brass costs, and a blended 8% hike in April. Only 25% of dealers currently stock sanitaryware.

segments.name: Adhesives
segments.commentary: Management expects healthy double-digit volume growth in FY27 for sanitaryware and adhesives combined; no separate adhesive figures were given.

segments.name: Outsourced / JV production
segments.commentary: Outsourced sales about 35-36% of volume after Acer and Amora moved from JV to outsourced status (about 30% excluding those). Total FY26 sales volume about 72 million sq m; capacity about 75 million sq m.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin to improve by at least 150 bps from the 9.3% FY26 base, to about 10.5-11% or better; management reiterated 10.8% or better when asked.
FY27 volume growth guided to decent single digits for tiles and double digits for sanitaryware and adhesives.
FY27 revenue growth of about 20-25% if current prices hold, per management, which would be driven by about 15% price hikes plus high single-digit volume growth; value outcome depends on gas prices.
Brand spend to rise slightly in absolute terms, while staying around 2% of sales as a percentage.
Capex limited to about INR 70-80 crore of routine capex and balancing equipment, mainly for the vintage plant and to add value at bathware plant.
South plant to move to a long-term gas contract from next month, expected to cut gas cost by at least INR 17-18 per SCM versus the current INR 78.
capex_capacity: Current gas price in Morbi is about INR 74 per SCM plus 6% (about INR 78) for May, sourced from GSPC; North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper.
Morbi restarting after gas supply from 1 May: about 60-65% of Morbi running in mid-May, with management expecting about 85% by month-end; labour shortage is the constraint.
Company plants running at about 100% of operating capacity across India, excluding a couple of kilns shut for product-mix reasons.
INR 30 crore invested in a new press at Somany Max to improve utilisation.
Vintage plant balancing equipment being added to turn it profitable; bathware capacity being augmented.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand improved in January and February with single-digit growth; March was disrupted as exports stalled. Industry exports were about INR 17,000+ crore versus about INR 18,000 crore potential.
April was a slow but growing month: Morbi supply shortfall, higher prices (company about 15-17%, Morbi about 30-35%), and dealer destocking caused slower volumes.
Gas cost increase is about INR 5.5-6 per sq ft; other input costs (transport, labour, packaging) add about INR 1-1.5 per sq ft; total cost pressure about INR 6.5-7 per sq ft.
Management says the price hike covers the full cost in retail, while about 15% of business (projects) recovers about 85-90%.
Sanitaryware and bathware blended price hike of about 8% in April 2026.
Stock levels at Q4 end reduced by about 2.5 million sq m (about 15 days) over the year; old stock over 180 days cleared in March.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are the receivable days and negative working capital, and what is the outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects receivable days to stay near current levels, possibly up 1-2 days. Working capital gains came from lower outsourced-vendor stock and clearance of old stock in March. Sustainability is uncertain given the delayed response to price hikes in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a tipping point where gas costs make running plants unviable?
qa_highlights.answer: Tile prices are about 15-20% below two years ago and current hikes bring prices back to historic levels. Management does not see plant shutdown even with a further 10-15% rise, excluding a severe oil shock (about USD 200/bbl).

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only about 2% in Q4 versus double digits for peers, and realisation lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume was focused on non-JV and outsourced material to clear inventory before April price increases. It said realisation was up INR 6 per sq m YoY, with the mix shifting toward cheaper outsourced product.

qa_highlights.question: Gas price differential between Morbi and North, and South plant pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi is about INR 74 plus 6% (about INR 78) per SCM for May; the North plant is about INR 3-5 cheaper. South is INR 78 per SCM currently, but a long-term contract from next month should cut it by at least INR 17-18.

qa_highlights.question: Is the share buyback possible given the market leader's INR 300 crore buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Not for the next 6-8 months, due to an SEBI embargo tied to consolidation of wholly owned subsidiaries. Promoters bought shares before the trading window closed.

qa_highlights.question: Will Morbi's recovery affect outsourced volumes and FY27 supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outsourced OEM plants for large organised players should keep running. Four or five supplier plants had short-term material gaps in April, expected to normalise in May. Full material availability is expected by June.

risks_watch: Gas prices and any further geopolitical escalation; management said price cuts would follow if gas prices fall.
Morbi restart pace (85% target by end-May) and labour availability; a 10-15% Morbi capacity may not restart.
Demand response to 15-17% tile price hikes; management expects pent-up demand but April was slow.
Transport and fuel costs, which had not yet been quantified after diesel and petrol price hikes.
Sustainability of working capital release and debtor days, and the 4-day rise in receivables risk.
Somany Max path to positive EBITDA in FY27, and Acer and Amora now sitting in the outsourced bucket.
531548|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins and industry structure, while openly cautious on near-term demand, gas costs and labour; management repeatedly tied its guidance to no further geopolitical shocks. Answers on gas pricing and April volumes were less precise and some figures were corrected or restated during Q&A.

Tile still being the most cheapest material for the flooring and wall, like I mentioned, there is no alternative to a tile.

rows.why: Somany Max loss narrowed to INR 21 crore in FY26 (from INR 27 crore) and was near breakeven in Q4 versus INR 9 crore loss in Q4 FY25; INR 30 crore new press is being added to lift utilisation.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin guidance (at least 150 bps FY27 improvement) and industry structure from Morbi disruption, but cautious on April demand, gas costs, labour and Morbi restart; analysts pushed on working capital sustainability, Q4 volume growth of about 2%, and the gas-price differen

531548|2026-06.headline: Somany Q1 FY27: EBITDA margin up 3.6 pts YoY to 11.6% on standalone utilisation of 83% (vs 72%), with volume growth only ~3%.
531548|2026-06.overview: Management attributed the margin expansion to higher in-house capacity utilisation and a swing in JV performance from a loss of INR10 crore to a profit of INR3 crore YoY. Sales grew about 3% while value grew about 24%, with a few percent of sales lost in April when Morbi supply was shut for roughly 1.5 months. Price hikes of about 16-17% were passed through to the market, and gas costs rose 16-18% in the current period. Management guided to single-digit to mid-single-digit volume growth, maintained margins of 11%+, and announced a 9-plus million sq m South plant (about INR220 crore capex) due around end-Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion and will it sustain from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to standalone utilisation rising to 83% from 72% and JV profit of INR3 crore vs a loss of INR10 crore YoY. It said margins are driven by efficiency rather than pricing and expects them to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Gas pricing across Morbi, North and South?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended natural gas cost is about INR68/unit. South and Morbi are around mid-INR70s (South partly on spot), and North is about INR68-69. Management did not give a blended fuel cost incl. biofuel.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth outlook and why guidance is only mid-single-digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is currently mid-single-digit. It said the leader's higher growth came from in-house PVT production. It has been cautious after missed high-single-digit targets in the past.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price premium over Morbi narrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Morbi raised prices by roughly double Somany's 16-17%, narrowing the gap. Morbi units are now on GEL gas, and their accounting is being rectified, which narrows landed-cost differences.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR275 crore to end-FY27 including the INR220 crore South plant and balancing equipment, with 65-70% from internal accruals. JV loan is without corporate guarantee from Somany.

qa_highlights.question: Is 2%-3% volume growth affected by outsourcing from Morbi, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Morbi outsourcing is not needed beyond a point because of freight. Own plants are targeted at 100% utilisation, with capacity located in North, South and West.

531548|2026-09.headline: Somany Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 25% to INR854 crore with EBITDA margin at 11.7%; FY27 margin uplift guided up to 2-2.5%.
531548|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR854 crore, up roughly 25%, with volume growth of about 5.5% and EBITDA margin of 11.7%, attributed to better plant utilisation, full pass-through of price increases and a richer product mix. Bathware grew about 18% (INR88 crore, 15% per the tiles-breakup remark) and Building Solutions about 28% (INR45 crore). Gas cost rose to about INR70/SCM from INR45 in FY26 and INR43 in Q2, and management says it has been fully passed on. Several plants were down for upgradation in July and August, which management says cost volume growth of about 1.5 percentage points. JV swing improved to a Q2 profit of INR3 crore versus a loss of INR12 crore a year earlier.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR88 crore, about 15% growth. Sanitaryware growing about 20%, guided to 20% for FY27 and next year. Margins said to be a couple of points above tiles; brass-driven faucet margins were weaker in Q1.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR45 crore, about 28% growth. Adhesives growing 40-50%, with a new plant commissioned in the north last month and a south plant started last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth only about 5% when peers reached double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 7-8% volume growth next quarter. Q2 was hit by about 20 days of downtime in July and some August downtime. Without it, volume would have been about 1.5 points higher.

qa_highlights.question: GVT mix and margin effect of new capacity?

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans, including Nepal JV?

rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided up 2-2.5pp over FY26 (raised from 1-1.5pp), Q2 margin at 11.7%, FY28 guided at 11.5-12% or higher, with full pass-through of 16-17% price increases and gas at about INR70/SCM.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 16-17 million sq m mainly GVT expansion is under construction for production around September of next year, plus about 4 million sq m debottlenecking already added this year and a north adhesives plant commissioned last month.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex already set out (Siravit INR250 crore, sanitaryware JV stake to 76%, Sudha and Vintage modernisation, routine INR70-80 crore a year) and plants ran at 100% capacity, so further announcements are plausible but the big expansion is already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Margin guidance was already raised to 2-2.5pp and Q3 EBITDA is guided at or above Q2, but FY27 revenue guidance was held at high single digits despite a 25% Q2 print, and gas and freight risks cap further raises.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gas price volatility tied to the Middle East war, incomplete brass pass-through in faucets, and export recovery weakness (Morbi exports down about 31% in value) could pressure the guide, though management is confident on pricing.

rows.label: Morbi capacity shrink benefits organised sector
rows.why: About 35% of Morbi is shut with about 10% more expected to close over Diwali, and management expects no substantial capacity increase for 18-24 months.

rows.label: Sanitaryware JV stake raised to 76% from 51%
rows.why: Stake purchase to be funded from internal accruals and is already announced.

rows.label: Adhesives growth 40-50% with new plants
rows.why: Adhesives growing 40-50% with a north plant commissioned last month and a south plant started last quarter, supporting Building Solutions growth of about 28%.

531569|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell YoY as March 2026 exports stalled on Middle East disruption; consolidated revenue INR 132.1 mn, EBITDA margin 15.74%.
531569|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined year-on-year because exports could not be executed in March 2026 after Iran-related conflict disrupted Middle East shipping and logistics. Input costs also rose in March, compressing gross margins. Consolidated revenue was INR 132.1 mn with EBITDA of INR 21.73 mn (15.74% margin) and PAT of INR 5.5 mn (3.97% margin). Management says alternative routes via Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Southeast Asia have restarted shipments and expects a broader export recovery in Q1 FY27. The Pune IV facility, commercial since December 2025, contributed INR 2.7 mn in Q4 versus INR 1.2 mn in Q3.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2.7 mn in Q4 FY26 vs INR 1.2 mn in Q3 FY26

segments.name: Injectables (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 46.7 mn, about 44.43% of revenue from operations.

segments.name: Tablets (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 54.6 mn, about 51.95% of revenue from operations. Management expects tablets and capsules to grow more as dossiers get approved in other countries.

segments.name: IV fluids (Pune, JV/subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Commercial production began December 2025; revenue INR 1.2 cr in Q3 FY26 and INR 2.7 cr in Q4 FY26. FY27 target is INR 60-65 cr at 17-18% EBITDA margin; 5 products approved and 18 in pipeline.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals (Prague JV, 45% stake)
segments.commentary: Equity-accounted, so only profit is consolidated, not revenue. Prague business did EUR 0.5-0.6 mn revenue last year; profit could not be remitted in FY26 due to EU first-year dividend restriction.

FY27 Pune IV revenue target INR 60-65 cr annually; quarterly numbers may vary. Utilisation expected at 40%, 45%, 60% and 70% across the next four quarters.
Base business EBITDA margin guided at 15.5-16.5%.
Pune IV EBITDA margin 17-18% on annualised basis; first two quarters may see margin strain. Management expects breakeven at the IV business in FY27.
Debtor days expected to fall from about 65-70 days to 55-60 days.

Pune facility approved and commercialised, but product-wise approvals are an ongoing process that gates scale-up.
Raw material inventory held at about two months.
demand_pricing: Export share 85.26% in Q4 FY26; Latin America, Middle East & Africa and CIS together 76.09% of revenue. Middle East (including Africa) contributes about 40-45% of revenue per management.
No March 2026 exports to the Middle East; new routes via Saudi Arabia and Turkey, and Southeast Asia, now in use, with added logistics cost partly reimbursed by the Government of India.
Pricing is open to international price revisions, with no long-term fixed-price contracts, so input cost increases can be passed on (management cited COVID-era precedent).
Management says import content is under 1% of turnover, but packaging (plastics, aluminium) has been sourced from China and Taiwan after Middle East supply issues.
Competitive positioning cited as quality, turnaround time and customer relationships of 15+ years; named peers Farbe Firma and Kamala Lifesciences.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue decline and how will it accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: March 2026 major shipments were lost to shipping and container disruption tied to the Middle East conflict. Alternate routes are now in use and a fair recovery is expected in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Base business INR 80-85 cr and Pune IV INR 60-65 cr annually, with quarterly figures possibly varying.

qa_highlights.question: Is the base business margin expected to dip given logistics costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no margin dip is expected because a stronger dollar offsets most of the cost pressure; margins expected to stay in line.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivables high relative to sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables were INR 11.5 cr on base-business sales of about INR 65 cr, roughly 65 days, down from about 90 days last year. Debtor days are targeted at 55-60.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pune plant's volume and revenue so far?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2 million bottles generated about INR 3.5 cr over Q3 and Q4 FY26, against 60 mn annual capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East disruption continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge could last 1-3 months, with some logistics cost reimbursed by the Government of India.

risks_watch: Middle East shipping disruption and container shortages could persist beyond Q1 FY27; management said the challenge may last 1-3 months.
Pune IV scale-up depends on product-by-product regulatory approvals; 18 pipeline products await approval, with delays due to government process and staff transfers.
Nutraceutical JV profit is not yet being remitted and the majority stake deal is still under negotiation after two years.
Receivables rose sharply versus FY24 and sales growth; collection performance needs tracking against the 55-60 day target.
Crude oil, USD-INR and packaging input costs (plastics, aluminium) remain volatile and could compress margins.
Management did not give a quarterly breakdown for IV revenue, and the INR 10-15 cr quarterly run-rate timeline was not committed to.

rows.why: Receivables fell to INR 11.5 cr from INR 17.3 cr in March 2025 and debtor days went from about 90 to about 65; management targets 55-60.

531595|2026-03.headline: Capri Global Q4 FY26 PAT hit record INR283 crore (+59% YoY) and FY26 PAT INR949 crore (~2x), with consolidated gross Stage 3 down to 0.9%.
531595|2026-03.overview: Capri Global posted its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR283 crore in Q4 FY26, up 59% YoY, with FY26 PAT of INR949 crore, almost double the prior year. Consolidated AUM reached INR36,623 crore (+60% YoY, +20% QoQ), led by gold loans at INR16,965 crore (+111% YoY, +33% QoQ). Asset quality improved, with consolidated gross Stage 3 at 0.9% (down 61 bps QoQ) and net Stage 3 at 0.5%. Management reiterated FY28 targets of INR55,000 crore AUM (revised FY28 AUM guidance cited as INR57,000 crore in Q&A, with FY27 at INR46,000 crore), ROA 4-4.5% and ROE 16-18%.

financial_highlights.value: INR247 crore, 29% of net total income
INR54 crore, incl. INR16 crore management overlay

financial_highlights.metric: Blended yield / spread on net advances

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR16,965 crore (+111% YoY, +33% QoQ), about 46% of AUM. Gross Stage 3 at 0.3%. Branch AUM INR17 crore vs INR14 crore last quarter; 90% of branches above INR5 crore breakeven. Co-lending share in gold fell to about 31% from about 39%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,465 crore (+23% YoY); FY26 disbursement INR2,550 crore (+65% YoY). Micro-LAP AUM INR824 crore. Gross Stage 3 flat at 3%.

segments.name: Housing finance (CGHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR7,447 crore (+43% YoY). Self-employed share 74% of AUM. Gross Stage 3 at 1%, improved QoQ. 25 branches in South India.

segments.commentary: AUM INR5,708 crore (+38% YoY) across 282 active projects; average sanction ticket INR48 crore. Gross Stage 3 at 0.3%; Stage 2 reduced by INR53 crore on collections and rollback of 3 accounts.

segments.name: Co-lending and DA
segments.commentary: Co-lending AUM INR7,783 crore (+91% YoY, 21% of AUM). Co-lending and DA income INR97 crore (+76% YoY, -16% QoQ). New RBI co-lending norms from 1 Jan 2026 are causing a temporary slowdown.

segments.commentary: Insurance net fee income INR65 crore in Q4 and INR153 crore in FY26. Car loan origination INR3,492 crore in Q4 (+18% YoY) and INR11,910 crore in FY26 (+13% YoY), across 14 partner banks and FIs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance about INR1,300 crore (per Q&A).
FY27 AUM guidance INR46,000 crore; FY28 AUM about INR57,000 crore (raised about INR2,000 crore), with conservative 25% overall growth assumed. Opening remarks reiterated INR55,000 crore AUM by FY28.
FY27 ROA about 4% and ROE not less than 16%; medium-term FY28 ROA 4-4.5% and ROE 16-18%.
Cost of borrowing: about 10-20 bps reduction in FY27 (management cited ~9% exit cost, 'conservatively 9%'); a further ~20 bps possible after an expected credit rating upgrade within 6-9 months.
Sustainable credit cost about 0.7% of average total assets (historical range 0.6-0.7%). Co-lending and DA about 20% of total AUM. Gold mix may reach about 50%.
Branch additions of about 700-800 over two years, including about 350 gold loan branches in FY27 to be operational within the year. No RBI permission now needed.

Fee guidance: car loan income +12-15%, insurance income +25-30%, co-lending income flat; capital markets/bond vertical net fee income INR20-25 crore (gross INR40-50 crore) once licence (expected by end-June) is obtained.
capex_capacity: Net addition of 98 branches in Q4 FY26 and 318 in FY26, taking the network to 1,429 locations; 89 gold branches added in Q4 (36 Telangana, 18 Andhra Pradesh, 8 Karnataka, 20 Odisha).
Plan of about 700-800 branches over two years, mainly gold loan; about 350 gold loan branches this fiscal year.
Employee base up 5% QoQ (692 net additions); gold loan AUM per employee INR3.1 crore vs INR1.6 crore earlier.
Tier 2 capital may be raised; DA and co-lending expected to conserve capital over 18-24 months. CGCL standalone CRAR fell to 25.8%, driven by subsidiary investments.
Proposed international bond issuance deferred for 2-4 months due to higher hedging costs linked to the West Asia situation; ratings from Fitch (BB, stable) and Moody's (Ba3 CFR, stable) obtained.
demand_pricing: Gold loan yields fell sequentially by about 90 bps; management attributed this to co-lending gold loans at lower yields, which it said are accretive to profit per branch. Gold portfolio LTV about 66%; new disbursement LTV about 70%.

Co-lending rules (effective 1 Jan 2026) require interest accrued in LTV on moratorium loans and income assessment above INR2.5 lakh. Partners expected to go live by June, with full volumes from the September quarter.
No deterioration seen in MSME collection efficiency or asset quality from recent macro events.
Car loan distribution to add used cars this year, then credit cards, personal loans and mortgages over 3-4 years; target of about INR60-70 crore fee income over 4-5 years.
Housing yields rising as the self-employed mix increased to 74%.

qa_highlights.question: Target gold loan mix and branch plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold mix can reach about 50% from about 46%. About 700-800 branches over two years, including about 350 gold branches in FY27; no RBI permission needed.

qa_highlights.question: Gold yield sustainability and co-lending target?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower gold yields reflect co-lending and volume growth, which management says is accretive. Combined co-lending and DA target is about 20% of total AUM.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Expect 10-20 bps reduction in FY27, with exit around 9%. A further 20 bps is possible after a rating upgrade expected within 6-9 months.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About 0.7% for the year; Q4 0.8% included a INR16 crore macro management overlay. No slippage seen; most provisions are on new book.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 PAT and AUM guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 PAT guidance about INR1,300 crore. AUM guidance INR46,000 crore for FY27 and about INR57,000 crore for FY28 (25% conservative growth).

qa_highlights.question: Gold LTV risk if prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin call to restore LTV within 75%, then 14-day notice and auction if not met. Portfolio LTV about 66%.

risks_watch: Co-lending volumes likely to slow for one to two quarters under new RBI norms; full volume expected from the September 2026 quarter.
Gold price volatility with a 70% new-disbursement LTV; a sharp fall would trigger margin calls or auctions.
Gold yield compression (about 90 bps QoQ), with branch-level profitability depending on continued volume growth.
Cost of funds guidance depends on a rating upgrade and on rate moves after elections; international bond timing depends on hedging costs.
Capital adequacy: CGCL standalone CRAR fell to 25.8%; capital plan relies on DA, co-lending and possible Tier 2 issuance.
Q4 PCR of 41.2% and credit cost of 0.8% including overlay; watch whether the management overlay reverses.
key_quotes: With this backdrop, I am pleased to say that Capri Global has delivered strong quarterly performance in Q4 FY '26, continuing its growth momentum and maintaining asset quality while delivering highest ever quarterly profit of INR283 crores, a 59% increase year -on-year and full year profit of INR949 crores, almost double from the last year.
So, there is no slippage.
So overall, if you look at our business mix is designed in a manner to grow in tandem with the overall growth.
So, portfolio level LTV is about 66%. And on the new disbursement, LTV is about 70%.
So overall growth, we are targeting conservatively 25%. And we are giving a guidance of INR46,000 crores by end of FY '27 and about INR57,000 crores by FY '28.

Cautious on near-term co-lending volumes under new RBI norms, cost of funds (guided only 10-20 bps FY27 reduction), gold price risk and international bond timing; several answers hedged with "depends on" and "conservatively".

531595|2026-06.headline: Capri Global posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of INR353 crore (+102% YoY) on AUM of INR40,112 crore (+62% YoY) and cost-to-income of 44.2%.
531595|2026-06.overview: Capri Global reported record quarterly profit after tax of INR353 crore, up 102% YoY, with consolidated AUM of INR40,112 crore, up 62% YoY and 10% QoQ. Gold loans (48% of AUM) drove growth, with AUM of INR19,179 crore (+111% YoY, +13% QoQ), while cost-to-income improved to 44.2% from 49.4% in Q4 FY26. Asset quality weakened at the margin: gross Stage 2 ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.8%, mostly on gold loans, and gross Stage 3 rose to 1.1%, largely from one construction finance account. Management revised its FY28 AUM target to INR65,000 crore and reiterated medium-term ROE of 19-21% and ROA of 4.2-4.7%.

segments.commentary: AUM INR6,779 crore, +24% YoY; disbursements INR616 crore, +32% YoY. Micro-LAP AUM INR876 crore. Share of AUM has declined as capital was prioritised to gold loans.

qa_highlights.question: Split of the INR385 crore sequential Stage 2 rise by segment, whether it is recent origination or seasonal, why coverage fell from 11.8% to 9.4%, and any mix shift into gold.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR125 crore DCCO extension within the 0.7% construction finance GNPA, and is it real slippage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCCO cases are outside GNPA and still classified as standard.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of a weak or strong monsoon on gold loan demand.
qa_highlights.answer: A weak monsoon could push microfinance and marginal farmers to gold loans. Management said 25% gold loan growth is achievable from existing branches, with new branches adding further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Branch rollout: why Q1 additions were modest versus the earlier plan of about 350 branches in FY27, and whether additions are back-ended.
qa_highlights.answer: About 150 branches in Q2 and 250 more in Q3, for 400 total, now revised up from 350 and to be completed on or before December 2026. Management said the plan is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of gold loan yields at about 18.6%, and risk of competition.
qa_highlights.answer: Yields were about 18.5% after a shift to smaller tickets with changed incentives. Management expects another 50-75 bps of improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Scope for further cost-of-funds reduction in FY27.
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees little scope for further cost reduction from current levels in FY27, and expects costs to stay broadly stable. Diversification via NCDs, CP, bank refinancing and a GMTN programme is under way, with bank share to decline.

qa_highlights.question: Target gold loan share of AUM and FY27 and FY28 AUM targets, including quarterly run-rate.

531768|2026-03.headline: Poly Medicure Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 21% YoY to INR534 crore; FY27 consolidated guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore with margin pressure from raw-material costs.

FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12.3% to INR1,875 crore, while standalone grew about 4% to INR1,662 crore and standalone EBITDA margin came in at 26.8%. Management flagged a raw-material cost increase of about 20% linked to crude, plus freight and wage pressure, and said gross margin could fall to roughly 66% (200-300 bps lower) on current conditions. FY27 guidance calls for consolidated revenue of INR2,300-2,400 crore and standalone of INR1,900-1,950 crore, with capex of INR200-225 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Brazil target is a small, non-operating medical-device storage and distribution company acquired for about USD40,000, saving 18-24 months. Citieffe and PendraCare are each about 50% Europe and 50% RoW; Citieffe also has about 35-40% in North America and Mexico.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q4 dip to product mix, with some lower-margin products in the portfolio.

qa_highlights.answer: The INR9 crore was transaction-related adviser costs and regulatory and employee provisions booked at year-end at international entities; no manpower rationalisation. The acquired entities had a negative EBITDA impact of about INR2.6 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable organic growth rate and the long-term revenue mix target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FY27 guidance of over 25% consolidated growth and 15-16% standalone growth. Long-term target is about one-third India and two-thirds RoW.

532054|2026-09.headline: KDDL H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.5% YoY to Rs 1,345.8 crore, with PAT of Rs 92.9 crore at a 6.9% margin.
532054|2026-09.overview: KDDL reported strong H1 FY27 top-line growth, with consolidated total income up 33.5% YoY to Rs 1,345.8 crore and Q2 up 31.6% to Rs 698.7 crore. Precision engineering (Eigen) and packaging (Ornapak) grew fastest, while the bracelet unit faced export softness linked to the Swiss watch industry. Management pulled forward Eigen capex (FY27 spend now about Rs 70-75 crore, up roughly Rs 15-20 crore from about Rs 50 crore) and said watch components growth would exceed the earlier 12-14% guidance. Consolidated PAT margin was 6.9% for both Q2 and H1, and management reiterated a 20-25% medium-term growth goal for Eigen.

segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew close to 50% YoY, driven by export demand and new customers. Medium-term goal is 20-25% CAGR; the US is about 50% of segment revenue per the analyst, and the company focuses on US, Americas and Europe.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 30% in H1 from a low base. Q2 achieved positive PBT for the first time, with positive profitability expected to continue.

segments.commentary: Sales volumes are above management expectations and the brand sells in over 35 countries with about 45 doors outside Ethos. Management expects FY27 loss to be significantly lower than FY26 and sees possible break-even next year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a backlog. Funnel projects converted faster and larger than expected from existing and new customers, and the company sees no major impact from AI/data-centre capex swings given its small share.

qa_highlights.answer: New customers span BESS, EV, electronics, aerospace and defence. Capabilities added include rack plating, welding, blanking and machining. qa_highlights.answer: Watch components grew about 30% YoY in H1, slightly below the company average because Eigen and packaging grew faster. Management said full-year watch components growth will exceed the 12-14% guidance.

segments.commentary: Corporate loans grew 6.3% YoY (about 15.3% in June). Mid-corporate grew about 26% and core corporate about 12%; the decline is in fine-priced high-quality assets where the bank is refusing to cut pricing.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International advances grew 39.7% YoY; international deposits grew 14.9% YoY.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits +16.4% YoY; domestic CASA +10.4% YoY and term deposits +20.5% YoY. Retail deposits ex-FCNR(B) grew about 8.3% and bulk deposits about 14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the NSE and valuation gain was taken into profit, and how much of it was used for provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Total NSE effect is about INR 3,600 crore, made up of about INR 1,300-1,349 crore cash profit and the rest valuation gain. About INR 1,600 crore of this was put into prudential and contingency provisions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,300 crore prudential provision for ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: It is specific provisioning on NPA and bad-debt accounts, not standard-asset provisioning. The INR 300 crore contingency sits in other provisions to cover bond and equity valuation swings. The CFO declined to give a standard-asset ECL estimate, saying the bank is still computing it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FCNR(B) money being used to repay bulk deposits or to fund loans?
qa_highlights.answer: It is stored liquidity. Only about INR 10,000 crore of bulk deposits were reduced. The funds will go to repay high-cost bulk deposits if rates stay elevated, or otherwise to credit growth. Management says the net book impact is the same either way.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 13-15% credit guidance achievable given the first-half run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The RAM book is expected to add about INR 60,000 crore, and the corporate pipeline is more than INR 60,000 crore. Management says this is achievable, as the same period in Q3 and Q4 last year delivered a similar increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 99% CRR requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: The impact is estimated at INR 2,000-3,000 crore, which management does not regard as significant.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank considering ECB or ODI borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: The bank has raised USD 1.1 billion against a USD 4 billion mandate, valid until December. It will tap more only if pricing is right.

FCNR(B) unhedged currency exposure and interest outgo of USD 350-400 million a year, with hedging decisions pending.

Rising rates, drought/El Nino effects on agri and restructuring under SLBC guidance (no state schemes yet), and gold loan scrutiny.
Insurance commission rules and MDR deferral; management could not quantify the impact on distribution income.

532143|2026-03.headline: SKM Egg Products FY26 sales rose 58% to ₹767 crore and PAT crossed ₹100 crore for the first time (₹102 crore).
532143|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 results: sales up 58% YoY to ₹767 crore, operating profit about ₹163 crore, PBT ₹136 crore and PAT ₹102 crore, the first year above ₹100 crore PAT. Q4 FY26 sales were ₹197 crore, with PBT ₹41 crore and PAT ₹32 crore against ₹9.7 crore and ₹6.22 crore a year earlier. Management said powder capacity is now running at full utilisation, so FY27 volume growth will be modest. The company is funding a ₹400 crore layer-shed expansion (about 20 lakh birds, completion targeted 2028-29) and is bringing the associate SKM Universal into the listed entity.

segments.commentary: About 7,000 tonnes of powder today with a stated target of 10,000 tonnes over roughly five years; powder capacity was 7,320 tonnes as of 2023. Management said FY27 powder volume growth will be small because capacity is fully used.

segments.name: Shellac (export and domestic)
segments.commentary: Export business is about ₹100 crore and domestic about ₹40 crore; management expects this to keep growing and to be a source of FY27 growth.

segments.name: Branded / value-added egg products
segments.commentary: Products include egg in tetra-pack, egg liquid, egg white cube and Egg Pro protein drink. Management reformulated Egg Pro for launch in June, and an R&D division is planned within six months. Revenue from these products has been small so far.

qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no exact volume or consideration figures on the call. It said capacity is full, realisation rose through FY26 with a Q4 dip on mix (~₹722/kg powder), and the ₹1,000 crore goal is for 2030. For SKM Universal, the valuation is about ₹37 crore for the whole company; the group already holds 26%, so the 74% stake costs about ₹27.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the country-wise revenue split and competitive position, and what is driving elevated egg prices in Japan?
qa_highlights.answer: The country split was declined as it is not public. Competitors are European producers in Japan and Russia. Management said it earns about 5% more than competitors. Price strength was attributed to bird flu culls, which take about two years to repopulate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity, the 400 crore capex timeline, and the value-added product plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Flock is moving toward 40 lakh birds by 2028-29. The capex is a cost-saving investment, not a revenue driver. Management is developing value-added products (Egg Pro relaunch, egg white cube) and an R&D unit. Shellac export and domestic are also growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Indian producers not consistently profitable outside bird flu cycles, and how are contracts priced and hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bird-flu disruptions are sporadic and under control, with vaccination under discussion with the government. Contracts are mostly 3–6 months, priced on cost and competition, and the forex hedge is currently only about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected ROC on the new EC-shed project and what drives FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exact ROC figures would follow later. It said the project cuts production cost by about ₹0.20 per egg. FY27 growth is expected to be small in powder and larger in shellac and domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: How does the USD–EUR rate affect other expenses, and will the investor presentation be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe is a small share of business and most pricing is in USD. Russia is invoiced in rupees and rubles, and Japan from H2. The presentation will be uploaded to the website.

532143|2026-06.headline: SKM Egg Products' Q1 FY27 realisation rose to about Rs 770/kg from Rs 722 last quarter, while management flagged feed-cost pressure lasting at least two more quarters.
532143|2026-06.overview: Management said the company is running near full capacity, so volume growth is capped and results depend on international egg product prices, exchange rates and feed costs. Realisation was stated at about Rs 770 per unit against Rs 722 last quarter, mainly helped by the rupee, while margins were hit by a substantial rise in soya-based feed costs. Management said the company is moving into domestic branded eggs, with a business plan due by end-March, and is adding easy-shed capacity with completion targeted for November-December 2028. Capex approval for further expansion is expected at the next board meeting, with a target of October. The call was largely Q&A; no formal presentation was given, and several answers were vague on numbers.

segments.commentary: About 20 lakh birds planned; first four sheds completed earlier, all to be complete by November-December 2028. Management said the cost advantage is at least 5% of overall production cost, from higher productivity and feed efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Will profit stay around 100 crore for the year, and can raw material inflation be passed on?

qa_highlights.question: Will quarterly profits exceed 16 crore in the next two quarters?

532144|2026-06.headline: Welspun Corp posted record quarterly EBITDA of INR756 crore (+35% YoY) and an INR25,750 crore order book, heavily US-weighted.
532144|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as robust, with the highest-ever quarterly EBITDA of INR756 crore, up 35% YoY, and ROCE above 20% annualised. Net cash rose to INR2,336 crore and the order book was about INR25,750 crore (~$2.7 billion), described as the strongest in company history and heavily loaded toward the US. Domestic DI pipe demand under Jal Jeevan Mission was weak on fund constraints and industry overcapacity, so the company shifted focus to exports and pig iron. Sintex remains under pressure from muted domestic demand, and management continues to invest in its dealer, distribution and branding base. Full-year guidance was not revised, which management attributed to a policy of giving realistic guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Strongest in company history; mid-call an analyst cited INR24,750 crore and management later said close to INR26,000 crore

financial_highlights.value: Guidance about $300 per tonne; current quarter slightly above

segments.name: US line pipe (Little Rock, HFIW/ERW and LSAW)
segments.commentary: Booked well through FY28 with FY29 discussions under way. The ERW/HFIW mill is commissioned and stabilised with orders being started. The LSAW plant is due by year-end. Order book split is about 75% export-to-Gulf Coast LNG and about 25% data centres.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia line pipe (KSA)
segments.commentary: Two facilities are progressing, with the first expected by Q2 and both progressively by Q3 FY27 per management. Competitive intensity is rising, and anti-dumping action on DI pipe imports is moving in the right direction.

segments.name: India DI pipes and pig iron
segments.commentary: Domestic Jal Jeevan Mission demand is under severe pressure. Capacity was scaled down and pig iron exports were ramped, with management calling the company one of the largest pig iron exporters this quarter. India LSAW exports run at about 150,000-200,000 tonnes a year.

segments.commentary: Impacted by muted domestic demand. Management is expanding its dealer, distributor and influencer network quarter on quarter and continuing announced capex. No segment financials were given on the call.

segments.commentary: Management said the project is on track and progressing as planned. No figures were given.

segments.commentary: Partial stake sale of about 3-4.5%. Welspun retains more than 22% and remains the largest shareholder, with no further dilution planned.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said competition is rising but the market is large enough for everyone, and the company has more than 15 years on the ground. Anti-dumping is progressing in the right direction, and the Saudi law requires imports to stop once domestic capacity is available.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin in Q1 sustainable and what is US EBITDA per tonne?

qa_highlights.question: Why is full-year guidance not being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers realistic guidance given project-based business and geopolitical uncertainty, and has met or exceeded guidance over the last four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the 26% GGBS (slag) associate stake?

qa_highlights.question: Is there any incremental capex or inorganic plan beyond FY28?

532144|2026-09.headline: Welspun Corp Q2 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR782 crore (+25% YoY) with order book near INR50,000 crore and net cash of INR3,887 crore.
532144|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 EBITDA of INR782 crore (+25% YoY) and H1 EBITDA of INR1,538 crore (+30% YoY), both all-time highs, against FY27 guidance of INR2,850 crore. Order book stands at a record ~INR50,000 crore (~USD 5.2 billion), with the US booked through FY29. The Board approved three investments: a US spiral pipe debottlenecking (225,000 MTPA, up to USD 115 million, ready by March 2028), a 50-50 Jordan spiral pipe and coating plant with Perma-Pipe (up to USD 125 million), and an India FBE coating JV with Perma-Pipe (about INR110 crore). Domestic India demand, especially water, remains weak, while exports and the US remain the growth drivers.

segments.name: US (Little Rock spiral pipe)
segments.commentary: Booked through FY29 with a INR5,500 crore data-centre pipeline order recently won; 800-acre site with port and rail access cited as a cost and speed advantage. US EBITDA per tonne called exceptional versus a sustainable ~$300/tonne, and current US order margins are locked in through FY29 per management.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia (LSAW and DI pipe)
segments.commentary: Commissioning on track, with LSAW and DIP plants to be completed in Q3 and up and running by year-end; order materialisation delayed by Middle East supply chain disruption. Management targets at least 50-60% utilisation in the first year, and noted anti-dumping duty on DI pipe imports in Saudi Arabia.

segments.name: India domestic DI and line pipe
segments.commentary: Domestic water demand under stress and Jal Jeevan Mission budget slowdown; domestic DI volumes to be substantially lower. Management is shifting DI production toward exports (Europe, Middle East) and reported that pig iron performed well.

segments.name: India exports
segments.commentary: Management called exports the bright spot, with bid pipeline robust for Middle East, Southeast Asia, Australia and LatAm, all serviced from India.

segments.name: Welspun Specialty Solutions (WSSL)
segments.commentary: Stainless steel bars and seamless pipes; Q2 exports to Europe hit by freight costs and tariffs, and domestic demand expected to improve over the next two quarters. Power gen, nuclear, defence, aerospace, oil and gas and petrochemicals are the focus sectors.

segments.name: Sintex
segments.commentary: Focused on premiumisation in water tanks and on plastic pipes, now in 15 states. Management said the fintech/Sintex loss was driven by marketing, R&D and digital investment, and that it is close to breakeven before those costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR2,850 crore retained; management said H2 is tracking well and it would be pleasantly surprised to exceed guidance, but stayed cautious.
ROCE guidance is more than 20% for FY27; H1 annualised ROCE is 22.7%.
Saudi plant readiness expected in Q3 FY27; incremental earnings from new US and Saudi capacity expected from FY28, with a possible lag if the Middle East supply chain does not normalise.
Jordan capacity is being finalised at about 350,000 to 500,000 tonnes, against a firm MoU and an existing order backlog.
Company expects to remain in net cash after all announced capex (Saudi, US, Jordan, India JV).
capex_capacity: US spiral pipe debottlenecking and capacity augmentation: 225,000 MTPA at up to USD 115 million, ready by March 2028.

Jordan greenfield spiral pipe and coating plant, 50-50 JV with Perma-Pipe, total capex up to USD 125 million, backed by a firm MoU with the Jordan National Water Carrier developers and the government.
India FBE coating JV with Perma-Pipe at Anjar, about INR110 crore total project cost, expected to be operational in the next financial year.
Saudi LSAW and DIP plants in final commissioning, targeted for Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: US demand is robust with a strong bid pipeline (data centres, LNG exports, gas-fired captive power). Management said ordering is being calibrated, with some projects still to be finalised over the next couple of quarters, and expects demand to last 3 to 5 years beyond FY29.

Total contested bid pipeline is about 2 to 3 million tonnes at any time, against a typical 3 to 4 million tonnes; India domestic bid pipeline described as weak, while India export and Saudi pipelines are robust.
Saudi DIP demand is seen as import substitution, with only about two-thirds of captive DI requirement currently served by imports; Welspun expects first right of refusal on local demand.
Management described US and Middle East demand as structural rather than cyclical, with 5 to 7 years of visibility.
Competition in the US from 2 to 3 players, who are mainly doing debottlenecking; Saudi line pipe competition is pre-existing and rising, and Welspun is targeting niche segments there.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers ordering beyond FY29 in the US, and how should order build-up be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline remains robust but ordering is being calibrated in timing; intensity will slow, but demand is expected to last 3 to 5 years beyond FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new Saudi and Jordan capacity fungible to the US if US demand stays high?
qa_highlights.answer: Fungibility exists technically, but Saudi demand is expected to keep Saudi capacity busy first; North America supply from Saudi is not ruled out. Jordan was a strategic decision based on reconstruction in Syria, Iraq and Lebanon.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi utilisation ramp in FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is aiming for at least 50-60% utilisation in the first year of operations, with a fast ramp if the supply chain stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US order margin locked in through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes, the margins on the existing US orders are locked in.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 outperform the INR2,850 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would love to but is cautious given uncontrollable variables; it expects to meet or exceed guidance based on past delivery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India domestic outlook and the net debt position after capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic demand may stay sluggish for several quarters, especially in water; the company remains in net cash of about INR3,800 crore even after all announced capex.

Sintex losses increased and Welspun Specialty export weakness to Europe.

532149|2026-06.headline: Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.23% YoY to Rs 3,068 crore; Global NIM eased to 2.52% and FY27 guidance was kept unchanged.

532149|2026-09.headline: Bank of India Q2 FY27: H1 net profit about Rs 6,000 crore, Global NIM 2.47%, Gross NPA 1.60%; ECL front-loading planned from Q3, about 0.5% CRAR impact per year.
532149|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong YoY growth: global business up 21.13% to Rs 18.92 lakh crore, and global advances up 20.58%. Operating profit rose 33.18% to Rs 5,089 crore and net profit rose 25.32% to Rs 3,202 crore for Sept'26 (the Q2 figure as stated on the call). Asset quality improved, with Gross NPA at 1.60% and Net NPA at 0.42%, and credit cost fell to 0.12% from 0.15% in June'26. Global NIM eased 5 bps YoY to 2.47%, which management attributed mainly to FCNR-linked leverage. Management guided FY27 global advances growth of 15-16% and global deposit growth of 16-17%, and said ECL provisioning will begin from Q3 after Board approval.

financial_highlights.change: +Rs 20,539 crore YoY; ratio down from prior quarters
down 5 bps from 2.52% (management cited Sept'25 at 2.41%)

segments.commentary: Corporate pipeline about Rs 65,000 crore as of 30 Sept; total pipeline across corporate, RAM, digital, pool/co-lending and supply chain about Rs 86,000-87,000 crore. Largest sector pipelines are renewable energy (over Rs 12,000 crore), power (over Rs 9,000 crore) and roads (over Rs 5,000 crore).

segments.name: Overseas book
segments.commentary: Overseas advances up 35.21% YoY to Rs 1.51 lakh crore against overseas deposits up 11.52% to Rs 1.37 lakh crore; FCNR raise of USD 2.2 billion was deployed into the international loan book.

segments.name: Supply chain / trade
segments.commentary: Supply chain book just over Rs 1,000 crore, with a Rs 1,500 crore first-year target; trade and MSME-linked assets grew about 10% in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guided at 15-16% and global deposit growth at 16-17%.
ROA guided above 1% on a quarterly basis; management said ROA was above 1% in March'26, June'26 and Sept'26, and expects above 1% in March'27. FY28 expected to be better.

ECL: provisions expected to start from Q3 FY27 after Board approval, with Q3 and Q4 as front-loading quarters; ECL regime applies from 1 April 2027. Ballpark CRAR impact about 0.5% per year over the next 4 years.
NIM expected to gain about 6-7 bps from the 25 bps repo hike, with deposit repricing staggered because about 60% of term deposits mature in 1 to 18 months.
Recovery in written-off accounts expected to sustain the run rate of about Rs 900-1,000 crore a quarter; non-interest income expected to hold above Rs 2,500 crore a quarter.
capex_capacity: Technology budget for opex and capex (core IT, digital, cybersecurity) said to be unchanged for FY27; Big Four consultants engaged on IT, digital and cybersecurity transformation.
AI policy approved by the Board; current AI use is predictive (Data Lake project), with analytics-led leads above Rs 21,000 crore.
Centralised supply chain branch in Mumbai handles pool, co-lending, trades and supply chain; 69 zones each asked to onboard one new supply chain vendor per month.
ECL: consultant onboarded; computation covers PD, LGD and SICR; Board note to be presented, with clarity expected by Q3.
demand_pricing: Domestic deposit and advances growth remained strong YoY, with management saying no impact from the macro headwinds is foreseen on FY27 business growth.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the ECL provisioning need, how much is already provided, and what is the road ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the broad total will not be shared until the Board note; the CRAR impact is about 0.5% per year over 4 years, covered by profits (H1 profit above Rs 6,000 crore, run rate of about Rs 12,000 crore for FY27). qa_highlights.question: Will the bank still meet its growth targets given global and drought headwinds?

qa_highlights.question: How much can NIM improve from the rate hike, and how will CASA be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: The FCNR raise cost about 5 bps of NIM. The repo hike is expected to add 6-7 bps, with a lag on deposits. Bulk deposits are being used to fund credit growth, while retail term deposits are about 43% of total deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What drove non-interest income, and why is other income down?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries from written-off accounts rose about 190% YoY to Rs 978 crore, and treasury/forex profit rose 157% to Rs 411 crore. Non-interest income was Rs 2,700 crore, up 25% YoY.

532155|2026-06.headline: GAIL Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to Rs 4,292 crore (from Rs 1,262 crore in Q4), led by gas marketing and LPG/LHC gains from West Asia price spikes.
532155|2026-06.overview: GAIL reported a sharply higher Q1 FY27, with consolidated PAT (ex-minority) of Rs 4,665 crore versus Rs 1,485 crore in Q4 FY26, driven by elevated crude and LPG prices and favourable Brent index movements in gas marketing. Management flagged that the gas marketing spread is largely a timing effect from the 9-month JCC sourcing versus 3-month Brent sales and will normalise. Gas marketing PBT guidance for FY27 was held at around Rs 4,500 crore despite Q1 gas marketing PBT of Rs 3,353 crore. Transmission volumes were 122.36 MMSCMD, and FY27 transmission guidance was set at around 123 MMSCMD. The Pata petchem complex is now at 100% load after a partial restart in mid-May, and the Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda pipeline became fully operational on 31 May 2026.

segments.commentary: Volume 122.36 MMSCMD vs 118.99 MMSCMD in Q4, with shipper volumes up about 4 MMSCMD. FY27 volume guidance raised to around 123 MMSCMD. Q4 transmission cost included a provision that fell from Rs 111 crore to Rs 11 crore in Q1.

segments.name: LPG transmission
segments.commentary: Volume 1,077 TMT vs 1,114 TMT in Q4 (down ~3%) due to West Asia disruption of LPG imports.

segments.commentary: Production rose about 20% to 232 TMT from 194 TMT after an extra 0.597 MMSCMD of New Well Gas allocation; PBT Rs 772 crore vs Rs 144 crore in Q4 and Rs 489 crore in FY26. Production is expected to stay in this range through FY27.

segments.name: Polymer (petchem)
segments.commentary: Production 51 TMT with a loss of Rs 130 crore due to gas diversion to priority sectors; plant at 100% capacity and expected to reach breakeven during FY27. Pata shifting from natural gas to ethane is being pursued.

segments.name: City gas (CGD) and GAIL Gas
segments.commentary: GAIL Gas (wholly owned) had 592 CNG stations and 7,93,684 DPNG connections as of 30 June 2026, adding 16,610 DPNG in Q1. Its Q1 turnover was Rs 3,326 crore and PAT Rs 120 crore (+3% QoQ). GAIL CGD added 20,069 DPNG connections and 3 CNG stations in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change in demand outlook given government steps to reduce LPG exposure, and how should FY28-29 demand be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited PNGRB paper projecting demand rising to 297 MMSCMD by FY30 from 200 MMSCMD; said GAIL has not revised its own volumes and relies on PNGRB figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Rs 4,500 crore gas marketing guidance far below the Q1 run rate, and is further upside likely?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 gains came from JCC 9-month vs 3-month Brent timing and a one-off Brent jump; much will cure within the year, depending on dated Brent. Guidance kept due to volatility, to be revised later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Henry Hub cross-index advantage sustain for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on Brent and Henry Hub levels; the cross-index is currently in a sweet spot, but the open volume is only about 25-30% of the 21 MMSCMD, and Pata will consume its allocated volume at 100% load.

qa_highlights.question: What is the petchem breakeven gas price and the average realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Average petchem landed gas cost was $10.54/MMBtu in Q1; breakeven at about $13-14 landed gas cost with selling price around Rs 130,000/MT.

qa_highlights.question: Is the unbundling obligation still in force, and what is the role of the independent TSO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PNGRB has withdrawn clause 5A, so no current obligation to unbundle transmission and marketing; the TSO would monitor the 25% third-party open-access quantities on pipelines.

qa_highlights.question: How will depreciation and interest move with new projects commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation about Rs 3,200-3,300 crore in the coming year, with PDH-PP adding about Rs 312 crore; finance cost Rs 310 crore in Q1, about Rs 1,200-1,300 crore annually, with PDH-PP adding about Rs 440 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q4 transmission provision reversed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No; the provision fell from Rs 111 crore to Rs 11 crore in Q1, and the Q4 one-off was not reversed in the current quarter.

532156|2026-03.headline: Vaibhav Global FY26: PBT up 41% YoY, record FCF of INR272 crore, EBITDA margin 10.8%; FY27 guidance 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion.
532156|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR935 crore (+10% YoY) with EBITDA of INR96 crore (about 10.3%) and PBT of INR64 crore (+41% YoY). For FY26, revenue was INR3,691 crore, EBITDA margin rose 140 bps to 10.8%, and free cash flow hit a record INR272 crore. In-house brands crossed 50% of B2C sales about a year ahead of plan, and Germany reached full-year EBITDA breakeven. Management guided FY27 to 9-11% revenue growth and a 50-100 bps EBITDA margin improvement, but gave no constant-currency guidance. U.S. and U.K. growth stayed weak in Q4, and the Mindful Souls write-off of about INR25 crore was a notable one-off.

segments.name: Germany

segments.name: Mindful Souls
segments.commentary: Digital-first acquisition; INR25 crore write-off taken on conservative impairment testing. Management says the business is still profitable and shows cross-learning benefits; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Positive numbers were seen in the current quarter.

segments.commentary: Lifestyle products are ~35% of total sales (medium-term target 50%). Lab-grown diamonds are ~11% of retail revenue at ASP around USD 250 (about 18 months old category).

capex_capacity: In-house jewellery casting line operationalised in the U.S. during FY26, reducing tariff impact on shipments.
New U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026; existing buildings to be vacated and move completed during FY27, consolidating 4 buildings into one.
100% of manufacturing power from solar; two U.S. sites and one each in U.K. and Germany run fully on renewable energy.
Capex quantum and timing for FY27 were not discussed on the call.

Management reported early-April/May trends: better digital traction in U.S. and U.K., TV audiences still stressed by inflation and higher gas and interest rates; Germany traction better than last quarter.
Elevated precious metal prices and cautious discretionary spend were cited as headwinds across core markets; tariff uncertainty persists.

qa_highlights.question: How can EBITDA margin rise back toward the 13-15% levels seen in FY22 when revenue is much larger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Germany's breakeven and digital/paid media investments weighed on margin; margin rose from 7% (FY23) to 11% (FY26). Leverage expected in HR, SG&A and shipping; peak 15% seen as achievable over time but no precise timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter India, and will the company consider a buyback given the share price decline?

qa_highlights.question: Lifestyle 50% target versus in-house jewellery mix: are these contradictory?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Panwad clarified that in-house brands are 50% of B2C, of which 85% is jewellery and 15% lifestyle; the 35% lifestyle share and 50% medium-term target are for total group sales, including external and umbrella brands.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins flat over three years despite digital mix shift, lab-grown and higher ASPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B sales growth (lower gross margin, no content cost) dilutes gross margin; Q4 gross margin rose ~180 bps and FY26 ~40 bps. Tariffs and metal spikes were a substantial headwind, and paid media channel margins are rising.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the 50-100 bps margin improvement come from, and what constant-currency growth to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin first, then employee cost efficiency; shipping leverage unlikely this year and SG&A not expected to leverage. No constant-currency guidance given; INR guidance used given macro and business transition.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a INR25 crore Mindful Souls write-off and what drove other expenses up ~16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment reflects conservative testing as double-digit growth did not materialise; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Other expenses rose on U.K. warehouse set-up, travel and AI technology spend, which management called temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in ROE and the ROU asset increase?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE was driven by PAT growth including a one-time MAT credit; normalised ROE still improves to ~15%. ROU increase is from a new U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Trends for U.S. growth and visibility from AI initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal cited AI across ad creatives, landing pages, conversion analytics and supply-chain forecasting, started about a year ago and accelerating recently. He expects U.S. and U.K. to reach double-digit growth in mid-to-long term but gave no timeline.

Mindful Souls impairment (INR25 crore) and payback extended to 7 years; further write-downs possible.

Shipping costs may rise due to geopolitical disruption (management referenced Asian crisis and war).

532156|2026-06.headline: Vaibhav Global Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 37% YoY to Rs 102 crore, but reported gains were helped by Rs 25.5 crore US tariff refund and FX; constant-currency revenue was broadly flat.

Analysts pressed on the tariff refund's accounting (recorded as other operating revenue, with questions on whether it sits in gross margin), the gap between digital revenue growth and volumes, and the Rs 5,000–5,500 crore FY30 vision. Management gave no hard margin guidance beyond saying gross margin and investment would keep improving.
