532156|2026-09.headline: Vaibhav Global Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7% to INR 938.4 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.1% and FY27 growth guidance was cut to 7-9%.
532156|2026-09.overview: Q2 was a transition quarter as Vaibhav moved all six retail websites to Shopify Enterprise and consolidated four UK warehouses and two studios into one site. Management attributed about $2.8 million (roughly 2.8 percentage points) of revenue growth loss to the platform migration. Gross margin expanded about 197 bps to 65.5%, but EBITDA margin fell 193 bps to 8.1% on deleverage in the US and UK. FY27 revenue growth guidance was cut to 7-9% from 9-11%, and FY27 margin is now expected broadly flat versus FY26 instead of 50-100 bps expansion.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 257.2 crore, +2.3% in INR and -7% in constant currency, the weakest region. Drivers were the platform migration, product unavailability during warehouse consolidation (INR 36 crore capex) and weak consumer sentiment.

532163|2026-03.headline: Saregama Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% YoY to INR 287 crore and adjusted EBITDA hit a record INR 133 crore (+31% YoY).
532163|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 287 crore (+19% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of INR 133 crore (+31% YoY) and operational PBT of INR 105 crore (+37% YoY). Asset quality stayed clean, with net NPA at 0.30% and the provision coverage ratio at 75%.

Order inflow was Rs.7,979 crore versus Rs.8,214 crore a year earlier, while the order book reached Rs.15,109 crore (Rs.11,717 crore a year earlier). Management flagged a slowdown in Middle East awards due to the regional conflict, while domestic and Africa activity was steady, and guided FY27 consultancy margins of 20-25% and LSTK margins of 5-7%.

segments.name: Consultancy & engineering
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.1,782 crore (vs Rs.1,678 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.489 crore with a reported Q4 margin near 29%, which management attributed to a Rs.221 crore change order, not a one-off write-back. Guided segment margin 20-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: FY26 turnover Rs.2,067 crore (vs Rs.1,349 crore); Q4 turnover Rs.410 crore. Guided segment margin 5-7%. Dangote refinery (USD 360 million) and fertilizer (USD 70 million, four lines) contracts are being executed, started around January 2026.

segments.name: Subsidiary CEIL
segments.commentary: Profit rose to Rs.24.71 crore in FY26 from Rs.20.62 crore. Associate (refinery-linked) profit was about Rs.40 crore in the latest quarter after a shutdown-affected earlier period; management expects 100% plant capacity this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow to stay around Rs.8,000 crore (consultancy plus LSTK), with an aim to exceed it; management said FY27 inflow is hard to predict beyond one or two quarters.
FY27 revenue growth guided at a minimum of 10-15%, based on two months of the year elapsed.
Consultancy segment margin to be sustained at 20-25%; LSTK segment margin at 5-7%.
Consultancy revenue growth seen conservatively at 15-20% a year over the next two to three years.
Middle East: management expects a delay of a couple of months in big-ticket awards; Africa and the new Saudi Aramco agreements (5+3 years) are the growth routes.
Final dividend of Rs.2.5 per share proposed; with the interim Rs.2.5, total FY26 dividend is Rs.5 per share (100% of face value Rs.5).
capex_capacity: Dangote refinery and fertilizer projects are about four years in duration; site activity expected to start around end-2026 or early 2027.
Andhra (BPCL) project: feasibility underway; licensor selection next, with project activities targeted in FY27.
IOCL Paradip phase-2 balance order (about Rs.8-10 billion) expected to be awarded by end of FY27, after the investment decision.
Panipat (P25) project is in advanced construction and expected to commission soon.
Company is setting up a CBG plant in Maharashtra on its own investment and is the OT consultant for an MRPL sustainable aviation fuel plant.
demand_pricing: Order book is at a record Rs.15,109 crore, but FY26 inflow was slightly lower than FY25 at Rs.7,979 crore.
Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured, and roughly 10-15% of the current order book. Big-ticket Middle East awards are slower, with client decisions delayed by security concerns.
Africa is the main overseas focus after the Dangote awards; management sees investment shifting to Africa as an alternative hub.
Infrastructure is about 25% of FY26 order inflow (clients include ONGC, NTPC, Government of Rajasthan, IIMs/IITs and data centres).
Coal gasification: government raised viability gap funding; a consultancy opportunity of about Rs.300-400 crore was indicated. Project sizes of Rs.10,000-40,000 crore were cited.
Public-sector tenders are competitive or negotiated; hit rate on bids is about 20-25%. Nomination only for critical projects.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for FY27 consultancy inflow in domestic and international markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to sustain inflow at roughly the current level of about Rs.8,000 crore total; Middle East slowdown is the key risk, with domestic projects not being delayed or cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East share of the order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East is about 30% of overseas business secured and 10-15% of the current order book; a Saudi Aramco long-term agreement (5+3 years) was signed, with an out-of-kingdom agreement pending.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or change order behind Q4 consultancy margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no write-offs; a Rs.221 crore change order was received in FY26 and the expenditure already incurred, and the Q4 margins are described as normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue slippage Q4 vs Q3 and cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue slippage; the prior quarter included a change order over Rs.200 crore, which made it high-profit. Management did not report commodity cost impacts.

qa_highlights.question: Expected growth in FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Minimum 10-15% growth expected in FY27 execution; FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance was deferred to next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East and Africa opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000-2,000 crore of projects is achievable over time, with an inflection expected around FY27-FY29.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict delaying big-ticket awards and revamp-led spending; monitor Saudi and out-of-kingdom agreement signing.
Consultancy order inflow, with FY26 slightly below FY25 and the Rs.8,000 crore FY27 target dependent on public-sector tenders.
Sustainability of 20%+ consultancy margins; Q4 margin benefited from a Rs.221 crore change order.
Dangote and IOCL Paradip conversion timing; large LSTK jobs carry 5-7% margins.
Associate plant operating at full capacity this year after a prior shutdown.
Disclosure readability: an analyst flagged that the figures uploaded to the exchanges are hard to read.

532178|2026-06.headline: Engineers India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 55% to INR109 crores, while turnover fell 7% to INR801 crores on Turnkey decline.

Turnkey turnover fell to INR302 crores from INR449 crores as major projects tapered. Order book stood at INR14,424 crores at 30 June 2026, but Q1 order inflow was only INR514 crores. Management kept the INR8,000 crore FY27 order inflow target and the FY27 operating margin guidance of 16%, and said the Middle East new-mega-project pipeline has slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore order inflow target still achievable, and how much would be consultancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is unchanged, with about INR2,750 crores in hand now and about two quarters left. Consultancy is about INR1,100 crores of this, with the rest mainly LSTK domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be write-backs or change orders this year, including HPCL Barmer?
qa_highlights.answer: No exceptional change order is in the current quarter and no provision write-backs are expected; provisions reverse only after the defect liability period ends.

qa_highlights.question: How should consultancy growth and margins be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consultancy growth target is at least 10%+ overall, with consultancy above 50% of turnover; segment profit is targeted at 24-25%. Operating margin target is 16%, with possible upside from change orders.

qa_highlights.question: Have Middle East clients put projects on hold due to the conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no existing project is stopped; new mega projects are on hold or slow, and routine jobs continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue be recognised on the Dangote Nigeria order?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on cost-progress basis, with turnover booked as cost progress is achieved over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan to distribute surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to distribute the full reserves now, as other investment plans are under consideration, and pointed to about 100% dividend this year.

532187|2026-06.headline: IndusInd Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs.1,037 crore from Rs.594 crore QoQ, with GNPA at 3.25% and a 16.10% CET1 ratio.
532187|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as an inflection point, with deposits and advances growing 3.7% and 3.3% QoQ after a year of balance sheet recalibration. Profit after tax reached Rs.1,037 crore, helped by a one-off Rs.284 crore interest recovery on an income tax refund; excluding one-offs, RoA was 0.63%. Asset quality improved, with annualised net slippages at 1.50% and Rs.1,435 crore of write-offs, while microfinance stress moderated. Management reiterated an exit-FY27 RoA target of 1%, with about 60% of the improvement expected from PPOP and 40% from lower credit costs.

segments.commentary: Book at Rs.99,718 crore, +3% YoY and flat QoQ; disbursements Rs.10,832 crore, down 4% YoY, with annualised net slippage at 2.01% vs 2.29% YoY. Management attributes Q1 weakness to seasonality, two-wheeler underwriting tightening and GST change.

segments.name: Micro Loans / Rural
segments.commentary: Micro loan book Rs.16,305 crore, -3% QoQ; gross slippages Rs.191 crore vs Rs.504 crore QoQ; 31-90 DPD at 0.6%. About 74% of the portfolio is covered under CGFMU guarantee. Merchant finance Rs.8,095 crore (+11% YoY), affordable housing Rs.2,889 crore (+21% YoY).

segments.commentary: Book at Rs.31,617 crore, +2% QoQ; consumer disbursements +16% QoQ. Home loans Rs.6,889 crore (+38% YoY, +6% QoQ); gold loans crossed Rs.1,200 crore; personal loans Rs.9,930 crore (-4% QoQ); credit cards Rs.9,418 crore (-3% QoQ). Annualised net slippage 4.19% vs 4.22% QoQ.

segments.commentary: SME is about 13% of mix per analyst. LAP grew 8% QoQ and business loans 4% QoQ, net of migrations to wholesale. Management says foundations are being built and growth is intended to be significantly faster.

segments.name: Wholesale Banking
segments.commentary: Average wholesale loan book +7% QoQ, with management citing about 11% period-end growth and large corporates up 16% per the analyst's question. Corporate and SME fees +28% QoQ; transaction banking is 55% of wholesale and SME fees. A-and-above rated share steady at 82%; annualised gross slippage 0.17%.

guidance_outlook: Exit-FY27 RoA target of 1%; the bridge is about 60% from PPOP and 40% from lower credit costs, to be firmed up quarter by quarter.

Consumer banking: leadership hires and investment in distribution, analytics and technology.

demand_pricing: Wholesale: management cited ample opportunity across mid-corporate, large corporate and strategic corporate, with selection based on RAROC and reciprocity (transaction banking, current account floats, GST and salary accounts).

qa_highlights.question: How different is the current wholesale growth profile from what was run down, and how should the retail/SME/corporate mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 82% of the wholesale portfolio is A-minus and above, and growth is a function of 6 to 9 months of capability building. Other engines (SME, vehicle, MFI) are also expected to grow, with growth optimised to meet ROA aspirations.

qa_highlights.question: How much further can cost of deposits fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is still a lot of work to do on deposit quantity and quality; the gap to the closest peer is about 150 bps, which it aims to narrow over the medium term. Mix shift toward retail and SBC deposits is also contributing, not just repricing.

qa_highlights.question: What portfolio actions are happening in retail and SME, and when will growth pick up?

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 8% QoQ fall in other expenses and what is the RoA bridge to 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Statutory costs (DICGC, PSLC, CSR) and operating expenses fell; some disbursal-linked costs will rise later. The 0.63% to 1% bridge is seen as about 60% PPOP and 40% lower credit costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why not bid out more deposits given the asset yield, and how should the liability mix be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bulk deposits cost about 50 bps more, and institutional deposits carry 25-40% outflow rates versus 5-12% for retail. It will use bulk tactically and keep the core funding base driven by retail and SBC deposits to reduce ROA volatility.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and will capital be needed?

532187|2026-09.headline: IndusInd Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose to Rs.1,242 crore and RoA to 0.87%, helped by FCNR(B) inflows of USD 3.51 billion.
532187|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed a sharp recovery: deposits and advances returned to double-digit YoY growth (10% and 11%), and asset quality improved across sub-segments with gross NPA at 2.73% and net NPA at 0.83%. Profit after tax reached Rs.1,242 crore against a normalised Rs.824 crore in Q1. Margins compressed to 3.23% (from a normalised 3.35%) due to FCNR(B) mobilisation, and management said it expects some deposit-rate uptick in H2. Management reiterated a 1% exit RoA ambition for FY27 and a medium-term 175-180 bps historical RoA benchmark.

segments.commentary: Book Rs.1,00,651 crore, up 5% YoY and 1% QoQ; disbursements Rs.11,968 crore, up 17% YoY and 10% QoQ. Annualised net slippages 1.67%.

segments.commentary: Micro-loan book grew 8% QoQ to Rs.17,571 crore after about eight quarters of decline; annualised net slippage 2.2%. Merchant Finance Rs.8,694 crore, up 20% YoY.

segments.name: Consumer loans (ex-FCNR(B))
segments.commentary: Book Rs.59,776 crore, up 7% QoQ; home loans up 39% YoY to Rs.7,733 crore. Credit card and personal loan books fell 3% and 2% QoQ respectively.

segments.name: Wholesale Banking
segments.commentary: Loan book up 10% QoQ and YoY; Commercial & Mid-Market up 13% QoQ. Fee income Rs.446 crore, up 37% YoY and 9% QoQ; gross slippage annualised 0.07%.

Plans to add 100+ bank branches in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY comparisons are distorted by FY26 de-growth; YTD Q1 book grew 4-5%. It expects to grow in line with market in H2.

qa_highlights.question: ECL transition impact and recurring credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: One-time impact is about 1.1% of loans pretax (not 1.5-1.7%); recurring credit cost 5-6 bps.

qa_highlights.question: FCNR(B) impact on NIM and cost of deposits outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Fee income sustainability and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: One-offs about INR100 crore (INR48-50 crore AFS/HTM sale gains plus FX sales); trading income about INR70 crore; core fees improving across retail and wholesale.

qa_highlights.question: Savings account weakness and CASA strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding NRI outflows to FCNR(B), SA would be roughly flat; new-to-bank accounts up 12% QoQ to about 3.6 lakh; focus on granular SA in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Tier 1 decline of 55 bps QoQ?

532209|2026-03.headline: J&K Bank posts FY26 net profit of INR2,363 crores, a fourth straight record, with Q4 profit near INR800 crores (up 36% QoQ); FY27 NIM guided at ~3.5%.
532209|2026-03.overview: FY26 delivered a record annual net profit of INR2,363 crores and a record quarterly profit of nearly INR800 crores, up 36% QoQ. Business grew 13.6%, with advances up 16.8% and deposits up 11.3%, both above guidance. NIM for FY26 was 3.60%, a marginal miss against guidance, attributed to 125 bps of RBI rate cuts in 2025 and deposit competition. Operating expenses fell about 4%, and GNPA/NNPA stood at 2.50%/0.64%. FY27 guidance is conservative: credit growth 12%, deposits 10%, NIM about 3.5%, RoA maintained, RoE about 16%, GNPA below 2.25%.

financial_highlights.value: INR180 crore impairment on EDB amalgamation into J&K Gramin Bank

segments.commentary: Loan growth 9.5% in FY26 versus 28.8% in Rest of India; J&K & Ladakh share of loan book is 63% versus 37% for Rest of India as on 31 March 2026. Bank holds about 60% market share but only 37% branch share.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Loan growth 28.8% in FY26 under the recalibrated strategy; Personal loans grew above 13%, with housing and education loans growing double digits.

segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 38.5% and Agriculture 27.6% in FY26. Financial market book (mainly AAA-rated NBFCs) rose sharply to about INR20,000 crores, with co-lending still immaterial.

segments.commentary: RAM remains more than two-thirds of the loan book. Car loans grew 17.5% and were the best-performing personal loan segment.

Management expects about INR500 crores per quarter for the next two quarters and about INR2,500 crores for the full year, with some hiring of specialists.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall, and what was the Gramin Bank item?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR180 crore impairment on the investment in J&K Gramin Bank, taken in other income after the NABARD-directed amalgamation of Ellaquai Dehati Bank (EDB). Management said it was a policy decision and occurred in the full year, not in Q4.

532209|2026-06.headline: J&K Bank Q1 FY27 net profit fell to INR424 crore on margin compression to 3.28% and higher standard-asset provisions, despite 25.44% advances growth.

Operating profit was INR703 crore (+5% YoY), but net profit of INR424 crore was below last year, driven by standard-asset provisions raised on strong credit growth and lower technical write-off recoveries. NIM compressed to 3.28% as cost of deposits stayed high (4.74%) while yield on advances was 8.56%. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged for now, to be reassessed after Q2, but indicated credit growth of 18-20% against the 12% guidance.

segments.name: Rest of India (ROI)
segments.commentary: ROI contributes around 26% of business as on 30 June 2026, versus less than 20% a year ago. Corporate lending in ROI at competitive rates drove the quarter's growth.

532209|2026-09.headline: J&K Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose about 29% QoQ to INR546 crore; management raised FY27 credit growth guidance to 14%+ and sees ROA of about 1.20%.
532209|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 net profit was INR546 crore, up about 29% QoQ with double-digit YoY growth, after a weak Q1. Operating profit rose 27% YoY to INR789 crore, helped by operating expenses up only 2% QoQ and cost-to-income falling to 56.57%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.23% and NNPA at 0.51%, and H1 gross slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier. Management revised FY27 guidance after the mid-term review: credit growth 14%+, deposit growth 12%+, CASA 42%+, ROA about 1.20% and GNPA below 2%. Key open items are the ECL transition impact, which management will quantify in December, and NIM, which management declined to quantify.

financial_highlights.change: RoA +20 bps QoQ; RoE +250 bps QoQ
Gross slippage amount roughly halved YoY

segments.name: Retail, Agri and MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: Entire net incremental credit in Q2 came from RAM; RAM contributed over 60% of YTD net incremental credit. Agri advances grew about 17% YoY and 7.62% QoQ; retail advances grew 3.90% QoQ.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Auto loans grew over 25% YoY; Rest of India housing grew double digits YoY. Retail yield about 10%. Management says 60% of FY27 growth target will come from retail.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri yield about 9.5%. Agri advances grew double digits in H1.

segments.name: Corporate / MSME
segments.commentary: MSME yield about 9%; Rest of India corporate yield about 7.2%. Little large corporate lending in J&K. Management targets 40% of FY27 growth from corporate.

segments.name: Government MoU personal loans
segments.commentary: Outstanding about INR13,400 crore on the MoU personal loan book (management cited INR16,000 crore+ across two variants). Declined last year after product revamp and EMI/salary-ratio correction; H1 FY27 disbursals already exceed full FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revised guidance (after mid-term review): credit growth 14%+, deposit growth 12%+, CASA 42%+, ROA about 1.20%, GNPA below 2%.
Management says it is 'conservative'; it aims for around 18% credit growth if retail momentum continues.
Management expects H2 FY27 ROA of about 1.40% or better, driven by recoveries from written-off accounts, a special OTS scheme, treasury, fee income and non-fund-based business.
NIM expected to improve substantially from Q3 as the 25 bps repo cut passes through, high-cost deposits are shed, and the repo rate may rise further. No numerical NIM guidance given.
Employee cost expected flat to slightly lower over the next two quarters, returning to current levels in FY28 after hiring.
Credit cost expected to stay around INR70-85 crore per quarter; ECL transition impact to be quantified by December board/next quarter. Management says the ECL hit will be below the industry average.
Capital raise planned: INR1,000 crore equity (timing dependent on market conditions) and INR500 crore debt (expected this quarter).
About 65% of loans are repo-linked and 31% MCLR-linked; repo changes passed through the same day.
capex_capacity: Capital raise planned: INR1,000 crore equity (timing dependent on market conditions; approval already in place, team says it is ready) and INR500 crore debt (expected this quarter).
Capital position at 30 Sep 2026: CRAR 16.57%, CET1 13.88%; RoA 1.07% and RoE 13.68% for Q2.
Employee cost expected flat to slightly lower over the next two quarters due to retirements; new hiring to be completed by end of Q3 or early Q4 FY27, taking cost back to current levels in FY28.
Two life insurance partners added (SBI Life, HDFC Life) to expand third-party product sales; management expects volume growth to offset IRDAI commission reductions.
Retail is the growth focus; management targets 60% of FY27 credit growth from retail and 40% from corporate, with about 18% credit growth aimed for if retail momentum continues.
demand_pricing: Retail and RAM led growth; management says retail is preferred for its higher yield.

Term deposit growth continues to outpace CASA, in line with industry trend. Deposit growth YTD about 7% against 10% guidance (now 12%+ for year). CASA inflows turned positive in Q2 after a sharp Q1 outflow.
Q1 CASA outflows were largely converted to term deposits within the bank, according to management; average and period-end balances are now close.
High-cost CDs of about 8% were taken in Q1 to fund loan commitments; most has been repaid. Remaining high-cost bulk deposits are under INR3,000 crore.
Non-fund-based business up about 30-40% QoQ. Two more life insurers added (SBI Life, HDFC Life); management expects volume growth to offset IRDAI commission cuts.
Government and salary-account MoUs: more than 20 organisations signed in the last quarter; a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU is expected to be signed the day after the call.

qa_highlights.question: What steps are being taken to improve the CASA mix, which lags term deposit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited salary-account MoUs with 20+ organisations, tighter monitoring of UPI POS and QR merchant routing, and a new 5-year Government of J&K salary MoU. It says CASA is at least held at around 42%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook, and what is the ongoing cost after ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify the ECL impact until the end of next quarter, with the model going to the December board. It sees no reason for credit cost to rise; current provisions are ageing-based and H1 slippages were INR234 crore versus INR550 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ROA guidance lowered to about 1.2%, and is H2 ROA of 1.4% achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is conservative and the guidance is '1.20 plus', not a downgrade. It expects H2 ROA of about 1.40%, and possibly better, supported by written-off account recoveries and an OTS scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 credit growth of 14% realistic versus 24-25% currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 14% is a conservative floor ('14% plus'), with an aim of around 18%. It does not expect 25%, since Q3 and Q4 of last year were strong comparators.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NIM outlook and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numerical NIM target but said it will rise substantially from Q3. Drivers are the 25 bps repo pass-through, the end of high-cost deposits, higher yields, and possible further rate hikes. About 65% of the book is repo-linked and 31% MCLR-linked.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-off treasury gain, and how much was recovered from TWO accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: TWO recoveries were INR25 crore in the quarter. A post-quarter equity stake sale and revaluation gain of about INR100 crore is not in Q2. AFS reserve movement was negative INR62 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ECL transition hit quantified, and how prepared is the bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL hit will be below the industry average and the bank holds about INR300 crore of buffer. The model is nearly ready and will go to the board in December, when the transitional range will be given.

risks_watch: ECL transition impact is not yet quantified; the range is due in December and the model goes to the board then. Analysts flagged high SMA-0/1/2 (about 5% SMA-1+2).

NIM improvement is not quantified; cost of deposits rose to 4.85% and yield on advances is flat at 8.55%.
Insurance commission will fall under new IRDAI rules; management expects volume growth to offset this.
Equity raise (INR1,000 crore) timing is open; debt raise (INR500 crore) is expected this quarter.
Q1 CASA outflow has not been fully reversed; CASA ratio is 41.97% against a 42%+ target.

532210|2026-03.headline: City Union Bank Q4 FY26: advances up 26% YoY to INR66,698 crore and PAT up 25% to INR360 crore, with gross NPA at 1.91%.
532210|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the bank's strongest quarter in recent years, with total business growing about 24% YoY and advances up 26% to INR66,698 crore. Asset quality kept improving: gross NPA fell to 1.91% from 3.09% a year earlier, and total SMA fell to 2.47% from 3.68% in Q3. Q4 PAT rose 25% to INR360 crore, the highest single quarter, and FY26 PAT rose 18% to INR1,326 crore with ROA at 1.56%. The call also marked the handover of MD and CEO from Dr. N. Kamakodi to R. Vijay Anandh effective 1 May 2026.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loans are about 30% of the book and growing faster than overall loans; management says the 30% level is near the upper limit, with 1-2% flexibility. Per-gram lending was capped around INR10,000-10,500 even at peak gold prices.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Core focus segment, with management citing rising capacity utilisation and CC limit usage as demand drivers. FY27 plan keeps MSME at 55-60% of the mix. Only 3-4% of MSME loans are under CGTMSE cover.

segments.name: Secured retail
segments.commentary: Housing and loans against property are growing and are an additional growth driver. FY27 plan uses secured retail to fill the remaining share of the mix after MSME and gold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth planned at 2-3% above industry credit growth, with MSME at 55-60%, gold loans and secured retail as additional enhancers.
FY27 NIM expected to stay in a narrow 5-10 bps band around the FY26 level of 3.74%.
FY27 operating expenses expected to rise 15-18% YoY, with about 75 branches to be opened in FY27 (about 50 in April, 25 by year-end).
ROA to exit FY27 at least 10 bps higher, at about 1.65-1.67%, supported by retail income and lower cost-to-income.
CD ratio to be kept at 85-87%. Third-party business to be 1-2% of the book. Fee income to be 55-60% of other income.

Credit cost expected to fall about 50% from the 15-year average of about 0.60% over the next 15 years; individual years may vary. Management said the ECL circular lets banks adjust the opening balance, so the ECL impact on P&L is expected to be limited.
capex_capacity: Branch network reached 1,000 with the opening of the 1,000th branch at Kumbakonam on 4 May 2026, up from about 950 at FY26 end.
About 75 branches to be opened in FY27, with about 50 in April 2026 (70 opened in the first month per the CEO-designate); branches typically reach breakeven in year one.
Distribution capacity was lifted by the Newgen LOS and digital process set, which the management credits for secured MSME and retail growth.
demand_pricing: Advances grew by over INR5,800 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR13,600 crore for the full year; double-digit growth has run for eight consecutive quarters.
Deposit growth was matched to credit growth, with CASA at 28% of deposits and the average CD ratio at 85% for FY26. Some CDs were replaced by retail term deposits.
Yield on advances was 9.80% in Q4 (9.73% in Q3) and 9.75% for FY26 (9.79% in FY25). The cost of deposits was 5.60% in Q4 (5.57% in Q3).
Management said rate passthrough was completed around December 2025, and incremental yields are holding up, with non-agri gold loans at double-digit yields.
Management is watching the US-Iran conflict and oil prices; no visible impact on asset quality so far. Management expects a 1-2% extra slippage rate in a downturn, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: How does the bank manage risk on gold loans given a 10-15% gold price fall from the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-gram lending was capped at about INR10,000-10,500 even when gold peaked at INR15,000-16,000, so there is a cushion. It cited a loss of about INR5 crore in the 2014 gold price crash.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise 3 bps QoQ, and where will it go?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some deposit rates were fine-tuned by 10-25 bps to support fast credit growth. It said the 3-5 bps movement is noise from CASA rate variation and it can add INR3,000 crore of advances without new deposits.

qa_highlights.question: Will yield on advances keep falling after the rate cuts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate passthrough is complete, and roughly 30% of the book is fixed-rate gold. Incremental book of about INR5,000 crore booked in H2 was at higher yields, which held the margin.

qa_highlights.question: When does ROA move to 1.7-1.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO-designate said FY27 exit ROA should be 1.65-1.67%, at least 10 bps above the FY26 level, based on retail income and lower cost-to-income.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for steady-state credit costs after the ECL norms?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the 15-year average credit cost is about 0.60%, and FY25 and FY26 were 0.09% and 0.04%. He expects at least a 50% reduction over the long run, with AI-based underwriting cited as the reason.

qa_highlights.question: Will underwriting filters tighten given fuel prices and demand risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it watches SMA trends and branch and customer feedback. It would add some caution to filters but has no plan to change them now, as underwriting is set for multiple business cycles.

risks_watch: Gold price correction on the INR30%+ gold book and whether LTV cushions hold.
Impact of the US-Iran conflict and oil prices on MSME demand and slippages; management expects an extra 1-2% slippage in a downturn.
Rising deposit costs as the bank fine-tunes rates to fund faster credit growth; the CD ratio is at 85% and CASA at 28%.
Opex growth of 15-18% in FY27 from branch expansion, against the ROA target of 1.65-1.67%.
Leadership transition: MD and CEO handover on 1 May 2026, plus the retirement of two independent directors in February 2026. The retiring MD's future non-executive board role depends on RBI approval.

532210|2026-06.headline: City Union Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 25% YoY to Rs 383 crore, a record, with GNPA down to 1.73% and NIM guided to 3.65-3.70%.
532210|2026-06.overview: Advances grew 25% YoY to Rs 67,645 crore and deposits 21% to Rs 79,342 crore, with CD ratio at 85%. Operating profit rose 29% to Rs 581 crore and PAT 25% to Rs 383 crore, both stated as record highs. Asset quality improved further: GNPA 1.73% (from 2.99% a year ago), Net NPA 0.61%, and recoveries exceeded slippages. Management guided to a moderate NIM dip from higher cost of funds, cost-to-income of 47-48% for FY27, and an exit ROA of 1.60-1.65%.

financial_highlights.change: up 25% QoQ as stated; vs Rs 54,020 crore in 1QFY26

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME average disbursement about Rs 3,500 crore per quarter; management targets MSME at 55-60% of book and growth 2-3% above system. Average utilisation fell from 73% to 70%; repayments about Rs 900 crore per month.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Share of book at 30-31%, guided to stay 31-32%. Agri gold yield about 10-10.5% and non-agri 11-11.5%; agri priced 100 bps lower. Average LTV 62.07%. Branches rose from 700 to 1,000.

segments.name: Retail secured (LAP)
segments.commentary: LAP yield about 9.60-9.70%. Management expects retail secured at about 10% of book.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Yield on investments fell to 6.42% from 6.61% in 4QFY26 because Rs 12 crore of mutual fund income (on about Rs 700 crore invested) was classified under other income; 6.67% on an interest-income basis.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 2-3% above industry credit growth for FY27; DSA business about 1-2% of book.
NIM expected at 3.65-3.70% over the next few quarters as cost of deposits rises about 5 bps; long-term view 3.70-3.75%.
Cost of deposits guided at 5.60-5.70%; borrowing cost of about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.
Cost-to-income guided at 47-48% for FY27 (currently 45%) because staff hikes start from July; long-term aspiration below 45% in about three years.
Exit ROA guided at 1.60-1.65%; full-year ROA 1.55-1.65%. Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%.
ECLGS participation: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date; total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provisioning about 0.45% of loan book, CAR consumption capped at 0.65%.
capex_capacity: Branch rollout front-loaded this year; branch count rose from 700 to 1,000 in the gold-loan context.
AI-led automation invested in operations; management expects it to lower cost further.
Liquidity: average LCR at 150%.

Business enterprise (non-MSME, no Udyam registration) loans at Rs 18,827 million; large-industry book fell from Rs 22,500 million (Dec-25) to about Rs 15,000 million then rose to Rs 19,000 million on exits and yield pressure.
demand_pricing: Gold loan rates unchanged; management ruled out raising rates to slow growth, citing agri customer needs and competitiveness in non-agri gold; rates up 20-25 bps over last year.
MSME utilisation fell to 70% from 73-74% norm; management attributes it to cautious borrowers and sees it recovering with textile demand after the European trade agreement.
Term deposit rates expected to rise on high demand; FCNR window brought in fresh deposits of Rs 150 crore.
SMA-0/1/2 at 1.20%/0.70%/0.90% (total 2.85%), down from 7.12% in June 2025 and 10.78% in September 2024. Domestic consumption said to be insulated from West Asia stress.
Fee income fell about 15% YoY and 19% in one comparison per analyst question; management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins move beyond the near-term cost-of-funds increase (FY27-FY28 levers), given stagnant lending yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to MSME, gold and retail secured yields (agri gold ~10-10.5%, non-agri 11-11.5%, LAP 9.60-9.70%, MSME 9.30-9.40%) and a low-cost deposit franchise; long-term NIM view 3.70-3.75%. The Q1 cost-of-funds decline was attributed to better repricing and lower borrowing cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MSME growing about 15% when system MSME growth is above 20%? Is utilisation falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Rs 900 crore monthly repayments, MSME utilisation down to 70% from a 73-74% norm, and slightly more cautious pricing. Guidance is MSME growth 2-3% above system, with MSME at 55-60% of book.

qa_highlights.question: What slippage and credit cost levels are sustainable over one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state credit cost about 0.40%; FY27 slippages Rs 700-750 crore; slippage ratio 1.20-1.30%. Recoveries have exceeded slippages for about 10 quarters and are expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank reach 25-30% higher growth with the mix intact (gold 31-32%, MSME 55-60%, retail 10%), and what is the MSME outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the mix targets and said lower utilisation cost about 3-4% of MSME growth. It expects MSME growth 2-3% above system, with the European trade agreement seen supporting textile utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in cost of funds despite lower deposit costs, and what is the treasury and borrowing cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost rose to Rs 94 crore from Rs 72.5 crore in 4QFY26; treasury gains were Rs 52.54 crore vs Rs 29 crore in 4QFY26. Borrowing cost is guided at about Rs 94 crore per quarter for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the bank participating in ECLGS, and how is the ECL provisioning assessed?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 800 crore disbursed to date (Rs 200 crore last quarter); total expected Rs 2,000-2,500 crore. ECL provision about 0.45% of loan book, with CAR consumption capped at 0.65%; flow impact described as negligible given the secured book.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income decline and how will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income was down about 15% YoY (analyst cited 19% in one comparison). Management expects catch-up in Q2-Q4 from processing fees, suit recoveries and insurance income; non-treasury other income was Rs 243 crore in Q1 vs roughly Rs 300 crore in Q4 last year.

risks_watch: Utilisation trend in MSME (70% in Q1 vs 73-74% norm) and whether the European trade-agreement recovery in textiles materialises.
Cost of deposits moving to 5.60-5.70% and the ~5 bps NIM hit; NIM guided 3.65-3.70%, below the 3.78% reported in Q1.
Cost-to-income rising to 47-48% for FY27 from 45.42% as staff hikes start from July; exit ROA 1.60-1.65% depends on fee income recovery.
Gold loan pricing: management ruled out rate hikes, so growth is supported only by volume; agri gold LTV around 62% with sensitivity to gold price drops.
West Asia stress and SMA trends (SMA-0/1/2 total 2.85%) and ECLGS-linked disbursements that may affect future asset quality.
Large-industry book volatility (Rs 22,500 million in Dec-25, down to ~Rs 15,000 million, then ~Rs 19,000 million) and the non-MSME business enterprise book of Rs 18,827 million.
key_quotes: For 1QFY27 as well, we have achieved 25% credit growth quarter-on-quarter, the highest growth rate in June-to-June and our advances had increased to Rs. 67,645 crores from Rs. 54,020 crores in 1QFY26.
So, the trend of recovery more than slippages continues, and we are confident of maintaining recovery more than slippages for the next quarter as well, which is the current quarter.
So, we are quite confident of maintaining the cost-to-income at 47%. We are currently at 45 as we speak.
We haven't changed any rate of interest for gold loans. We are at the same rate, and we continue to do the same.

532210|2026-09.headline: City Union Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 416 crores, with advances up 26% to INR 72,442 crores and Gross NPA down to 1.44%.
532210|2026-09.overview: Management reported a strong Q2 FY27: advances grew over INR 4,800 crores QoQ (over 7%) to INR 72,442 crores, deposits rose 21% YoY to INR 83,893 crores, and NIM expanded 9 bps QoQ to 3.87%. Asset quality improved sharply, helped by sale of INR 803 crores of technically written-off and live accounts to an ARC, with Gross NPA falling to 1.44% from 1.73%. Management guided NIM to 3.85-3.95% for Q3 and Q4, and addressed scrutiny on gold loan practices, LTV norms and ECL transition impact (about INR 300 crores, of which about INR 30 crores already provided).

financial_highlights.change: Up from 3.78% in Q1 FY27; H1 FY26 was 3.59%
Down from 1.73% in Q1 FY27 (29 bps); Net NPA 0.48% vs 0.9% a year ago
+35% YoY from INR 259 crores; includes ARC-related income
Created as buffer for economic uncertainty

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances rose INR 2,600 crores QoQ to INR 42,862 crores from INR 40,262 crores; management calls it the core strength. Utilisation of SME lines is about 71-72%, up from 69% last quarter.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book rose INR 1,062 crores QoQ to INR 21,777 crores from INR 20,715 crores; about 30% of advances. Agri is about 50% of customers; 96% of the book is in South India; blended yield about 10.8%. Gold SMA-2 at about INR 173 crores (0.24% of gold advances).

segments.name: Secured retail loans
segments.commentary: Secured retail advances rose INR 1,134 crores QoQ to INR 7,802 crores from INR 6,668 crores.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income was INR 36 crores in Q2 vs INR 52 crores in Q1; about INR 12 crores of mutual fund income was reclassified to interest income after the bank exited its MF holdings.

guidance_outlook: NIM guided to 3.85% to 3.95% for Q3 and Q4 FY27, supported by repricing of about 55% EBLR-linked loans after recent policy rate changes.
Deposit cost expected to rise about 10 bps in the next quarter; deposit rates had not yet moved as liquidity remained ample.
ROA expected to move above 1.6% (management also cited a 1.6-1.65% range on closing).
Cost-to-income expected at 45-47% for FY27; quarterly staff cost run rate of about INR 275-280 crores going forward.
Credit growth targeted at 2-3 percentage points above industry; deposit growth to stay aligned with credit growth.
Tax rate expected at 21-23% going forward, a blended 22-23% for the year; ECL transition impact about INR 300 crores, with management saying no P&L impact as it is adjusted against capital.
capex_capacity: Branch network grew from about 800 to over 1,000 branches; newly opened branches are reported to be contributing consistently.
Gold loans are offered from 250-260 branches, mainly rural and semi-urban; a typical branch book is INR 40-50 crores.
Deposit verticalisation launched across salary, TASC, government, CASA and NRI segments.
demand_pricing: Deposits grew 21% YoY; CASA ratio stable at 27%; average CD ratio 86%. Term deposits below INR 3 crores are 48% of the book, INR 3-50 crores 17%, and above INR 50 crores 8%.
Bank took FCNR deposits of USD 69 million under the RBI swap window (USD 15 million from new-to-bank customers), swapped into rupees and deployed domestically.
Gold loan yields are rising on fixed-rate book repricing; management sees 5-10 bps more headroom from loan renewals. Agri vs non-agri yield differential about 100 bps.
Average ticket size per account: gold agri INR 1.90 lakhs, gold non-agri INR 3 lakhs; retail INR 70-80 lakhs excluding Mumbai and Delhi.
Management said 20% deposit growth would be hard to sustain over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan scrutiny: how was INR 9.5 crores of gold NPA resolved, and what is the loan structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Only INR 20 lakhs of the INR 9.5 crores NPA went to auction; the rest was repaid by borrowers. 99% of consumption loans are bullet, with no change in behaviour seen. The bank does not do top-ups, and says it does not finance NPAs.

qa_highlights.question: Why were the technically written-off accounts sold to the ARC at 16% cash recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 803 crores sold (INR 131 crores consideration; INR 792 crores provided). About INR 740 crores were over three years old, including 757 loans of INR 645 crores over five years. INR 303 crores was secured and INR 500 crores unsecured. TW pool outstanding is INR 900 crores, fully provided; no reversal taken.

qa_highlights.question: Is the staff cost increase one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly the July wage revision, plus INR 32 crores of leave encashment provision in Q2 against a normal INR 3-5 crores. Run rate is INR 275-280 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 were 23-24% because of write-offs; the going-forward range is 21-23%, around 22-23% blended.

qa_highlights.question: Quantum of ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental ECL requirement at 30 Sep 2026 is INR 299.42 crores, down from INR 445 crores at 31 Mar 2025. About INR 30 crores already provided and INR 20 crores adjusted against capital; the remaining is to be absorbed in capital.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit growth of 20% be sustainable in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was doubtful about 20% growth over the next two years. Granularity is improving and new branches are contributing, but it said it needs more time to confirm.

risks_watch: Gold loan quality: sharp gold price correction could strain LTV cushions; SMA-0/1/2 totalled 2.53% of gross advances.
Asset quality reliance on recoveries and ARC sales; the TW pool and recoveries will need watching.
Deposit cost rise of about 10 bps next quarter could compress the NIM guidance if lending repricing lags.
Deposit growth sustainability against competition, with management doubtful about 20% growth.
Treasury/AFS mark-to-market: bond MTM loss sits in AFS reserve; CFO to share figures later.
Contingent provisioning and ECL transition impact (about INR 270 crores net unprovided) to be absorbed through capital.

rows.why: Deposits up 21% YoY to INR 83,893 crores with CASA stable at 27% and verticalisation launched across salary, TASC, government, CASA and NRI segments; management cautious on sustaining 20% growth.

rows.why: Gold book rose INR 1,062 crores QoQ to INR 21,777 crores (about 30% of advances), with 96% in South India and blended yield about 10.8%, with 5-10 bps further yield headroom from renewals.

532215|2026-06.headline: Axis Bank Q1FY27 PAT rose 23% YoY to ₹7,114 cr, but NIM fell to 3.46%, which management calls the cycle bottom.
532215|2026-06.overview: Axis Bank reported Q1FY27 PAT of ₹7,114 cr, up 23% YoY and 1% QoQ, with core operating profit up 10% YoY to ₹11,122 cr. Net credit cost fell 75 bps YoY to 0.63% and GNPA improved to 1.28%. NIM compressed 34 bps YoY to 3.46%, which management said is the cycle bottom, with a 19 bps repo-cut drag and 16 bps from balance sheet mix. Advances grew 19% YoY, led by wholesale (38%), while retail grew 8%. Management also flagged the upcoming FCNR(B) inflows and an AT-1 raise, and the CFO announced his departure.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -29 bps YoY; NNPA -6 bps YoY

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Advances grew 8% YoY; retail disbursements grew 18% YoY (home loans +24%, vehicle +21%, personal +23%, retail agri +16%). Retail is 54% of advances; retail gross slippages were ₹5,176 cr.

segments.name: Wholesale / CBG / SME
segments.commentary: Wholesale advances grew 38% YoY, SME 25%, and CBG is 12% of advances. Corporate loans are 34% of advances, with 91% rated A- and above. Wholesale fees grew 18% YoY.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Domestic subsidiaries' PAT was ₹546 cr, up 21% YoY. Axis Finance PAT was ₹244 cr, up 29%, with AUM above ₹50,000 cr. Axis AMC PAT was ₹134 cr, up 3%. Axis Capital PAT was ₹65 cr, up 72%. Axis Securities PAT was ₹96 cr, up 8%.

segments.name: Wealth (Burgundy)
segments.commentary: Burgundy AUM grew 20% YoY and 11% QoQ; Burgundy Private AUM grew 16% YoY and 12% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Structural NIM guidance of 3.8% is unchanged, with the time frame from earlier intact. Management expects the path to 3.8% to start from the Q1FY27 cycle bottom of 3.46%. It gave no near-term or full-year NIM outlook.
Medium-term growth target remains industry plus 300 bps. Management declined to give a run-rate outlook.
Cost-to-assets: no terminal guidance. Productivity and AI investment are expected to continue over the next 18-24 months.
FCNR(B) raise is expected to add surplus liquidity, to be deployed into growth. The quantum raised will be disclosed with Q2 results.
AT-1 raised: US$500 mn in the quarter plus US$100 mn post quarter-end. Management expects to call the existing AT-1 on its contracted call date, subject to regulatory approval.
ECL transition: net-worth impact is expected to be marginal, but industry provisioning is likely to be higher in the first year of transition.
Max Financial Services: the bank is evaluating a stake increase toward 30% under RBI's December clarification, pending internal approvals and regulator consent.
capex_capacity: Branches: 20 opened in the quarter.
Technology and digital expenses were about 11% of total operating expenses.
AI: AXIOM enterprise AI operating model; Adi handled about 7.4 lakh queries and Kaleidoscope enabled about 30.9 lakh servicing interactions in the quarter.
Headcount fell by 609 QoQ. Staff costs were down 6% YoY.
demand_pricing: Loan pricing compressed by 9 bps QoQ, which management attributed to repricing of contracted loans and lower pricing on incremental corporate lending amid competitive intensity. The balance sheet mix change cost a further 4 bps.
Deposits grew 18% YoY on a QAB basis (term +21%, CA +13%, SA +14%, CASA +13%). QoQ, deposits grew 6%, CASA 5% and term deposits 7%.
Market share gains: about 10 bps on loans and about 20 bps on deposits, both YoY.
Foreign currency loans grew sharply; management called this opportunistic and said there is no directional change in the portfolio mix.
ECLGS: sanctions of about ₹5,000 cr, with ₹2,400 cr disbursed to date, mainly to MSMEs in manufacturing and trading.
About 74% of loans are floating rate, and about 45% of the fixed-rate book matures within 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 9 bps QoQ loan pricing hit, and are the corporate loans temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to spillover of last quarter's mix shift plus about one percentage point of mix shift this quarter, with competitive pricing. Loans span project finance, term loans and working capital, and are expected to stay on book until maturity. Management said there is no bunching of temporary loans.

qa_highlights.question: Where does NIM go from here, and what is the normalised opex run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The 3.8% structural NIM target is unchanged, and Q1 is seen as the bottom. Management gave no terminal cost-to-assets guidance, citing branch productivity and AI over the next 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 34 bps NIM decline can be reversed, and what is the walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the 34 bps YoY fall, 19 bps came from the repo cut and 16 bps from mix change. Management declined to give an itemised bridge, saying retail disbursement growth would drive gradual recalibration.

qa_highlights.question: What were the one-offs in opex?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹271 cr of QoQ opex decline was one-time staff items: a reversal of the ₹129 cr Q4 provident fund charge after G-Sec yields eased, a gratuity item, and a variable pay true-up.

qa_highlights.question: Why were upgrades and recoveries weak, and how should technical slippages be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stopped disclosing technical versus non-technical splits. It said Q3 and Q1 credit costs are similar, that recoveries from the technical pool improved, and that technical slippages will not cause economic loss.

qa_highlights.question: Would the bank raise its Max Financial stake toward 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating the option under RBI's December clarification, will weigh pros and cons internally, and will then check with the regulator.

qa_highlights.question: Does the FCNR(B) raise dilute NIM, and how much has been raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no near-term NIM outlook and said it would not disclose FCNR(B) amounts raised until Q2 results. It expects to exceed its organic market share in FCNR(B).

qa_highlights.question: Why chase wholesale lending at lower NIM when retail disbursements are rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wholesale returns are judged on composite RAROC including fees, FX and balances, which it says matches retail RAROC. Surplus deposits are being deployed into wholesale while retail ramps up gradually.

risks_watch: NIM recovery to 3.8% depends on retail mix recalibration and deployment of FCNR(B) liquidity. Management gave no timeline.
Corporate loans are growing at tight spreads and are funded partly by wholesale deposits. Management says loans are not temporary, but CASA is softer.
ECL transition is expected to raise provisions to assets in the first year, and the ₹2,001 cr one-time standard provision is held as a buffer.
The CFO, Puneet Sharma, is leaving the bank after six-plus years. A successor announcement is pending.
Reporting remains on Saturdays, which analysts flagged; management said it will continue this format.
El Nino and geopolitical or energy-price shocks were flagged as macro risks.

532215|2026-09.headline: Axis Bank Q2FY27 PAT rose 38% YoY to ₹7,003 crore, but NIM fell to 3.36% (3.47% ex-FCNR(B) impact).
532215|2026-09.overview: Axis Bank reported Q2FY27 PAT of ₹7,003 crore (up 38% YoY) with NII up 12% YoY and 5% QoQ to ₹15,371 crore. Reported NIM was 3.36%, down 37 bps YoY and 10 bps QoQ, with management attributing 11 bps of the QoQ decline to FCNR(B) grossing-up and liquidity carry. Asset quality improved: GNPA 1.16% (down 30 bps YoY), net credit cost 0.45% (down 28 bps YoY). Advances grew 23% YoY and 9% QoQ (19% YoY ex-international-branch FCNR(B) loans), while the corporate mix rose and retail share slipped toward 54%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail book up 16% YoY and 10% QoQ (10% YoY ex-FCNR(B) leverage facility); retail disbursements up 22% YoY in Q2, with home loans +24%, vehicle +25%, SBB +33%. Retail is 54% of advances.

segments.name: Wholesale / Corporate
segments.commentary: Wholesale banking book grew 34% YoY; corporate loans are 34% of advances. Management says growth is selective, filtered on RAROC, transfer pricing and RWA.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: SME book grew 25% YoY and 9% QoQ; SME is 12% of advances.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Domestic subsidiaries earned ₹1,210 crore PAT in H1FY27 (up 29% YoY). Axis Finance AUM ₹54,590 crore (up 23% YoY), H1 PAT ₹546 crore (up 42%). Axis AMC H1 PAT ₹370 crore (up 36%, adjusted). Axis Capital PAT ₹149 crore (up 61%).

guidance_outlook: No numerical NIM guidance for next quarter; management expects sequential NIM improvement from FCNR(B) fund deployment and optimisation over the next couple of quarters, with Q2 described as the bottom.
Through-cycle NIM target of 3.8% unchanged structurally, but no timeline given.
Management says the 8.6% QoQ fall in non-retail term deposits reflects utilisation of FCNR(B) funds to retire costlier NRTDs at quarter-end.
Repo-linked book repricing happens in the last week of the quarter, so recent repo hikes benefit the book from Q4 rather than Q3; new repo-linked loans reprice immediately.
Credit cost: no specific guidance, but management expects further directional improvement.
Cost-to-assets expected to keep declining; the labour code and one-off items are excluded from the trend.
Medium-term guidance of advances growth 300 bps above industry average retained; no NII uplift guidance given.
Management reiterates no need for equity capital for growth or protection. Standard asset and other buffers total ₹8,006 crore, worth ~49 bps of incremental capital cushion.
Insurance (bancassurance) impact from the draft IRDA consultation: management expects about 6-9 months before changes come through; mitigation levers not quantified.
UPI MDR implementation postponed; no quantified revenue guidance given.
capex_capacity: Net 119 new branches opened in Q2FY27 and 139 in H1FY27; period-end headcount down 375 versus 31 March 2026.
Technology and digital expenses were about 10% of total operating expenses in Q2FY27.
LCR at 119%; management stated an operating band of 115% to 120%.
AT-1 of US$600 mn raised in H1FY27 used to call the earlier AT-1 in September 2026; a further US$600 mn of senior notes raised in Q2.
demand_pricing: Corporate growth is broad-based across capex, project finance, refinancing and working capital; management says it is not chasing assets and is letting go of deals that fail filters.
Retail share of the loan mix is still falling; management has not guided to a bottom but aims to return above 55% retail.
Fee growth is weak on a YoY basis: asset-linked fees are lower as the corporate mix rises, and credit card spends were soft, with the festive period shifting to October.
FCNR(B) fees were not charged; the deposit drive carried no fee income.
Personal loans are salaried-only; the business loan segment covers self-employed borrowers.
Market share gained ~10 bps on loans and ~10 bps on deposits YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Will the retail share of the loan mix keep falling while corporate opportunities stay strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Subrat Mohanty said no retail topping-out level was guided; retail disbursements are strong and retail book growth moved from 6% to 8% to 10% over recent quarters, with the aim of returning above 55% retail mix.

qa_highlights.question: What NIM movement should be expected next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Mantri said the 11 bps FCNR drag was a one-quarter effect, with 3.47% ex-FCNR up 1 bp QoQ; optimisation should lift NIM in Q3 and Q4, but no timeline is guaranteed, and the through-cycle target of 3.8% is intact.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour code one-off recurring and how much of the ₹254 crore was FCNR-related?
qa_highlights.answer: Slightly more than half of the ₹254 crore was labour-code related (outsourced staff, ESIC clarifications), with the rest tied to FCNR(B) mobilisation; more labour-code costs could arise if new guidance is issued.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fee growth weak and what is the bancassurance impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Subrat Mohanty cited lower asset-linked fees from corporate growth, late non-asset fees and soft card spends; on bancassurance, management said the impact is early-stage, with 6-9 months before changes and possible glide paths.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FCNR NIM hit the bottom, and will NIM rise from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Mantri said Q2 is the bottom and that sequential improvement should follow, but the timing cannot be pinned down; repricing of the repo book benefits Q4 more than Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank's LCR flat because excess liquidity has been fully deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Neeraj Gambhir said LCR is actively managed within 115-120%; if it rises above that, the bank will shed other liabilities, and FCNR(B) funds have not been fully used to grow assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost trajectory and the ECL transition impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Mantri said there is no specific credit cost guidance but the trend is improving; ECL transition is not expected to be material, supported by around ₹8,000 crore of existing contingent provisions.

risks_watch: NIM recovery depends on FCNR(B) deployment and repo repricing timing (benefit mostly in Q4); the reported NIM may stay pressured in Q3.
Corporate-heavy growth could keep the retail share below 55%, which affects the medium-term NIM and the 3.8% through-cycle target.
Fee income growth is weak YoY; insurance commission changes from the draft IRDA rules could hit fees within 6-9 months; UPI MDR is postponed with no revenue estimate.
Labour code and other one-time opex items recur, keeping the cost-to-assets trend noisy.
LCR management in the 115-120% band with a higher liability outflow rate on non-retail term deposits.
ECL transition in FY28: no material impact expected, but the floor rates for stages 1 and 2 are still to be worked through.
Macro headwinds from West Asia tensions, energy and food inflation, and trade disruptions.

532218|2026-03.headline: South Indian Bank FY26 net profit rose 12% to INR1,455 crore; Q4 PAT INR408 crore, GNPA down to 1.43% for the year.
532218|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the bank's highest-ever annual profit, with deposits up 15% and gross advances up 14.5% (about 15.8% excluding the INR1,163 crore technical write-off). Asset quality improved sharply, with gross NPA at 1.43% and net NPA at 0.29%, and Q4 credit cost was 3 bps. Q4 non-interest income fell mainly because Treasury income was near nil versus about INR77 crore in Q3, and employee costs were lowered by an INR80 crore actuarial write-back. Management said credit cost and slippages are likely to rise from here, and it flagged a CEO succession process, with the current term ending September 30, 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR342 crore in Q4 FY25
Q4 NIM up 9 bps QoQ; Q3 up 6 bps
GNPA down 177 bps from 3.2%; NNPA down 63 bps from 0.92%

financial_highlights.value: 15 bps in Q4 (not annualised); 72 bps for FY26

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book grew 46% in FY26 to INR24,729 crore, average LTV 57.18%, average ticket about INR2.71 lakh. Management said the vast majority is organic; buyouts and co-lending are about 8-10% of the book.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate is about 38% of the loan book; management targets about 33% over time, with ultra-short-duration corporate lending falling from roughly 20-25% of book to about 10%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 15% YoY. Sequential decline of about 2% was attributed to a INR554 crore write-off, per management, with no material stress seen.

segments.name: Retail and mortgage/auto
segments.commentary: Management reported significant YoY growth in mortgage and auto loans. Personal loans are largely pre-approved sales to existing customers, with loss rates of about 3.5-4% against spreads of 11-12%.

segments.name: Treasury and fee income
segments.commentary: Treasury income was nil in Q4 versus about INR77 crore in Q3, which drove the non-interest income dip. FX revenue grew substantially; a new TF Online export platform is planned.

guidance_outlook: Loan growth guided at 15-16% for FY27, and the bank aims to match industry growth if industry grows faster.
NIM expected to keep widening through asset mix shift to retail and MSME, repricing of about 60-65% of deposits during FY27, and possible rate hikes, where the bank would be a large beneficiary.
Operating expenses will rise as the bank invests in distribution and technology, but management aims for positive operating leverage for a third straight year.
Management expects credit cost and slippages to trend upward from current lows due to Middle East geopolitical stress; it sees Q3 credit cost of 3 bps as the trough.
Branch network to grow selectively in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat and New Delhi; branches fell from 955 to 948 over the past seven to eight quarters.
Corporate share targeted to fall from 38% to about 33% of the loan book over two to three years.
capex_capacity: Branch count at 948, down from 955 over seven to eight quarters; selective additions planned in several states.
SIB RED, a full digital bank offering, launched towards end-March 2026.
New TF Online platform under development for export and trade finance for corporate and MSME clients.
Management said investment in distribution, manpower and technology will start, after costs were held flat for eight to ten quarters.
demand_pricing: Deposit cost rose about 3 bps QoQ in Q4 as the bank selectively repriced deposits to fund growth; management said it had been priced below competitors.
NRI deposits grew 12% in FY26 versus 7% in FY25; management said there is no stress from West Asia conflict, with a slight pickup in inward remittances.
Management said the new ECLGS-type scheme targets airlines and MSMEs, and it did not expect a material drawdown given the current borrower stress levels.
Gold price fell from about $5,500 to about $4,100 per ounce in January-February; margin calls were met promptly and gold loan risk is managed with a 30-day VaR framework and standard-deviation caps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vinod Francis said Treasury income was almost nil in Q4 versus about INR77 crore in Q3 because of market conditions. Management said the drop was industry-wide and that the shift to retail and MSME should raise fee income over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off in employee expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was an actuarial valuation write-back of close to INR80 crore at year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost and ECL transition look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 credit cost of 3 bps is the trough and expects slippages and credit cost to rise given geopolitical stress; it cannot quantify this. For ECL transition, no floating provision is held and no material one-time impact is expected, given SMA 1 and 2 at about 0.6% of the book and PCR near 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the cost of deposits rise, and will NIM keep improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank repriced deposits slightly to support growth, adding about 3 bps. It said NIM rose about 15 bps over two quarters and expects further widening from mix, repricing of 60-65% of deposits, and rate hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CEO succession on track?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO P.R. Seshadri said the Board is actively searching and will send names to RBI in time. His term ends September 30, and management expects the new incumbent to be in place before or just after that date.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank add branches or expand distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will add branches selectively in the under-penetrated states, and rely more on DSAs, digital channels and the SIB RED digital bank.

risks_watch: Rising slippages and credit cost, which management expects from Middle East stress; the outcome is unquantified.
Gold price volatility on a book of INR24,729 crore; a fall beyond the VaR-based caps would hit the bank, and the portfolio's LTV is blended.
Fee income volatility from Treasury; Q4 Treasury income was near nil.
Deposit cost pressure from selective repricing, versus expected repricing benefit in FY27.
CEO succession: the search is ongoing and the term ends September 30, 2026.
Old and new book classification was debated internally; the old book was about 12% of gross advances, and the Q4 GNPA reduction was largely driven by INR1,048 crore of technical write-off.
Possible difficulty recovering the 25% ECLGS guarantee portion if settlements are made with borrowers.
